title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
式錄成將馳驛以
獻威當序諸首敢進一言為士
之登名者告焉福建濱海地
也秦漢以前無所考見入宋
而文物繁興遂齒于上國迨
我
皇明人文化成遠在海外重譯而
===
獻者皆識文字况處海內為
巨藩而被化之乆者乎宜士
之詵詵焉出倍蓰於往昔也
昔人有謂海濱鄒魯今鄒魯
制額出福建下亦其驗矣諸士
子行將與天下士爭先挾其
所有以獻于
punctuated:
式。錄成，將馳驛以獻，威當序諸首，敢進一言，為士之登名者告焉。
福建濱海地也，秦漢以前無所考見。入宋而文物繁興，遂齒于上國。迨我皇明，人文化成，遠在海外重譯而獻者，皆識文字，况處海內為巨藩而被化之乆者乎？宜士之詵詵焉出，倍蓰於往昔也。昔人有謂「海濱鄒魯」，今鄒魯制額出福建下，亦其驗矣。諸士子行將與天下士爭先，挾其所有以獻于
translation_en:
…the prescribed form. The record is complete and will be sent by the imperial relay service for presentation to the throne. I, Wei, am charged with placing a preface at its beginning, and venture to offer a word to those scholars whose names appear in it.
Fujian is a coastal land. For the Qin and Han periods and earlier, nothing can be established from the evidence. With the advent of the Song, its literary culture flourished, and it came to rank alongside the central regions. Under our august Ming dynasty, transformation through literary culture has reached such a degree that even those far overseas who present tribute through successive interpreters understand writing. How much more must this be true of a great province within the realm that has long received this transforming influence! It is fitting that scholars should emerge in abundance, several times more numerous than in the past. People of former times called it “Zou and Lu by the sea.” Today, the prescribed examination quota for Zou and Lu falls below Fujian’s: this too bears out that description. You scholars will soon vie for precedence with scholars from throughout the realm, bringing all your attainments to present at…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
王庭躋華陟要有日矣自視昔
之涵濡於文教所以佩服誦
說者何如於今獨不知所以
仰
德意而圖報稱哉萬一舍其平素
而别爲趨向則錄不足榮矣
威於是與有責焉盍相與戒
===
勉之
湖廣鄖陽府鄖西縣儒學教
諭徐威謹序
punctuated:
王庭，躋華陟要有日矣。自視昔之涵濡於文教，所以佩服誦說者何如？於今獨不知所以仰德意而圖報稱哉？萬一舍其平素而别爲趨向，則錄不足榮矣。威於是與有責焉，盍相與戒勉之？
湖廣鄖陽府鄖西縣儒學教諭徐威謹序。
translation_en:
…to the imperial court; the day when they rise to illustrious rank and important office is within reach. Let them reflect upon their former immersion in literary and moral instruction: what were the teachings they embraced, recited, and expounded? Can they now fail to understand how to honor the emperor’s benevolent intentions and seek to repay them fittingly? Should they abandon their longstanding principles and pursue a different course, this record would bring them no honor. I, Wei, also bear responsibility in this matter. Should we not admonish and encourage one another?
Preface respectfully composed by Xu Wei, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yunxi County, Yunyang Prefecture, Huguang.

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
君子學道則愛人
知斯三者則知所以脩身
人皆有所不忍達之於其所忍仁也人皆
有所不為達之於其所為義也人能
充無欲害人之心而仁不可勝用也
人能充無穿踰之心而義不可勝用
也
===
易經
敦復无悔中以自考也
柔在內而剛得中
日新之謂盛德
兼三才而兩之故易六畫而成卦分陰分
陽迭用柔剛故易六位而成章
書經
在璿璣玉衡以齊七政
若作和羹爾惟鹽梅
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書
君子學道則愛人。
知斯三者，則知所以脩身。
人皆有所不忍，達之於其所忍，仁也。人皆有所不為，達之於其所為，義也。人能充無欲害人之心，而仁不可勝用也。人能充無穿踰之心，而義不可勝用也。

易經
敦復无悔，中以自考也。
柔在內而剛得中。
日新之謂盛德。
兼三才而兩之，故易六畫而成卦；分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，故易六位而成章。

書經
在璿璣玉衡，以齊七政。
若作和羹，爾惟鹽梅。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
When the gentleman studies the Way, he loves others.
Knowing these three things, one knows how to cultivate oneself.
Everyone has things he cannot bear to do. Extending this feeling to what he can bear to do is benevolence. Everyone has things he will not do. Extending this restraint to what he does do is righteousness. If one can fully develop the disposition that has no desire to harm others, one’s benevolence will be inexhaustible in its application. If one can fully develop the disposition that refuses to bore through walls or climb over them to steal, one’s righteousness will be inexhaustible in its application.

Book of Changes (Yijing)
“Returning with steadfast sincerity brings no regret”: through centrality, one examines oneself.
The yielding is within, and the firm occupies the central position.
Daily renewal is called abundant virtue.
It encompasses the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—and doubles them; thus, in the Changes, six lines form a hexagram. It distinguishes yin and yang and employs the yielding and the firm in alternation; thus, in the Changes, the six positions form an ordered pattern.

Book of Documents (Shujing)
He examined the jade celestial instrument and its jade sighting tube to bring the seven celestial regulators—the sun, moon, and five planets—into accord.
If I were preparing a well-seasoned soup, you would be its salt and sour plums.

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
六卿分職各率其屬以倡九牧阜成兆民
六年五服一朝又六年王乃時巡考
制度于四岳諸侯各朝于方岳大明
黜陟
用賚爾秬鬯一卣彤弓一彤矢百盧弓一
盧矢百
詩經
羔裘如濡洵直且侯彼其之子舍命不渝
羔裘豹飾孔武有力彼其之子邦之
===
司直羔裘晏兮三英粲兮彼其之子
邦之彦兮
豈敢定居一月三捷
卬盛于豆于豆于登其香始升上帝居歆
既作泮宫淮夷攸服
春秋
州公如曹〔桓公五年〕公會宰周公齊侯宋子
衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯于葵丘〔僖公九年〕
公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯
punctuated:
六卿分職，各率其屬，以倡九牧，阜成兆民。

六年，五服一朝；又六年，王乃時巡，考制度于四岳，諸侯各朝于方岳，大明黜陟。

用賚爾秬鬯一卣，彤弓一，彤矢百，盧弓一，盧矢百。

詩經

羔裘如濡，洵直且侯。彼其之子，舍命不渝。羔裘豹飾，孔武有力。彼其之子，邦之司直。羔裘晏兮，三英粲兮。彼其之子，邦之彦兮。

豈敢定居？一月三捷。

卬盛于豆，于豆于登。其香始升，上帝居歆。

既作泮宫，淮夷攸服。

春秋

州公如曹。〔桓公五年〕公會宰周公、齊侯、宋子、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯于葵丘。〔僖公九年〕

公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯
translation_en:
The six ministers divide their duties, each leading his subordinates, to guide the governors of the nine provinces and bring prosperity and good order to the myriad people.

Every six years, those of the five service zones attend court once. After another six years, the king makes a tour of inspection in the appropriate seasons, examining institutions and standards at the four sacred mountains. The regional lords each attend him at the sacred mountain of their region, and demotions and promotions are determined with perfect clarity.

I therefore bestow upon you one you-vessel of black-millet sacrificial wine, one red bow and one hundred red arrows, and one black bow and one hundred black arrows.

Book of Odes

His lambskin robe gleams as though moistened; truly upright and noble is he. That man will give his life without wavering. His lambskin robe is trimmed with leopard skin; he is mighty in arms and strong. That man is the state's guardian of uprightness. How splendid his lambskin robe, how brilliant its three ornaments! That man is an eminent worthy of the state.

How dare we settle down to rest? In one month, three victories!

We fill the dou dishes, the dou dishes and the deng vessels. As their fragrance begins to rise, the Lord on High accepts and enjoys the offering.

Once the Pan Palace, the state school, had been built, the Huai Yi submitted.

Spring and Autumn Annals

The Duke of Zhou 州 went to Cao. 〔Fifth year of Duke Huan.〕 The duke met with the Chief Minister, the Duke of Zhou 周, the Marquis of Qi, the Viscount of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao at Kuiqiu. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xi.〕

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
于鹹〔僖公十三年〕諸侯城緣陵〔僖公十四年〕
公會宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯晉趙
盾癸酉同盟于新城〔文公十四年〕

晉師白狄伐秦〔宣公八年〕
禮記
廟堂之上罍尊在阼犧尊在西廟堂之下
縣鼓在西應鼓在東
禮義立則貴賤等矣
===
是故君子不自大其事不自尚其功以求
處情過行弗率以求處厚彰人之善
而美人之功以求下賢
故孝弟忠順之行立而後可以為人
第貳場
論
孔子與天地參而四時同
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢戒二千石脩職詔〔景帝後二年〕
punctuated:
于鹹〔僖公十三年〕。諸侯城緣陵〔僖公十四年〕。
公會宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、晉趙盾，癸酉，同盟于新城〔文公十四年〕。
晉趙穿帥師侵崇〔宣公元年〕。秦師伐晉〔宣公二年〕。晉師、白狄伐秦〔宣公八年〕。
禮記
廟堂之上，罍尊在阼，犧尊在西；廟堂之下，縣鼓在西，應鼓在東。
禮義立，則貴賤等矣。
是故君子不自大其事，不自尚其功，以求處情；過行弗率，以求處厚；彰人之善，而美人之功，以求下賢。
故孝弟忠順之行立，而後可以為人。
第貳場
論
孔子與天地參，而四時同。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢戒二千石脩職詔〔景帝後二年〕。
translation_en:

Record of Rites
Above, in the ancestral temple hall, the lei wine vessel stands by the eastern steps, and the animal-shaped wine vessel stands to the west; below the hall, the suspended drum stands to the west, and the responding drum to the east.
When ritual and righteousness are established, the noble and the lowly have their proper ranks.
Therefore, the gentleman does not magnify his own undertakings or exalt his own achievements, seeking thereby to abide in what is genuine. He does not follow extravagant conduct, seeking thereby to abide in sincerity. He makes others’ goodness manifest and praises their achievements, seeking thereby to place himself below the worthy.
Thus, only after conduct marked by filial piety, respect for elder brothers, loyalty, and obedience has been established can one truly be a person.
Second Session
Discourse
Confucius ranks alongside Heaven and Earth and accords with the four seasons.

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
擬唐以宋璟為黃門侍郎誥〔神龍元年〕
擬宋賜禮部進士呂蒙正等及第謝表〔太平〕
〔興國元年〕
判語〔五條〕
制書有違
別籍異財
男女婚姻
毆受業師
干名犯義
===
第叄塲
策五道
問治天下者有本不獨君身而已朱子以
為治急務告君而必先之以輔翼太子
選任大臣蓋太子所以嗣天下大臣所
以輔天下根本之地所繫尤大不可以
不謹也我
朝
宣宗章皇帝嘗以君臣為人倫之首故所製五
punctuated:
擬唐以宋璟為黃門侍郎誥〔神龍元年〕。
擬宋賜禮部進士呂蒙正等及第謝表〔太平〕〔興國元年〕。
判語〔五條〕：制書有違；別籍異財；男女婚姻；毆受業師；干名犯義。

第叄塲
策五道
問：治天下者有本，不獨君身而已。朱子以為治急務告君，而必先之以輔翼太子、選任大臣。蓋太子所以嗣天下，大臣所以輔天下，根本之地，所繫尤大，不可以不謹也。我朝宣宗章皇帝嘗以君臣為人倫之首，故所製五
translation_en:

Legal judgments 〔five topics〕: Contravening an imperial edict; establishing separate household registration and dividing family property; marriage between men and women; striking the teacher under whom one has studied; violating status distinctions and moral obligations.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions
Question: Governing All under Heaven has its foundations, which lie not only in the ruler’s own person. When Master Zhu advised the ruler on the urgent tasks of government, he invariably began with supporting and guiding the heir apparent and selecting and appointing high ministers. For the heir apparent is to inherit All under Heaven, and the high ministers are to assist in governing it. These foundational positions carry especially great consequences and must be treated with care. Our dynasty’s Emperor Xuanzong Zhang once regarded the relationship between ruler and minister as foremost among human relationships; thus, in his composition on the Five …

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
倫書於建儲任人之事特加詳焉有謂
狀大多知者有謂聖表有異者有欲其
動皆由禮者有欲其練歷庶務者皆所
以為太子計也至述
太祖高皇帝之訓累數十言而不足不知於所
謂輔翼者何切有謂首百司而理陰陽
者有謂理天下必資良佐者有謂每藉
輔佐以成其理者有謂公為元老宜輔
朕政者皆所以為大臣責也至述
===
太祖高皇帝之訓歷十數事而可指不知於所
謂選任者何最今我
皇上嗣守大業動由
舊章
東宮聰明仁孝行已端矣而薰陶德性愈重
其託大臣忠敬直亮職已脩矣而咨諏
委任益盡其道其所以培植天下之根
本如此其固抑皆有得
祖宗貽謀之深意乎書曰聖有謨訓明徵定保
punctuated: 倫書，於建儲任人之事特加詳焉。有謂「狀大多知」者，有謂「聖表有異」者，有欲其動皆由禮者，有欲其練歷庶務者，皆所以為太子計也。至述太祖高皇帝之訓，累數十言而不足，不知於所謂輔翼者何切？有謂「首百司而理陰陽」者，有謂「理天下必資良佐」者，有謂「每藉輔佐以成其理」者，有謂「公為元老，宜輔朕政」者，皆所以為大臣責也。至述太祖高皇帝之訓，歷十數事而可指，不知於所謂選任者何最？今我皇上嗣守大業，動由舊章。東宮聰明仁孝，行已端矣，而薰陶德性愈重其託；大臣忠敬直亮，職已脩矣，而咨諏委任益盡其道。其所以培植天下之根本如此其固，抑皆有得祖宗貽謀之深意乎？《書》曰：「聖有謨訓，明徵定保。」
translation_en:
…Book of the Five Human Relationships, giving particular attention to establishing the heir apparent and appointing officials. Some passages speak of being “physically mature and broadly knowledgeable” [?], and others of “a sagely appearance unlike that of others.” Some express the wish that his every action accord with ritual propriety, and others that he gain experience in the many affairs of government. All these concern provision for the crown prince. When recounting the instructions of Taizu, the Gao Emperor, even several dozen statements do not suffice. Among these measures for assisting and guiding the crown prince, which is most essential?

Some passages speak of “heading the hundred offices and harmonizing yin and yang”; others say that “governing the realm requires worthy assistants,” that “one always relies on assistants to accomplish its governance,” or that “you, as a venerable senior minister, should assist my government.” All these concern the responsibilities of high ministers. When recounting the instructions of Taizu, the Gao Emperor, more than ten specific matters can be identified. Among these measures for selecting and appointing ministers, which is foremost?

Now our Emperor has inherited and safeguards the great imperial enterprise, following established precedents in every action. The crown prince is intelligent, humane, and filial, and his conduct is already upright; yet the charge of nurturing his moral character is entrusted with ever greater care. The high ministers are loyal, respectful, upright, and trustworthy, and already discharge their duties well; yet the proper methods of consulting them and entrusting them with responsibilities are observed ever more fully. The foundations of the realm are thus cultivated and made so secure: might all this reflect an understanding of the profound intent of the plans bequeathed by the imperial ancestors? The Book of Documents says: “The sage has counsels and instructions; clearly verify them, establish them, and preserve them.” …

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
諸生皆囿於
盛治之下盍宣揚
聖訓之萬一以示天下後世
問六經之文尚矣自周而下文之純駁不
齊由人之學術有淺深世道有隆污耳
請相與評之文者貫道之器唐人有是
言矣何以有以本為末之譏文必與道
俱宋人有是言矣何以有二本之說法
言擬乎論語者也何以譏其為長楊較
獵之流聖德頌無愧風雅者也何以譏
其為李斯頌秦之陋大學之明明德學
也有言為文之大者何歟聖門之道義
德也有指為文之一般者何歟有治世
之文有衰世之文有亂世之文何以見
有譎諫之文有裁成之文有通儒之文
何以名後世諸子之文不一也何者為
文之祖聖人經世之文常道也何者為
經之變作文必要悟入有讀伯夷傳而
punctuated:
諸生皆囿於盛治之下，盍宣揚聖訓之萬一，以示天下後世？

問：六經之文尚矣！自周而下，文之純駁不齊，由人之學術有淺深，世道有隆污耳。請相與評之。「文者貫道之器」，唐人有是言矣，何以有以本為末之譏？「文必與道俱」，宋人有是言矣，何以有二本之說？《法言》擬乎《論語》者也，何以譏其為《長楊》《較獵》之流？《聖德頌》無愧《風》《雅》者也，何以譏其為李斯頌秦之陋？《大學》之明明德，學也，有言為文之大者，何歟？聖門之道義，德也，有指為文之一般者，何歟？有治世之文，有衰世之文，有亂世之文，何以見？有譎諫之文，有裁成之文，有通儒之文，何以名？後世諸子之文不一也，何者為文之祖？聖人經世之文，常道也，何者為經之變？作文必要悟入，有讀《伯夷傳》而
translation_en:
…You students all live within the embrace of this flourishing reign. Why not expound even a fraction of the sage instructions, to make them known to the world and to later generations?

Question: The writings of the Six Classics are venerable indeed! From the Zhou onward, writings have varied in their purity and admixture, simply because people’s learning has differed in depth and the condition of the world has risen or declined. Let us examine these matters together.

“Writing is a vessel that conveys the Way”: a man of the Tang said this. Why, then, was he criticized for treating the root as the branch? “Writing must accompany the Way”: a man of the Song said this. Why, then, was there talk of establishing two roots? Model Sayings (Fayan) was patterned upon the Analects. Why was it criticized as belonging to the same class as the Rhapsody on Changyang Palace and the Rhapsody on the Hunt (Jiaolie)? The Ode to Sagely Virtue could stand without shame beside the Airs and Odes. Why was it criticized as sharing the baseness of Li Si’s praise of Qin?

The Great Learning’s “making luminous virtue manifest” concerns learning. Why has someone called it the greatest form of writing? The Way and moral principles taught in the school of the sages concern virtue. Why has someone identified them as one category of writing? There are writings of well-governed ages, writings of declining ages, and writings of disordered ages: how can these be recognized? There are writings of indirect remonstrance, writings that shape and perfect, and writings of comprehensively learned Confucians: on what grounds are these names given?

The writings of the various masters of later ages are diverse. Which constitute the progenitor of writing? The sages’ writings for ordering the world embody the constant Way. Which constitute variations upon the Classics? Composing writing necessarily requires a breakthrough in understanding. There was someone who read the Biography of Bo Yi and…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
悟者有讀貨殖傳而悟者誰歟學文必
得古法有自戰國策而得者有自孟子
書而得者誰歟文有六說三等之辨古
能一之何道文有四科三易之殊今欲
備之何由唐之文莫過於韓柳其學之
有得於六經者何在宋之文莫過於歐
蘇其文之有同於韓柳者何居經所以
明道後世明道之儒其文章有可以表
裏六經者乎學貴乎窮經後世窮經之
===
士其文章有可為六經之階梯者乎夫
由六經之階梯而造乎六經之蘊奧則
漢唐以下辭章之文不足貴矣請條陳
之毋忽
問古之人布衣而有公輔之望江湖而有
廟堂之思則宰相之職雖在筮仕之初
要不可以不講也三代而上若伏羲之
六佐黃帝之六相唐虞之百揆有商之
伊傅成周之周召固無容議矣三代
punctuated:
悟者，有讀《貨殖傳》而悟者，誰歟？學文必得古法，有自《戰國策》而得者，有自《孟子》書而得者，誰歟？文有六說三等之辨，古能一之，何道？文有四科三易之殊，今欲備之，何由？唐之文莫過於韓柳，其學之有得於六經者何在？宋之文莫過於歐蘇，其文之有同於韓柳者何居？經所以明道，後世明道之儒，其文章有可以表裏六經者乎？學貴乎窮經，後世窮經之士，其文章有可為六經之階梯者乎？夫由六經之階梯而造乎六經之蘊奧，則漢唐以下辭章之文不足貴矣。請條陳之，毋忽。
問：古之人布衣而有公輔之望，江湖而有廟堂之思，則宰相之職，雖在筮仕之初，要不可以不講也。三代而上，若伏羲之六佐、黃帝之六相、唐虞之百揆、有商之伊傅、成周之周召，固無容議矣。三代
translation_en:
…gained insight; others gained insight from reading the Biographies of the Money-makers. Who were they? In studying composition, one must grasp the methods of antiquity. Some acquired them from the Stratagems of the Warring States, others from the book of Mencius. Who were they? Writing has distinctions of six theories and three grades: by what means could the ancients unify them? Writing has differences of four categories and three kinds of ease [?]: by what means can one now encompass them all? Among Tang writers, none surpassed Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan. In what respects did their learning draw upon the Six Classics? Among Song writers, none surpassed Ouyang Xiu and Su Shi. In what respects did their writing resemble that of Han and Liu? The Classics serve to illuminate the Way. Among later Confucian scholars who illuminated the Way, were there any whose writings could complement the Six Classics as outer and inner aspects of a whole? In learning, what matters is to investigate the Classics thoroughly. Among later scholars who investigated the Classics thoroughly, were there any whose writings could serve as steps leading up to the Six Classics? If one proceeds by these steps to reach the profound mysteries of the Six Classics, then the literary compositions of the Han and Tang and subsequent ages are scarcely worth esteeming. Please set out your answers point by point, neglecting none.
Question: Men of antiquity, though still clad in commoners’ clothes, showed promise of becoming chief ministers; though dwelling among rivers and lakes, they gave thought to affairs of court. Thus, even at the very beginning of an official career, one must study the duties of a chief councilor. As for the Three Dynasties and earlier times—Fuxi’s six assistants, the Yellow Emperor’s six ministers, the directors of the hundred affairs under Yao and Shun, Yi Yin and Fu Yue of the Shang, and the Dukes of Zhou and Shao of the Zhou—these surely admit of no dispute. The Three Dynasties…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
下稱漢相者必曰蕭曹丙魏稱唐相者
必曰房杜姚宋稱宋相者必曰韓范富
歐皆足以為賢矣然數子之外豈無可
稱之人歟夫論其世必知其名循其人
必責其實就一人而論之何者為長何
者為短歟就一代而論之何人為優何
人為劣歟就數子而通論之又何人為
卓冠歟諸士子行將陟華躋要以効用
于時不知所設施者以何人為法以何
===
事為先以何言為要歟夫比方人物固
聖人不暇為不知人亦君子所當患幸
悉陳之
問將者三軍之司命國家安危之所繫也
求之貴乎廣任之貴乎專求之不廣則
才或遺任之不專則才難盡試以昔人
之所論者言之有謂就諸班中搜羅智
勇者有謂只於軍中自可求將者有謂
可復武舉而為之新制者有謂請近臣
punctuated:
下，稱漢相者必曰蕭、曹、丙、魏，稱唐相者必曰房、杜、姚、宋，稱宋相者必曰韓、范、富、歐，皆足以為賢矣。然數子之外，豈無可稱之人歟？夫論其世，必知其名；循其人，必責其實。就一人而論之，何者為長，何者為短歟？就一代而論之，何人為優，何人為劣歟？就數子而通論之，又何人為卓冠歟？諸士子行將陟華躋要，以効用于時，不知所設施者，以何人為法，以何事為先，以何言為要歟？夫比方人物，固聖人不暇為；不知人，亦君子所當患。幸悉陳之。

問：將者，三軍之司命，國家安危之所繫也。求之貴乎廣，任之貴乎專。求之不廣，則才或遺；任之不專，則才難盡。試以昔人之所論者言之：有謂就諸班中搜羅智勇者，有謂只於軍中自可求將者，有謂可復武舉而為之新制者，有謂請近臣
translation_en:
…after the Three Dynasties, those who speak of Han chief ministers invariably name Xiao He, Cao Shen, Bing Ji, and Wei Xiang; those who speak of Tang chief ministers invariably name Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, Yao Chong, and Song Jing; and those who speak of Song chief ministers invariably name Han Qi, Fan Zhongyan, Fu Bi, and Ouyang Xiu. All deserve to be considered worthy. Yet beyond these men, were there no others deserving praise? In discussing their times, one must know their reputations; in examining the men themselves, one must demand evidence of their actual achievements. Considering each man individually, what were his strengths and weaknesses? Considering each dynasty, who was superior and who inferior? Considering all these men together, who stood foremost? You candidates will soon ascend to illustrious and important posts, putting your abilities to use in your age. In carrying out your duties, whom will you take as your model, what matters will you put first, and what words will you regard as essential? Comparing individuals was indeed something the sage had no leisure to do; yet failure to understand others is also something a gentleman should be concerned about. Please set forth your views in full.

Question: A general holds the lives of the armies in his charge; upon him depend the security and peril of the state. In seeking generals, breadth is essential; in employing them, undivided trust is essential. If the search is not broad, talent may be overlooked; if the trust placed in them is not undivided, their abilities cannot be fully exercised. Consider what men of former times have argued: some advocated searching among the various ranks for men of wisdom and courage; some maintained that generals could be found within the army itself; some proposed restoring the military examinations and establishing new regulations for them; and some proposed requesting that ministers close to the throne…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
及藩鎮大臣各舉有武略者其求將之
方可謂廣矣然止於此而已乎抑别有
他道乎有言端拱於委任者有言宜久
於其職者有言進退不可輕用人言者
有言功必賞罪必刑者其任將之道可
謂專矣然止於是而已乎抑或有他術
乎方今醜虜桀驁邊境告急兵不可一
日而去戰不可一日而忘則將誠不可
不廣求而專任之也諸士子懷有用之
===
學必慮之熟矣請悉陳之將采擇以
獻
問先民有言達時務者為俊傑知大體者
為志士諸士子游庠序之中抱用世之
學皆有志之士俊傑之才也特舉其一
二時務大體以商確之科目賢才所由
出也古今之法詳矣何者為至當考課
治道所由興也古今之法備矣何者為
至要教化以士習為先何法而可以去
punctuated:
及藩鎮大臣各舉有武略者，其求將之方可謂廣矣。然止於此而已乎？抑别有他道乎？有言端拱於委任者，有言宜久於其職者，有言進退不可輕用人言者，有言功必賞、罪必刑者，其任將之道可謂專矣。然止於是而已乎？抑或有他術乎？方今醜虜桀驁，邊境告急，兵不可一日而去，戰不可一日而忘，則將誠不可不廣求而專任之也。諸士子懷有用之學，必慮之熟矣。請悉陳之，將采擇以獻。

問：先民有言：「達時務者為俊傑，知大體者為志士。」諸士子游庠序之中，抱用世之學，皆有志之士、俊傑之才也。特舉其一二時務、大體以商確之。科目，賢才所由出也，古今之法詳矣，何者為至當？考課，治道所由興也，古今之法備矣，何者為至要？教化以士習為先，何法而可以去
translation_en:
…and the high ministers commanding regional garrisons each to recommend men versed in military strategy. These methods of seeking generals may be called broad indeed. Yet should one stop at these alone, or are there other ways? Some have said that the ruler should sit with hands folded, entrusting responsibility to his appointees; some, that generals should remain long in their posts; some, that in promoting or dismissing them one must not lightly act upon what others say; and some, that merit must be rewarded and offenses punished. These approaches to employing generals may be said to give them undivided responsibility. Yet should one stop at these alone, or are there other methods? At present the vile enemy is unruly, and urgent alarms come from the frontier. Troops cannot be dispensed with for a single day, nor can warfare be forgotten for a single day. Thus generals must indeed be sought widely and entrusted with undivided responsibility. You candidates possess learning suited to practical use and must have considered these matters thoroughly. Please set out your views in full; selections will be made for presentation to the throne.

Question: Our predecessors said: “Those who comprehend the affairs of their time are outstanding talents; those who understand the larger essentials are men of resolve.” You candidates study in the schools and possess learning suited to serving the world. You are all men of resolve and outstanding ability. We raise just one or two matters concerning contemporary affairs and the larger essentials for discussion and careful consideration. The examination system is the means by which worthy talent emerges. Its methods, ancient and modern, have been elaborated in detail: which are the most appropriate? Performance evaluations are the means by which good government flourishes. Their methods, ancient and modern, are fully developed: which are the most essential? Moral education gives priority to the habits of scholars. By what method can one eliminate…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
其奔競之風致治以得民為本何施而
可以結其愛戴之心甲兵所以禦侮今
戎伍耗矣若何而可以足兵穀粟所以
養民今倉廩竭矣若何而可以足食夷
狄不能無也伊欲使之不擾吾邊也何
道異端不能免也伊欲使之不惑吾民
也何方凡是數者其所關於時務甚大
於此而不知惡乎有所知耶其為我詳
著于篇
punctuated: 其奔競之風？致治以得民為本，何施而可以結其愛戴之心？甲兵所以禦侮，今戎伍耗矣，若何而可以足兵？穀粟所以養民，今倉廩竭矣，若何而可以足食？夷狄不能無也，伊欲使之不擾吾邊也，何道？異端不能免也，伊欲使之不惑吾民也，何方？凡是數者，其所關於時務甚大，於此而不知，惡乎有所知耶？其為我詳著于篇。
translation_en: …their tendency to scramble for advancement? Achieving good government rests on winning over the people: what measures can secure their affection and allegiance? Arms and troops serve to repel aggression, but the ranks are now depleted: how can troop strength be made sufficient? Grain serves to sustain the people, but the granaries are now exhausted: how can food supplies be made sufficient? The peoples beyond our borders cannot be made to cease to exist; by what means, then, can we keep them from disturbing our frontiers? Heterodox teachings cannot be avoided; by what methods, then, can we keep them from deluding our people? All these matters have a very great bearing on the pressing affairs of the day. If you do not understand these, what can you claim to understand? Set forth your views for me in detail in your essays.

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
君子學道則愛人
張𤇍
同考試官訓導俞批題以禮樂立說前
後貫串渾然無斧鑿痕作手也
同考試官教諭魏批文足以發題意他
日有位必能推所學以愛人者
考試官教諭姜批親切有味
===
考試官教諭徐批文有曲折斡旋可
羨
惟在上知所學則於下知所愛夫愛人本於學
道也然則君子之於道可不知所學哉昔子游
以禮樂治武城因夫子莞爾之戲而質以平日
所聞之言如此意謂君子任民社之寄有家國
之責固不可以不學學不可以不致於道必也
格物致知而於事物之理無不明篤志力行而
於事物之理無不體如道不外乎禮也而禮有
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
君子學道則愛人
張𤇍

同考試官訓導俞批：題以禮樂立說，前後貫串，渾然無斧鑿痕，作手也。
同考試官教諭魏批：文足以發題意，他日有位，必能推所學以愛人者。
考試官教諭姜批：親切有味。
考試官教諭徐批：文有曲折斡旋，可羨。

惟在上知所學，則於下知所愛。夫愛人本於學道也，然則君子之於道，可不知所學哉？昔子游以禮樂治武城，因夫子莞爾之戲，而質以平日所聞之言如此。意謂君子任民社之寄，有家國之責，固不可以不學，學不可以不致於道。必也格物致知，而於事物之理無不明；篤志力行，而於事物之理無不體。如道不外乎禮也，而禮有
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“When the gentleman studies the Way, he loves others”
Zhang 𤇍 [given-name reading uncertain]

Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Assistant Instructor: The argument on the topic is grounded in rites and music and is coherent throughout, perfectly integrated without any trace of forced workmanship. This is an accomplished writer.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wei, Instructor: The essay fully brings out the meaning of the topic. When the author holds office in the future, he will surely be able to extend what he has learned to loving others.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: Apt and rich in meaning.

Comment by Examiner Xu, Instructor: The essay develops through turns and skillful transitions—admirable.

Only when those above know what to learn will they know how to love those below. Loving others is rooted in studying the Way. Can the gentleman, then, fail to know what he must learn concerning the Way? Formerly, Ziyou governed Wucheng through rites and music. When the Master smiled and teased him, he responded by appealing to words he had previously heard from him, as quoted here. His meaning was that a gentleman entrusted with the people and the altars of the soil, bearing responsibility for a ruling house and its state, certainly cannot dispense with learning; nor can his learning fail to reach the Way. He must investigate things and extend his knowledge, leaving no principle of affairs and things uncomprehended; he must be steadfast in purpose and diligent in practice, leaving no principle of affairs and things unembodied in his conduct. Thus, the Way does not lie outside ritual, and ritual has…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
三千三百之詳君子則博而約之以究其至中
之歸道不外乎樂也而樂有五聲六律之變君
子則講而習之以探其至和之蘊由是持循也
久而鄙詐慢易之心釋涵養也熟而易直子諒
之心生以之治人則廓然大公而無非仁愛之
周流以之臨民則怡然樂易而無非慈愛之浹
洽如民未協乎中吾所憫也於是節之以禮使
其薰陶漸染而皆趨於至中之域民未得其和
吾不忍也於是和之以樂使其優游厭飫而皆
===
囿於至和之化夫君子學道之功至於如此曾
謂爲治者可不以禮樂爲教哉嗟夫天下一道
也君子學之則愛人小人學之則易使皆不可
以不學也彼武城雖小將爲君子焉將爲小人
焉使不以禮樂爲教則上虐其下下凌其上不
可一日而爲治矣故子游以昔日之所聞爲今
日之所教誠知所先務矣夫子驟聞而深喜之
不亦宜乎
知斯三者則知所以脩身
punctuated:
三千三百之詳，君子則博而約之，以究其至中之歸。道不外乎樂也，而樂有五聲六律之變，君子則講而習之，以探其至和之蘊。由是持循也久，而鄙詐慢易之心釋；涵養也熟，而易直子諒之心生。以之治人，則廓然大公，而無非仁愛之周流；以之臨民，則怡然樂易，而無非慈愛之浹洽。如民未協乎中，吾所憫也，於是節之以禮，使其薰陶漸染，而皆趨於至中之域；民未得其和，吾不忍也，於是和之以樂，使其優游厭飫，而皆囿於至和之化。夫君子學道之功至於如此，曾謂爲治者可不以禮樂爲教哉？嗟夫！天下一道也，君子學之則愛人，小人學之則易使，皆不可以不學也。彼武城雖小，將爲君子焉，將爲小人焉，使不以禮樂爲教，則上虐其下，下凌其上，不可一日而爲治矣。故子游以昔日之所聞爲今日之所教，誠知所先務矣。夫子驟聞而深喜之，不亦宜乎？

知斯三者，則知所以脩身。
translation_en:
…with their three thousand and three hundred detailed provisions. The gentleman studies them broadly and draws them together into their essentials, seeking their ultimate convergence in perfect balance. The Way likewise does not lie outside music. Music has the variations of the five notes and six pitch standards; the gentleman studies and practices these to explore the depths of perfect harmony. Through sustained observance, thoughts of baseness, deceit, arrogance, and disrespect dissolve; as moral cultivation matures, an easy, upright, loving, and trustworthy disposition arises. Applied to governing others, this produces an expansive impartiality through which benevolence flows everywhere. Applied to presiding over the people, it produces a cheerful ease through which compassionate care reaches all. If the people have not attained balance, this arouses my compassion. I therefore regulate them through ritual, allowing its gradual influence to bring them all toward perfect balance. If the people have not attained harmony, I cannot bear it. I therefore harmonize them through music, allowing them to dwell at ease in it and absorb it fully, until all are embraced by the transforming influence of perfect harmony.

When the gentleman’s achievement in learning the Way reaches this point, could anyone claim that those who govern need not teach through ritual and music? Ah! There is one Way throughout the world. When gentlemen learn it, they love others; when common people learn it, they become easy to direct. Neither can dispense with learning it. Small though Wucheng is, there will be gentlemen there, and there will be common people. If ritual and music are not used to teach them, those above will oppress those below, and those below will defy those above; orderly government could not be maintained for even a day. Thus Ziyou made what he had heard in former days the basis of what he taught in his own day. He truly understood what deserved priority. Was it not fitting that the Master, upon hearing of this, should have been deeply pleased?

Knowing these three things, one knows how to cultivate oneself.

考試官教諭姜批平正通達有
國初渾厚氣味
考試官教諭徐批可謂文章爾雅者
===
能知所以入乎德則知所以治乎己蓋治己本
乎道而行道本乎德也能知入德之事則所以
行道而脩身者豈外是哉中庸引夫子告哀公
之言以明道之費隱及此謂夫為政之本固在
於身而脩身之道則由於德德豈易及哉是故
知雖有未及也能知自是之為愚而惟學之是
好則足以破愚而近乎知焉仁雖有未及也能
知徇欲之為私而惟行之是力則足以忘私而
近乎仁焉勇雖有未及也能知甘為人下之為
punctuated:
戴大賓

同考試官教諭李批：題中二知字頗為有力，而所以脩身處亦難發揮。惟此作剖析明白，而詞理俱到，故録之。

同考試官學正王批：題甚冠冕，而佳作絶少。求其辭理明暢、快人心目者，僅見此篇，允宜前列。

考試官教諭姜批：平正通達，有國初渾厚氣味。

考試官教諭徐批：可謂文章爾雅者。

能知所以入乎德，則知所以治乎己。蓋治己本乎道，而行道本乎德也。能知入德之事，則所以行道而脩身者，豈外是哉？中庸引夫子告哀公之言，以明道之費隱。及此，謂夫為政之本固在於身，而脩身之道則由於德。德豈易及哉？是故知雖有未及也，能知自是之為愚，而惟學之是好，則足以破愚而近乎知焉。仁雖有未及也，能知徇欲之為私，而惟行之是力，則足以忘私而近乎仁焉。勇雖有未及也，能知甘為人下之為
translation_en:
Dai Dabin

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: The two occurrences of “know” in the topic carry considerable force, while the passage concerning the means of cultivating oneself is also difficult to expound. This composition alone analyzes the matter clearly and does full justice to both expression and reasoning; hence its inclusion.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, School Director: The topic is most dignified, yet excellent compositions are exceedingly few. In seeking one whose expression and reasoning are clear and fluent, delighting the reader’s mind and eye, I have found only this essay. It certainly deserves a place among the foremost.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: Balanced, correct, and lucid, it has the substantial, unadorned quality characteristic of the dynasty’s early years.

Comment by Examiner Xu, Instructor: This may well be called a composition of literary refinement and correctness.

If one can understand how to enter into virtue, one understands how to govern oneself. For governing oneself is rooted in the Way, while practicing the Way is rooted in virtue. If one understands what entering into virtue entails, how could the means of practicing the Way and cultivating oneself lie outside this? The Doctrine of the Mean quotes the Master’s words to Duke Ai to illuminate the Way’s wide reach and hidden subtlety. At this point, it says that the foundation of government assuredly lies in oneself, while the means of cultivating oneself proceeds from virtue. But is virtue easy to attain? Thus, although one may not yet have attained wisdom, if one can recognize the foolishness of assuming oneself to be right and devote oneself solely to a love of learning, this suffices to overcome foolishness and draw near to wisdom. Although one may not yet have attained benevolence, if one can recognize the selfishness of yielding to desires and exert oneself solely in practice, this suffices to forget selfishness and draw near to benevolence. Although one may not yet have attained courage, if one can recognize that being content to remain beneath others is …

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
懦而恥之則其學也不厭其行也不倦亦足以
起懦而近乎勇焉夫知三近以入德則知行道
以脩身彼知所以知達道也道有未知則身有
未脩能知好學近乎知則必以此知而知此道
心與道而相涵矣非知所以脩身乎仁所以體
達道也道有未體則身有未脩能知力行近乎
仁則必以此仁而體此道身與道而相安矣又
非知所以脩身乎勇所以強達道也使道有餒
焉則身亦不可得而脩矣能知知恥近乎勇則
===
必以此勇而強此道愚可進於明柔可進於強
不謂之脩身而何哉是則欲盡脩身之道當先
入德之事君子欲脩其身者可不知所務歟大
抵人君一身家國天下之本也不脩其身則取
舍不明而無以為取人之則欲家國天下之治
難矣故夫子於哀公之問既曰脩身以道脩道
以仁又曰君子不可以不脩身下文又以脩身
為九經之首一篇之中言之不一而足無非欲
其脩身以立家國天下之本耳哀公果能體而
punctuated: 懦而恥之，則其學也不厭，其行也不倦，亦足以起懦而近乎勇焉。夫知三近以入德，則知行道以脩身。彼知所以知達道也，道有未知，則身有未脩。能知好學近乎知，則必以此知而知此道，心與道而相涵矣，非知所以脩身乎？仁所以體達道也，道有未體，則身有未脩。能知力行近乎仁，則必以此仁而體此道，身與道而相安矣，又非知所以脩身乎？勇所以強達道也，使道有餒焉，則身亦不可得而脩矣。能知知恥近乎勇，則必以此勇而強此道，愚可進於明，柔可進於強，不謂之脩身而何哉？是則欲盡脩身之道，當先入德之事。君子欲脩其身者，可不知所務歟？大抵人君一身，家國天下之本也。不脩其身，則取舍不明，而無以為取人之則，欲家國天下之治難矣。故夫子於哀公之問，既曰「脩身以道，脩道以仁」，又曰「君子不可以不脩身」。下文又以脩身為九經之首，一篇之中言之不一而足，無非欲其脩身以立家國天下之本耳。哀公果能體而
translation_en:
…cowardice and feel ashamed of it, then one will be tireless in learning and unflagging in practice. This too is sufficient to rouse one from cowardice and bring one close to courage. Knowing these three approaches to virtue, one knows how to practice the Way and thereby cultivate oneself. Wisdom is what enables one to understand the universally applicable Way. Wherever the Way remains unknown, self-cultivation remains incomplete. If one knows that loving learning brings one close to wisdom, one will surely use this wisdom to understand this Way, so that the mind and the Way mutually permeate one another. Is this not knowing how to cultivate oneself? Benevolence is what enables one to embody the universally applicable Way. Wherever the Way remains unembodied, self-cultivation remains incomplete. If one knows that strenuous practice brings one close to benevolence, one will surely use this benevolence to embody this Way, so that one's person and the Way are at ease with one another. Is this not, again, knowing how to cultivate oneself? Courage is what enables one steadfastly to uphold the universally applicable Way. If one's commitment to the Way falters, self-cultivation likewise becomes impossible. If one knows that knowing shame brings one close to courage, one will surely use this courage steadfastly to uphold this Way. The ignorant can advance toward understanding, and the weak toward strength. What could this be called but self-cultivation? Thus, to fulfill the way of self-cultivation, one must first attend to the means of entering into virtue. Can a gentleman who wishes to cultivate himself fail to know where to direct his efforts?

In general, the ruler's own person is the foundation of the family, the state, and all under Heaven. If he does not cultivate himself, he will lack discernment in what he accepts and rejects, and thus have no standard for selecting men. It will then be difficult to bring order to the family, the state, and all under Heaven. Thus, in answering Duke Ai's question, Confucius said both, “Cultivate oneself through the Way, and cultivate the Way through benevolence,” and “The gentleman cannot fail to cultivate himself.” The subsequent text also places self-cultivation first among the nine guiding principles. Within this single chapter, the subject is repeatedly addressed, always with the intention that the ruler cultivate himself and thereby establish the foundation of the family, the state, and all under Heaven. If Duke Ai could truly embody this and…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
行之則有君有臣而政無不舉東魯其西周矣
惜乎其不能也噫
人皆有所不忍達之於其所忍仁也人皆
有所不為達之於其所為義也人能充無
欲害人之心而仁不可勝用也人能充無
穿窬之心而義不可勝用也
陳良山
同考試官教諭杜批達充二字此題關鍵
場中知者絕少此作會註成文而理自見錄之
===
同考試官教諭羅批意達而詞不費稠
人中僅見此篇
考試官教諭姜批融會傳註成文冲
淡中有不盡之味
考試官教諭徐批簡潔
推仁義之端而用以行充仁義之量而用以廣
夫仁義之心本然全具也誠能推而充之豈有
不足於用哉昔孟子之意謂夫仁義之性雖出
於天而擴充之功則在於人是故惻隱之心仁
punctuated:
行之，則有君有臣，而政無不舉，東魯其西周矣。惜乎其不能也！噫！

「人皆有所不忍，達之於其所忍，仁也；人皆有所不為，達之於其所為，義也。人能充無欲害人之心，而仁不可勝用也；人能充無穿窬之心，而義不可勝用也。」

陳良山

同考試官教諭杜批：「達、充二字，此題關鍵。場中知者絕少，此作會註成文，而理自見，錄之。」

同考試官教諭羅批：「意達而詞不費，稠人中僅見此篇。」

考試官教諭姜批：「融會傳註成文，冲淡中有不盡之味。」

考試官教諭徐批：「簡潔。」

推仁義之端，而用以行；充仁義之量，而用以廣。夫仁義之心，本然全具也。誠能推而充之，豈有不足於用哉？昔孟子之意，謂夫仁義之性雖出於天，而擴充之功則在於人。是故惻隱之心，仁
translation_en:
…put it into practice, then ruler and ministers would each fulfill their roles, and every affair of government would be carried out. Lu in the east would become another Western Zhou. Alas that he could not do so! Ah!

“All people have things they cannot bear to do. To extend this feeling to what they can bear to do is benevolence. All people have things they will not do. To extend this restraint to what they will do is righteousness. If people can fully develop the heart that has no desire to harm others, their benevolence will be inexhaustible in its application. If people can fully develop the heart that has no desire to break through walls or climb over them to steal, their righteousness will be inexhaustible in its application.”

Chen Liangshan

Associate Examiner Du, Instructor, comments: “The two words ‘extend’ and ‘fully develop’ are the key to this topic. Very few in the examination hall understood this. This composition integrates the annotations into an essay, and the principle emerges of itself. I select it for inclusion.”

Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: “The meaning is fully conveyed without wasting words. Among the multitude of candidates, this is the only essay of its kind I have seen.”

Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “The commentaries and annotations are thoroughly assimilated into the composition. Within its tranquil simplicity lies an inexhaustible savor.”

Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “Concise and clear.”

Extend the beginnings of benevolence and righteousness, and their application is put into practice; fully develop the capacity for benevolence and righteousness, and their application becomes broad. The heart of benevolence and righteousness is, in its original state, fully endowed with both. If one can truly extend and fully develop it, how could it ever prove insufficient in practice? What Mencius meant was that, although the nature endowed with benevolence and righteousness comes from Heaven, the work of extending and fully developing it rests with human beings. Thus, the heart of compassion is benevolence’s…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
之端也人皆有之故莫不有所不忍焉然氣拘
物蔽有不忍於此而或忍於彼者但推所不忍
以達於所忍則惻隱之心無所壅蔽而無非仁
矣羞惡之心義之端也人皆有之故莫不有所
不爲焉然知誘物化有不爲於此而或爲於彼
者但推所不爲以達於所爲則羞惡之心無所
間隔而無非義矣夫有所不忍即無欲害人之
心也人能推所不忍以達於所忍而至於事事
皆不忍焉則能充其無欲害人之心而愛無不
===
周矣仁之用寧有既乎有所不爲即無穿窬之
心也人能推所不爲以達於所爲而至于事事
皆不爲焉則能滿其無穿窬之心而行無不宜
矣義之用寧有窮乎是則仁義之心人所固有
苟有之而不能推推之而不能充而以爲未嘗
有仁義焉者是豈人之本心哉太抵人有是心
莫非全體雖包括天地兼利萬物亦其能事也
然有所蔽而不能盡乎此心之量則恩及禽獸
而功不至于百姓耻受嘑蹴而義不辨乎萬鍾
punctuated: 之端也，人皆有之，故莫不有所不忍焉。然氣拘物蔽，有不忍於此而或忍於彼者。但推所不忍，以達於所忍，則惻隱之心無所壅蔽，而無非仁矣。羞惡之心，義之端也，人皆有之，故莫不有所不爲焉。然知誘物化，有不爲於此而或爲於彼者。但推所不爲，以達於所爲，則羞惡之心無所間隔，而無非義矣。夫有所不忍，即無欲害人之心也。人能推所不忍，以達於所忍，而至於事事皆不忍焉，則能充其無欲害人之心，而愛無不周矣。仁之用寧有既乎？有所不爲，即無穿窬之心也。人能推所不爲，以達於所爲，而至于事事皆不爲焉，則能滿其無穿窬之心，而行無不宜矣。義之用寧有窮乎？是則仁義之心，人所固有。苟有之而不能推，推之而不能充，而以爲未嘗有仁義焉者，是豈人之本心哉？太抵人有是心，莫非全體，雖包括天地、兼利萬物，亦其能事也。然有所蔽，而不能盡乎此心之量，則恩及禽獸而功不至于百姓，耻受嘑蹴而義不辨乎萬鍾
translation_en:
… is the sprout of benevolence. Everyone possesses it, and thus everyone has things they cannot bear to do. Yet, constrained by their material constitution and obscured by external things, people may be unable to bear doing one thing while being able to bear doing another. If they simply extend what they cannot bear to do to encompass what they can bear to do, their compassion will be neither obstructed nor obscured, and all will be benevolence. The sense of shame and aversion is the sprout of righteousness. Everyone possesses it, and thus everyone has things they will not do. Yet, with their understanding enticed and themselves swayed by external things, people may refuse to do one thing while doing another. If they simply extend what they refuse to do to encompass what they do, their sense of shame and aversion will encounter no barrier, and all will be righteousness.

Having things one cannot bear to do is precisely having a heart that does not desire to harm others. If people can extend what they cannot bear to do to encompass what they can bear to do, until they cannot bear to cause harm in any matter, they can fully develop this heart that does not desire to harm others, and their love will embrace everyone. How could the application of benevolence ever be exhausted? Having things one refuses to do is precisely having a heart that has no wish to break through walls or climb over them to steal. If people can extend what they refuse to do to encompass what they do, until they refuse wrongdoing in every matter, they can bring this heart that has no wish to steal to its fullness, and all their conduct will be fitting. How could the application of righteousness ever reach its limit?

Thus, the heart of benevolence and righteousness is inherent in everyone. If people possess it but cannot extend it, or extend it but cannot develop it fully, and then conclude that they never possessed benevolence or righteousness, how could this reflect their original heart? Generally speaking, this heart exists in everyone in its entirety. Even embracing Heaven and Earth and benefiting all things together lies within its capacity. Yet when it is obscured and people cannot fully realize its scope, their kindness may reach birds and beasts while its benefits fail to reach the common people; they may feel ashamed to accept food offered with a shout or a kick, yet fail to discern what is right when faced with a stipend of ten thousand measures of grain…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
者有矣是皆不善推其所為也故孟子教人因
其善端之發而悉推之以各造乎其極則天之
所以與我者可以無不盡矣說者謂孟子平生
受用惟在善推所為一語觀此尤信
易
敦復无悔中以自考也
張燮
同考試官訓導俞批自考就復上立說
非膚見可到
===
同考試官教諭魏批敦復自考原無二
道是作能知之而辭又醞藉宜錄出以破群疑
考試官教諭姜批詞不費而意盡
考試官教諭徐批深得象傳申爻之
旨
論復之厚而无慊於內惟中之成而无待於外
此易象之旨也盖復不外乎中德也今以中德
而自成於已豈非復之厚而无慊於內者乎且
夫復之六五中順居尊當復之時周公繫以敦
punctuated:
者有矣。是皆不善推其所為也。故孟子教人因其善端之發而悉推之，以各造乎其極，則天之所以與我者可以無不盡矣。說者謂孟子平生受用，惟在善推所為一語，觀此尤信。

易
敦復无悔，中以自考也。
張燮

同考試官訓導俞批：自考就復上立說，非膚見可到。
同考試官教諭魏批：敦復自考，原無二道。是作能知之，而辭又醞藉，宜錄出以破群疑。
考試官教諭姜批：詞不費而意盡。
考試官教諭徐批：深得象傳申爻之旨。

論復之厚而无慊於內，惟中之成而无待於外，此易象之旨也。盖復不外乎中德也。今以中德而自成於已，豈非復之厚而无慊於內者乎？且夫復之六五，中順居尊，當復之時，周公繫以敦
translation_en:
…there are such people. All this results from failing to extend properly what they already practice. Thus Mencius teaches people to take the emerging sprouts of goodness and extend them fully, bringing each to its utmost development. In this way, everything Heaven has endowed us with can be fully realized. Commentators say that what Mencius relied upon throughout his life lay solely in the phrase “skillfully extending what one already practices.” This passage makes that claim especially convincing.

Book of Changes
“Wholehearted return brings no regret: through centrality one brings oneself to completion.”
Zhang Xie

Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Assistant Instructor: The explanation of “bringing oneself to completion” is grounded in “return.” This is beyond the reach of superficial understanding.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wei, Instructor: Wholehearted return and bringing oneself to completion were never two separate ways. This composition understands that, and its language is also rich and restrained. It should be included in the record to dispel widespread doubts.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: The wording is economical, yet the meaning is fully expressed.

Comment by Examiner Xu, Instructor: This deeply grasps the intent of the Commentary on the Images in elucidating the line statement.

To discuss depth of return and the absence of inward dissatisfaction is simply to discuss attaining centrality without depending upon anything external. Such is the intent of the Commentary on the Images of the Book of Changes. For return does not lie outside the virtue of centrality. If one now brings oneself to completion through this virtue, is this not depth of return with no inward dissatisfaction? Furthermore, the six in the fifth place of the hexagram Return is central and yielding and occupies the honored position. At the time of return, the Duke of Zhou appended to it the words “Wholehearted…”

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
復无悔之辭矣孔子象傳申之意謂二雖休復
未必其能敦也五則敦厚於復而善心渾乎其
恒存不困於心而衡於慮也尚何悔之内出乎
四雖獨復未必其能厚也五則篤厚於復而善
行慥乎其純篤不徵於色而發於聲也又何悔
之可憂乎其若是者豈有他哉亦惟中以自成
而已盖六五以柔順之爻得居中之道如不偏
不倚中之具於心者也向也内欲一萌有時而
或忘矣今則自成其中而復於既忘之後未甞
暫得而暫失焉無過不及中之見於行者也向
也外物一交有時而或失矣今則自考其中而
復於既失之餘未甞屢失而屢復焉善心自存
而中之體以立不假人以交脩也豈若二之下
仁而為休復者乎善行自篤而中之用以行不
資人以相輔也豈若四之從道而為獨復者乎
吁以得中之道而致自成之功此所以為敦復
之象无悔之道也傳象者舉爻辭而申之明矣
抑論之人受天地之中以生中本人之所固有
punctuated:
復无悔之辭矣。孔子象傳申之，意謂二雖休復，未必其能敦也；五則敦厚於復，而善心渾乎其恒存，不困於心而衡於慮也，尚何悔之内出乎？四雖獨復，未必其能厚也；五則篤厚於復，而善行慥乎其純篤，不徵於色而發於聲也，又何悔之可憂乎？其若是者，豈有他哉？亦惟中以自成而已。盖六五以柔順之爻，得居中之道，如不偏不倚，中之具於心者也。向也，内欲一萌，有時而或忘矣；今則自成其中，而復於既忘之後，未甞暫得而暫失焉。無過不及，中之見於行者也。向也，外物一交，有時而或失矣；今則自考其中，而復於既失之餘，未甞屢失而屢復焉。善心自存，而中之體以立，不假人以交脩也，豈若二之下仁而為休復者乎？善行自篤，而中之用以行，不資人以相輔也，豈若四之從道而為獨復者乎？吁！以得中之道，而致自成之功，此所以為敦復之象、无悔之道也。傳象者舉爻辭而申之，明矣。

抑論之，人受天地之中以生，中本人之所固有
translation_en:
…the words concerning return and freedom from regret. Confucius elaborates on them in the Commentary on the Images. His meaning is that although the second line represents an admirable return, it may not necessarily achieve steadfastness. The fifth, however, is steadfast in returning: its good heart remains whole and constantly present, without distress of heart or obstruction in thought. What regret could still arise within? Although the fourth line represents returning alone, it may not necessarily achieve depth. The fifth, however, is deeply committed to returning: its good conduct is assured in its purity and sincerity, without distress showing in the countenance or issuing in the voice. What regret could there be to fear? Is there any other reason for its being so? It is simply that it perfects itself through centrality.

The yielding and compliant line of Six in the Fifth attains the Way of occupying the center. Being neither partial nor inclined to either side is centrality present in the heart. Previously, whenever an inward desire arose, this centrality might sometimes be forgotten. Now, however, it perfects its own centrality and returns to it after forgetting it; it does not gain it momentarily only to lose it again. Being neither excessive nor deficient is centrality manifest in conduct. Previously, whenever it encountered external things, this centrality might sometimes be lost. Now, however, it examines its own centrality [?] and returns to it after losing it; it does not repeatedly lose it and repeatedly return to it.

Its good heart sustains itself, and thus the substance of centrality is established, without depending on others for mutual cultivation. How could it be like the second line, which achieves an admirable return by placing itself below one who is humane? Its good conduct grows steadfast of itself, and thus the functioning of centrality is realized, without relying on others for assistance. How could it be like the fourth line, which returns alone by following the Way? Ah! By attaining the Way of centrality, it accomplishes self-perfection. This is what constitutes the image of steadfast return and the way to freedom from regret. The author of the Commentary on the Images cites the line statement and elaborates on it: the meaning is clear.

To discuss this further: human beings receive the centrality of Heaven and Earth at birth; centrality is inherently theirs…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
也但有生之後氣稟拘之物欲蔽之聖賢而下
能復本然之中者幾何人哉六五之中雖或失
之而能復之不徒復之而能敦之其天資之美
不可誣也求之古人其成湯之改過不吝武王
之以義勝欲者歟
兼三才而兩之故易六畫而成卦分陰分
陽迭用柔剛故易六位而成章
王忠
同考試官訓導俞批人知六畫有三才
而不知六位亦有二才也此篇認理分明措辭
===
醇雅其深於易者歟
同考試官教諭魏批倍六畫分六位正
聖人作易順性命處塲中罕有得此意者發明
精切無踰此篇
考試官教諭姜批體認明白
考試官教諭徐批理到之言自別
聖人作易以順理有見於卦畫之重者有見於
爻位之分者盖聖人作易重之則為六畫分之
punctuated:
也。但有生之後，氣稟拘之，物欲蔽之，聖賢而下，能復本然之中者幾何人哉？六五之中，雖或失之，而能復之；不徒復之，而能敦之。其天資之美，不可誣也。求之古人，其成湯之改過不吝、武王之以義勝欲者歟？
兼三才而兩之，故易六畫而成卦；分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，故易六位而成章。
王忠
同考試官訓導俞批：人知六畫有三才，而不知六位亦有二才也。此篇認理分明，措辭醇雅，其深於易者歟？
同考試官教諭魏批：倍六畫，分六位，正聖人作易順性命處。塲中罕有得此意者，發明精切，無踰此篇。
考試官教諭姜批：體認明白。
考試官教諭徐批：理到之言，自別。
聖人作易以順理，有見於卦畫之重者，有見於爻位之分者。盖聖人作易，重之則為六畫，分之
translation_en:
…Yet after birth, people are constrained by their endowment of vital energy and obscured by material desires. Below the sages and worthies, how many can recover their original equilibrium? Though the equilibrium of the six in the fifth place may sometimes be lost, it can be recovered; and not merely recovered, but firmly established. The excellence of this natural endowment cannot be denied. Seeking examples among the ancients, might these be Cheng Tang, who did not hesitate to correct his faults, and King Wu, who used righteousness to overcome desire?
“Encompassing the Three Powers and doubling them, the Changes thus forms a hexagram with six lines. Distinguishing yin and yang and employing the yielding and the firm alternately, the Changes thus establishes its pattern through six positions.”
Wang Zhong
Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Assistant Instructor: People know that the six lines contain the Three Powers, but do not know that the six positions also contain the Two Powers [?]. This essay apprehends the principles clearly and expresses them in refined and elegant language. Is its author not deeply versed in the Changes?
Comment by Associate Examiner Wei, Instructor: Doubling the six lines [?] and distinguishing the six positions are precisely where the sages, in composing the Changes, accorded with human nature and destiny. Few in the examination hall have grasped this meaning. In precision and aptness of elucidation, no essay surpasses this one.
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: Clear understanding and apprehension.
Comment by Examiner Xu, Instructor: Words that fully comprehend the principles naturally stand apart.
In composing the Changes to accord with principle, the sages perceived something in the doubling of the trigram lines and something in the differentiation of the line positions. For when the sages composed the Changes, doubling produced six lines; differentiating them…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
則爲六位也然則卦爻之間何莫而非性命之
理哉昔吾夫子說卦論聖人作易以順性命之
理及此謂夫聖人之作易也既成三畫之卦巳
具三才之象由是因而重之兼三才而爲兩三
才引而伸之倍三畫而爲兩三畫以上二爻爲
天天道以兩而成象也以中二爻爲人人道以
兩而成德也以下二爻爲地地道以兩而成質
也是以一内一外而大成之卦以備有貞有悔
而全體之象以立豈非六畫而成卦乎然此特
===
統言之耳又細分之陰位半於陽陽位半於陰
而陰陽之中分剛位間於柔柔位間於剛而剛
柔之迭用五陽上陰天道相間而立於上矣三
仁四義人道相間而立於中矣初剛二柔地道
相間而立於下矣是以陰陽經緯燦然而可觀
剛柔間雜蔚然而可覩豈非六位而成章乎是
則卦之重者此三才也爻之分者此三才也聖
人作易以順性命之理豈不從可見哉大抵易
書不外乎卦爻而卦爻不外乎三才三才也者
punctuated: 則爲六位也。然則卦爻之間，何莫而非性命之理哉？昔吾夫子《說卦》論聖人作易以順性命之理，及此，謂夫聖人之作易也，既成三畫之卦，巳具三才之象。由是因而重之，兼三才而爲兩三才；引而伸之，倍三畫而爲兩三畫。以上二爻爲天，天道以兩而成象也；以中二爻爲人，人道以兩而成德也；以下二爻爲地，地道以兩而成質也。是以一内一外，而大成之卦以備；有貞有悔，而全體之象以立。豈非六畫而成卦乎？然此特統言之耳。又細分之，陰位半於陽，陽位半於陰，而陰陽之中分；剛位間於柔，柔位間於剛，而剛柔之迭用。五陽上陰，天道相間而立於上矣；三仁四義，人道相間而立於中矣；初剛二柔，地道相間而立於下矣。是以陰陽經緯，燦然而可觀；剛柔間雜，蔚然而可覩。豈非六位而成章乎？是則卦之重者，此三才也；爻之分者，此三才也。聖人作易以順性命之理，豈不從可見哉？大抵易書不外乎卦爻，而卦爻不外乎三才。三才也者，
translation_en:
…then there are six positions. Thus, among the hexagrams and their lines, what is not an expression of the principles of human nature and destiny? Formerly, our Master, in Explaining the Trigrams, discussed how the sages made the Changes to accord with the principles of human nature and destiny. When he reached this point, his meaning was that, in making the Changes, the sages had already embodied images of the Three Powers—Heaven, humanity, and Earth—once they had formed the three-line trigrams. They then proceeded to double these, combining the Three Powers into two sets of Three Powers; extending and developing them, they doubled the three lines into two sets of three lines. The upper two lines represent Heaven: the Way of Heaven forms its images through a pair. The middle two lines represent humanity: the Way of humanity fulfills its virtue through a pair. The lower two lines represent Earth: the Way of Earth forms its substance through a pair. Thus, with one inner and one outer trigram, the fully developed hexagram is complete; with the lower trigram, called zhen, and the upper trigram, called hui, the image of the whole is established. Is this not what is meant by six lines forming a hexagram? Yet this is only a general account.

To distinguish them more finely, yin positions constitute one half and yang positions the other, so that yin and yang are evenly divided. Firm positions alternate with yielding ones, and yielding positions with firm ones, so that firmness and yielding function in alternation. The fifth position is yang and the top position yin: the Way of Heaven is established above through their alternation. The third is benevolence and the fourth righteousness: the Way of humanity is established in the middle through their alternation. The first is firm and the second yielding: the Way of Earth is established below through their alternation. Thus yin and yang interweave, brilliantly visible; firmness and yielding intermingle, richly manifest. Is this not what is meant by six positions forming a pattern? Thus, what is embodied in the doubling of the trigrams is these Three Powers; what is embodied in the division of the line positions is likewise these Three Powers. Can we not see from this how the sages made the Changes to accord with the principles of human nature and destiny? Broadly speaking, the book of Changes encompasses nothing beyond hexagrams and lines, and hexagrams and lines encompass nothing beyond the Three Powers. As for the Three Powers, they are…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
形而上之理也卦爻也者形而下之器也理非
器不形器非理不立故聖人作易以有形之卦
爻而順无形之性命此易所以爲性命之源也
世之論者以卜筮而小吾易烏足與言易哉
書
在璿璣玉衡以齊七政
戴大賓
同考試官教諭李批七政自有常度察
璣衡以齊之恐曆法有差爾此作能知此意便
===
有此詞是宜錄之
同考試官學正王批觀象為授時計作
者不知以七政為在器之象殊戾本旨惟此篇
卓有定見且詞氣渾融誠璧經中之巨擘歟
考試官教諭姜批詞氣寛平必佳士也
考試官教諭徐批不戾經傳佳作
察象之在器者以合象之在天者此聖人之初
政也甚矣天象之難定也使不察器以合之其
何以爲曆象授時之計哉史臣記聖人之初政
punctuated:
形而上之理也，卦爻也者，形而下之器也。理非器不形，器非理不立。故聖人作易，以有形之卦爻而順无形之性命，此易所以爲性命之源也。世之論者以卜筮而小吾易，烏足與言易哉？

書
在璿璣玉衡，以齊七政。
戴大賓

同考試官教諭李批：「七政自有常度，察璣衡以齊之，恐曆法有差爾。此作能知此意，便有此詞，是宜錄之。」

同考試官學正王批：「觀象為授時計，作者不知，以七政為在器之象，殊戾本旨。惟此篇卓有定見，且詞氣渾融，誠璧經中之巨擘歟！」

考試官教諭姜批：「詞氣寛平，必佳士也。」

考試官教諭徐批：「不戾經傳，佳作。」

察象之在器者，以合象之在天者，此聖人之初政也。甚矣，天象之難定也！使不察器以合之，其何以爲曆象授時之計哉？史臣記聖人之初政
translation_en:
…are principles above the realm of physical form; the hexagrams and their lines are concrete configurations within that realm. Without concrete configurations, principles cannot become manifest; without principles, concrete configurations cannot be established. Thus, in composing the Changes, the sage used the visible hexagrams and lines to accord with invisible human nature and destiny. This is why the Changes is the source of understanding human nature and destiny. Those who belittle our Changes as merely a book of divination—how could they be fit to discuss it?

Book of Documents
“He examined the jade armillary instrument and jade sighting tube, to bring the seven celestial regulators into accord.”
Dai Dabin

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “The seven celestial regulators have their own constant measures. Examining the armillary instrument and sighting tube to bring them into accord was simply a precaution against errors in calendrical methods. This essay understands that meaning and therefore finds these words to express it. It deserves inclusion.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, School Instructor: “Observing celestial phenomena serves the purpose of determining and promulgating the seasons. Essay writers fail to understand this and take the seven celestial regulators to mean representations within the instrument, greatly contradicting the original purport. This essay alone displays a remarkably firm understanding; moreover, its language and tone form a harmonious whole. Truly it is an outstanding work among the essays on the ‘Jade Classic’ [?]!”

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “The language and tone are composed and even. The author must be an excellent scholar.”

Comment by Examiner Xu, Instructor: “It does not contradict the Classic or its commentaries. A fine composition.”

To examine the representations within the instrument so as to bring them into agreement with the phenomena in heaven: this was the sage’s first act of government. How very difficult it is to ascertain celestial phenomena! Without examining the instrument to bring them into agreement, how could one devise a means of calculating celestial movements, observing celestial phenomena, and promulgating the seasons? The court historian recorded the sage’s first act of government…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
如此盖謂為治莫先於治曆治曆莫要於觀象
彼璣之為噐以璿飾之其制則東西運轉所以
象天而載七政也衡之為管以玉為之其制則
南北低昂所以窺璣而齊七政也然歲久易湮
不能無差舜則精以察之竭心思於推歩之時
而象之或遲或速皆有以知其度數之詳世遠
易弛不能無異舜則明以審之竭目力於窺測
之際而象之或順或逆皆有以知其次舍之位
所以然者盖日月運行於天有遲有速今焉察
===
之噐以驗諸天其度數果合歟否歟必使上下
之間遲速為之一致也五星運行於天有順有
逆今焉審之璣以徵諸天其次舍果同歟異歟
必使上下之際順逆為之不爽也高遠難知者
即諸噐而可知法制易見者驗諸天而益合夫
然則天時以定曆法以審人時不於此而授哉
舜之急先務有如此夫大抵天下之政未有重
於人時者苟曆法不定則時有不正四時一失
萬事俱爽尚何以撫五辰而成天下之治哉故
punctuated: 如此。盖謂為治莫先於治曆，治曆莫要於觀象。彼璣之為噐，以璿飾之，其制則東西運轉，所以象天而載七政也；衡之為管，以玉為之，其制則南北低昂，所以窺璣而齊七政也。然歲久易湮，不能無差，舜則精以察之，竭心思於推歩之時，而象之或遲或速，皆有以知其度數之詳；世遠易弛，不能無異，舜則明以審之，竭目力於窺測之際，而象之或順或逆，皆有以知其次舍之位。所以然者，盖日月運行於天，有遲有速，今焉察之噐以驗諸天，其度數果合歟否歟？必使上下之間，遲速為之一致也。五星運行於天，有順有逆，今焉審之璣以徵諸天，其次舍果同歟異歟？必使上下之際，順逆為之不爽也。高遠難知者，即諸噐而可知；法制易見者，驗諸天而益合。夫然則天時以定，曆法以審，人時不於此而授哉？舜之急先務有如此夫！大抵天下之政，未有重於人時者。苟曆法不定，則時有不正，四時一失，萬事俱爽，尚何以撫五辰而成天下之治哉？故
translation_en:
…in this way. The meaning is that, in governing, nothing takes precedence over regulating the calendar, and in regulating the calendar, nothing is more essential than observing the celestial configurations. The revolving instrument, the ji, is ornamented with fine jade; its construction allows it to rotate east and west, thereby representing the heavens and bearing representations of the seven celestial bodies—the sun, moon, and five planets. The sighting tube, the heng, is made of jade; its construction allows it to be lowered and raised north and south, thereby permitting observations through the ji and bringing the seven celestial bodies into alignment.

Yet over many years knowledge readily becomes obscured, and discrepancies inevitably arise. Shun therefore examined these matters with precision, applying his mind to the utmost when calculating celestial motions, so that, whether the configurations moved slowly or swiftly, he could ascertain their angular measurements in detail. As generations pass, practices readily grow lax, and divergences inevitably arise. Shun therefore scrutinized these matters discerningly, exerting his eyesight to the utmost when making observations and measurements, so that, whether the configurations moved directly or retrogressively, he could ascertain their positions in the celestial stations.

The reason was this: the sun and moon move through the heavens at varying speeds. By examining them now in the instrument and checking the results against the heavens, could one establish whether their angular measurements actually agreed? Their slower and faster motions above and below had to be brought into complete correspondence. The five planets move through the heavens both directly and retrogressively. By scrutinizing them now in the ji and verifying the results against the heavens, could one establish whether their celestial stations were identical or different? Their direct and retrograde motions above and below had to correspond without discrepancy. What was lofty, remote, and difficult to know could be known by recourse to the instrument; the readily visible rules embodied in its construction could be checked against the heavens and brought into still closer agreement. Thus celestial seasons were determined and calendrical methods verified: was this not the basis for announcing to the people the times for their work? Such was Shun’s urgency in attending to the foremost task!

In general, among all the affairs of government under Heaven, none is more important than the proper timing of the people’s work. If calendrical methods are not settled, the reckoning of the seasons will be incorrect. Once the four seasons are misreckoned, all affairs go awry. How then could one regulate the five seasonal markers and bring good order to all under Heaven? Therefore…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
堯即位而曆象授時舜攝位而察器齊政皆此
意也噫庶績咸熙無為而治良有以哉有天下
者其致意焉
六卿分職各率其屬以倡九牧阜成兆民
六年五服一朝又六年王乃時巡考制度
于四岳諸侯各朝于方岳大明黜陟
黃肯堂
同考試官教諭李批此題作者類多以
體統保治立說殊戾本旨是篇認理明白而文
===
足以發之蓋究心于經學者允宜錄出
同考試官學正王批此篇約繁就簡寫
出成王訓迪百官之意前後相貫文采爛然錄
之以範來學
考試官教諭姜批周官內外相維意
政如此
考試官教諭徐批發明訓迪建官體
統處甚是
賢王訓迪建官之體統在內者有其要在外者
punctuated:
堯即位而曆象授時，舜攝位而察器齊政，皆此意也。噫！庶績咸熙，無為而治，良有以哉！有天下者，其致意焉。
「六卿分職，各率其屬，以倡九牧，阜成兆民。六年，五服一朝；又六年，王乃時巡，考制度于四岳。諸侯各朝于方岳，大明黜陟。」
黃肯堂
同考試官教諭李批：此題作者類多以體統保治立說，殊戾本旨。是篇認理明白，而文足以發之，蓋究心于經學者，允宜錄出。
同考試官學正王批：此篇約繁就簡，寫出成王訓迪百官之意，前後相貫，文采爛然，錄之以範來學。
考試官教諭姜批：周官內外相維意，政如此。
考試官教諭徐批：發明訓迪建官體統處甚是。
賢王訓迪建官之體統，在內者有其要，在外者
translation_en:
…When Yao ascended the throne, he calculated and observed the celestial phenomena and imparted the seasons to the people; when Shun assumed the regency, he examined the astronomical instruments and brought the celestial movements into accord. Both acted with this intention. Ah! There was indeed good reason why all undertakings flourished and order prevailed without exertion! Let those who possess the realm give this their attention.
“The six ministers divide their duties, each leading his subordinates to set an example for the nine regional governors and to enrich and perfect the myriad people. Every six years, those of the five zones of submission attend court once. After another six years, the king makes a tour of inspection in the appropriate seasons, examining institutions and standards at the Four Sacred Peaks. The feudal lords each attend him at the sacred peak of their region, and he makes demotions and promotions fully manifest.”
Huang Kentang.
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: Most writers on this topic base their arguments on maintaining order through the hierarchy of authority, seriously departing from its original meaning. This essay understands the underlying principle clearly, and its writing adequately brings that principle out. Its author has evidently devoted himself to the study of the Classics; it certainly deserves to be included.
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: This essay condenses complexity into simplicity, bringing out King Cheng’s intention in instructing and guiding the hundred officials. Its beginning and end are connected, and its literary brilliance shines forth. It is included as a model for future students.
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: The idea in “The Officers of Zhou,” that officials at court and in the regions mutually sustain one another, is precisely this [?].
Comment by Examiner Xu, Instructor: The passage elucidating instruction and guidance concerning the hierarchy of appointed offices is very sound.
The worthy king gave instruction and guidance concerning the hierarchy of appointed offices: for those at court there were essential principles; for those in the regions …

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
有其法盖率屬圖治之要朝巡考課之法六卿
諸侯所當知者也成王各訓迪之有以哉昔成
王訓官之意謂夫致治莫要於建官建官莫先
於體統但內外不同體統亦異自六卿言之內
則統領乎群工外則管攝乎州牧彼曰治曰教
曰禮既各分其職矣必率其屬以為九牧之倡
使皆率屬以趨事焉曰政曰禁曰土既各分其
任矣必統其屬以為九牧之先使皆統屬以赴
工焉自內達外政治脩明而兆民之衆莫不歸
===
於阜厚也由近及遠教化浹洽而黎庶之繁莫
不底於化成也如此則六卿之體統立矣自諸
侯言之定以六年五服一朝會于京師又歷六
年王者乃時巡于四岳凡治也教也禮也悉有
以考其廢興而諸侯各朝于方岳之下凡政也
政也土也咸有以稽其脩否而諸侯各覲于方
岳之前其有不職者則罰以懲之而大明其黜
之之法其有脩職者則賞以勸之而大明其陟
之之典如此則諸侯之體統立矣吁六卿治內
punctuated: 有其法。盖率屬圖治之要、朝巡考課之法，六卿諸侯所當知者也。成王各訓迪之，有以哉！昔成王訓官之意，謂夫致治莫要於建官，建官莫先於體統。但內外不同，體統亦異。自六卿言之，內則統領乎群工，外則管攝乎州牧。彼曰治、曰教、曰禮，既各分其職矣，必率其屬以為九牧之倡，使皆率屬以趨事焉；曰政、曰禁、曰土，既各分其任矣，必統其屬以為九牧之先，使皆統屬以赴工焉。自內達外，政治脩明，而兆民之衆莫不歸於阜厚也；由近及遠，教化浹洽，而黎庶之繁莫不底於化成也。如此，則六卿之體統立矣。自諸侯言之，定以六年五服一朝，會于京師；又歷六年，王者乃時巡于四岳。凡治也、教也、禮也，悉有以考其廢興，而諸侯各朝于方岳之下；凡政也、政也、土也，咸有以稽其脩否，而諸侯各覲于方岳之前。其有不職者，則罰以懲之，而大明其黜之之法；其有脩職者，則賞以勸之，而大明其陟之之典。如此，則諸侯之體統立矣。吁！六卿治內
translation_en:
…has its prescribed rules. The essentials of leading subordinates in pursuit of good government, and the rules for court audiences, royal inspection tours, and assessments of performance, are what the six ministers and the regional lords ought to know. King Cheng had good reason to instruct and guide each of them!

The intent of King Cheng’s instruction to officials was that nothing is more essential to achieving good government than establishing offices, and nothing takes precedence in establishing offices over the ordering of authority. Yet the court and the regions differ, and so do their respective hierarchies. As for the six ministers, within the court they command the various officials; beyond it they oversee the provincial governors. Those responsible for administration, education, and rites each have their distinct duties. They must lead their subordinates and set an example for the governors of the nine provinces, so that all these governors lead their own subordinates in attending to their tasks. Those responsible for governance, prohibitions, and lands each have their distinct responsibilities. They must command their subordinates and take the lead for the nine provincial governors, so that all these governors command their own subordinates in undertaking their work. Extending from the court to the regions, government becomes well ordered and enlightened, and all the multitudes of the people attain prosperity. Spreading from near to far, moral instruction permeates everywhere, and the entire populace achieves moral transformation. Thus the hierarchy of the six ministers is established.

As for the regional lords, it is stipulated that those of the five service zones attend court once every six years, assembling at the capital. After another six years, the king makes inspection tours at the appropriate seasons to the Four Sacred Peaks. In administration, education, and rites, there are means to examine what has fallen into neglect and what has flourished, and the regional lords each attend an audience at the foot of the sacred peak of their region. In governance, governance [?], and lands, there are means to assess whether duties have been properly performed, and the regional lords each appear before the king at their regional sacred peak. Those who fail in their duties are punished to correct them, making fully manifest the rules for their demotion. Those who fulfill their duties are rewarded to encourage them, making fully manifest the regulations for their promotion. Thus the hierarchy of the regional lords is established. Ah! The six ministers govern within the court…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
諸侯治外内外相承體統不紊制治保邦之道
孰有要于此哉成王其善于訓官者矣嗟夫為
政固當任人又當任法唐虞之時二十二人之
咨任人也三載九載之制任法也故當時庶績
咸熈萬國咸寧固由于建官之得人實由于人
法之並任成王訓廸建官體統而有及于考課
之法亦此意也世稱泰和之治者必曰虞周其
以是歟
詩
===
豈敢定居一月三捷
陳良山
同考試官教諭杜批筆力老健說理詳
明周王以義遣戍之意宛然在目佳作也
同考試官教諭羅批周王遣戍何等精
神氣燄此作摸寫得出豈胸中有幾萬甲兵者
耶
考試官教諭姜批得周人風諭戍卒
之意讀之令人勃勃生氣得士如此吾豈憂戎
punctuated:
諸侯治外，内外相承，體統不紊，制治保邦之道，孰有要于此哉？成王其善于訓官者矣！嗟夫！為政固當任人，又當任法。唐虞之時，二十二人之咨，任人也；三載九載之制，任法也。故當時庶績咸熈，萬國咸寧，固由于建官之得人，實由于人法之並任。成王訓廸建官體統，而有及于考課之法，亦此意也。世稱泰和之治者，必曰虞周，其以是歟？
詩
豈敢定居？一月三捷。
陳良山
同考試官教諭杜批：筆力老健，說理詳明，周王以義遣戍之意，宛然在目，佳作也。
同考試官教諭羅批：周王遣戍，何等精神氣燄！此作摸寫得出，豈胸中有幾萬甲兵者耶？
考試官教諭姜批：得周人風諭戍卒之意，讀之令人勃勃生氣。得士如此，吾豈憂戎
translation_en:
…the regional lords govern outside. Those within and those without support one another, and the hierarchy remains orderly. Among the means of establishing good government and safeguarding the realm, what could be more essential than this? King Cheng was indeed skilled in instructing his officials! Ah! In governing, one must certainly rely on people, but one must also rely on institutional rules. In the time of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, consulting the twenty-two men exemplified reliance on people; the system of three-year and nine-year assessments exemplified reliance on rules. Thus, all undertakings flourished and the myriad states enjoyed peace. This certainly owed much to finding the right people when establishing offices, but its true basis was reliance on both people and rules. King Cheng's instruction concerning the hierarchy of established offices also extended to the procedures for assessing officials’ performance: his intention was the same. Whenever people speak of government that achieved supreme harmony, they invariably cite Yu and Zhou. Is this not the reason?
Book of Odes
“How dare we remain settled? Three victories in a single month.”
Chen Liangshan
Comment by Associate Examiner Du, Instructor: The writing is seasoned and vigorous, and the reasoning detailed and clear. The Zhou king’s intention in dispatching troops for garrison duty in accordance with righteousness appears vividly before our eyes. An excellent composition.
Comment by Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor: What spirit and martial ardor the Zhou king displayed in dispatching the garrison troops! This composition succeeds in portraying them. Could its author be someone who holds tens of thousands of armored soldiers within his breast?
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: It captures the Zhou people’s intention in indirectly exhorting the garrison soldiers. Reading it fills one with vigorous spirit. Having obtained men of such caliber, why should I fear warfare…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
九重無北顧之憂也兵威遠振于邊庭而戎馬
無南牧之患也夫如是則多難以紓戌事以定
中國豈有不尊疆圉豈有不靖者哉周王歌此
於遣戍之日其真得鼓舞激勸之道也歟大抵
兵事以哀敬爲本而所尚則威此章之一月三
捷作其奮揚之威也下章之豈不日戒動其戒
懼之心也敬勇相資並行不悖此行師之要御
戎之道也嚴尤頗謂周得中策然則如何而爲
策之上書曰明王慎德四夷咸賓策之上者其
===
在茲耶
卬盛于豆于豆于登其香始升上帝居歆
黃鞏
同考試官教諭杜 批 周人奉祭格天之
意類能言之而詞氣舂容親切有味者僅見此
篇
同考試官教諭羅 批 能以配饗意貫講
且詞氣溫純典則要非初學可到
考試官教諭姜 批 詞氣溫柔敦厚蓋
punctuated:
九重無北顧之憂也，兵威遠振于邊庭，而戎馬無南牧之患也。夫如是，則多難以紓，戌事以定，中國豈有不尊、疆圉豈有不靖者哉？周王歌此於遣戍之日，其真得鼓舞激勸之道也歟！大抵兵事以哀敬爲本，而所尚則威。此章之「一月三捷」，作其奮揚之威也；下章之「豈不日戒」，動其戒懼之心也。敬勇相資，並行不悖，此行師之要、御戎之道也。嚴尤頗謂周得中策，然則如何而爲策之上？《書》曰：「明王慎德，四夷咸賓。」策之上者，其在茲耶？
卬盛于豆，于豆于登，其香始升，上帝居歆。
黃鞏
同考試官教諭杜批：周人奉祭格天之意，類能言之，而詞氣舂容、親切有味者，僅見此篇。
同考試官教諭羅批：能以配饗意貫講，且詞氣溫純典則，要非初學可到。
考試官教諭姜批：詞氣溫柔敦厚，蓋
translation_en:
…the imperial palace has no anxiety about the north; military might resounds far across the frontier, and there is no danger of enemy cavalry coming south to pasture. With this, the many troubles can be relieved and garrison affairs settled. How could the Central Kingdom fail to command respect, or its borders fail to be tranquil? When the king of Zhou sang this on the day he dispatched the garrison troops, had he not truly grasped the way to inspire and encourage them? In general, military affairs rest upon compassion and reverent care, while what they prize is might. This stanza’s “three victories in one month” rouses their vigorous martial might; the next stanza’s “How could we fail to be on guard each day?” stirs their vigilance and apprehension. Reverent care and courage sustain one another and proceed together without conflict: this is the essential principle of conducting an army and the way to resist the Rong. Yan You held that Zhou had attained the middle strategy. What, then, would constitute the highest strategy? The Book of Documents says: “When an enlightened king attends carefully to his virtue, the barbarians of the four quarters all come as guests.” Does not the highest strategy lie in this?
“I fill the wooden offering vessels, the wooden vessels and the earthenware vessels. Their fragrance begins to rise, and the Lord on High accepts and enjoys it.”
Huang Gong
Associate Examiner Du, Instructor, comments: Most can articulate the Zhou people’s intent in presenting sacrifices to reach Heaven, but this is the only essay I have seen whose language and tone are ample and unhurried, intimate and rich in meaning.
Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: He sustains his exposition throughout with the idea of the ancestor sharing in the sacrificial offerings to Heaven. Moreover, his language and tone are gentle, pure, and in accord with classical standards. This is certainly beyond a beginner’s reach.
Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: The language and tone are gentle and kind, sincere and generous. Surely…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
有得於詩者也
考試官教諭徐批典則
祀禮方行而天心遂格周人尊祖配天然也盖
奉祭莫難於格天也周人郊祀方行而格天之
速如此其亦有由然哉昔周公制禮尊后稷以
配天此則言其奉祭之事也謂夫我祖后稷克
配彼天今而尊事于南郊實能感孚乎上帝是
故祭必有豆所以薦菹醢也我則以菹醢而盛
之于豆祭必有登所以薦太羹也我則以太羹
===
而盛之于登或肆焉或將焉菹醢之芳臭始升
而圭璧未之或薦也以享焉以祀焉太羹之馨
香始達而歌樂未之或奏也斯時也感之遂通
而皇矣上帝居然其来歆假之即應而倬彼昊
天安然其来饗鑒精禋於冲漠之表盖與后稷
而相為陟降也曾謂高高在上而不吾應乎歆
祀事於對越之頃盖與后稷而相為上下也曾
謂蕩蕩難忱而莫予格乎夫莫大於郊也而薦
之之禮甚簡莫尊於帝也而饗之之應甚速是
punctuated:
有得於詩者也。
考試官教諭徐批：典則。
祀禮方行，而天心遂格，周人尊祖配天，然也。盖奉祭莫難於格天也。周人郊祀方行，而格天之速如此，其亦有由然哉！昔周公制禮，尊后稷以配天，此則言其奉祭之事也。謂夫我祖后稷，克配彼天，今而尊事于南郊，實能感孚乎上帝。是故祭必有豆，所以薦菹醢也；我則以菹醢而盛之于豆。祭必有登，所以薦太羹也；我則以太羹而盛之于登。或肆焉，或將焉，菹醢之芳臭始升，而圭璧未之或薦也；以享焉，以祀焉，太羹之馨香始達，而歌樂未之或奏也。斯時也，感之遂通，而皇矣上帝居然其来歆；假之即應，而倬彼昊天安然其来饗。鑒精禋於冲漠之表，盖與后稷而相為陟降也，曾謂高高在上而不吾應乎？歆祀事於對越之頃，盖與后稷而相為上下也，曾謂蕩蕩難忱而莫予格乎？夫莫大於郊也，而薦之之禮甚簡；莫尊於帝也，而饗之之應甚速。是
translation_en:
…one who has gained an understanding of the Poetry.
Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “Elegant and in accord with the canons.”
The sacrificial rites had only just begun, yet Heaven’s heart was already moved: this was because the people of Zhou honored their ancestor by associating him with Heaven in sacrifice. In offering sacrifice, nothing is harder than moving Heaven. Yet the Zhou suburban sacrifice had barely begun when Heaven was moved so swiftly. Surely there was a reason for this! Formerly, when the Duke of Zhou established the rites, he honored Hou Ji by associating him with Heaven in sacrifice. This passage speaks of the conduct of that sacrifice. It means: Our ancestor Hou Ji was worthy to be associated with Heaven. Now, in reverently serving him at the southern suburban altar, we can truly move the Lord on High and win his trust. Thus, sacrifices must have dou vessels, in which to present pickled vegetables and meat pastes; we fill those vessels with pickled vegetables and meat pastes. Sacrifices must have deng vessels, in which to present the plain broth; we fill those vessels with plain broth. As the offerings are set out and presented, the fragrance of the pickled vegetables and meat pastes has only just risen, and the jade tablets and disks have not yet been offered. As the offerings are made and the sacrifice performed, the aroma of the plain broth has only just reached its destination, and the songs and music have not yet been performed. At this moment, the appeal immediately reaches its object, and the august Lord on High assuredly comes to savor the offerings; the approach immediately elicits a response, and that resplendent vast Heaven serenely comes to enjoy them. Beyond the realm of silent emptiness, he beholds the pure sacrifice, ascending and descending together with Hou Ji. Could one really say that he remains high above and does not respond to us? At the very moment we stand reverently before him, he savors the sacrificial service, moving above and below together with Hou Ji. Could one really say that he is so vast and difficult to trust that he will not come to us? No sacrifice is greater than the suburban sacrifice, yet the rites for presenting its offerings are exceedingly simple. None is more exalted than the Lord on High, yet his response in accepting the offerings is exceedingly swift. This…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
蓋后稷之克饗天心之有素焉耳豈但芳臭之
薦信得其時哉雖然南郊祭天既配之以后稷
矣而明堂享帝則又配之以文王焉蓋封國之
受始於后稷而王業之成由於文王以稷配天
所以尊稷也倣乎古也以文王配帝所以親文
王也以義起也尊尊親親兩盡其道此禮文之
所以備也此天心之所以格也此有周所以為
有道之長也
春秋
===
州公如曹桓公五年公會宰周公齊侯宋子
衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯于葵丘僖公九年
張天顯
同考試官教諭周批題有明傳作者率
欠融會冗碎厭觀此作能悉傳意而文理自然
接續属比之教得之深矣
考試官教諭姜批理明詞健
考試官教諭徐批謹嚴
諸侯假朝禮春秋原所稱而錄其本宰臣與會
punctuated:
蓋后稷之克饗天心之有素焉耳，豈但芳臭之薦信得其時哉？雖然，南郊祭天既配之以后稷矣，而明堂享帝則又配之以文王焉。蓋封國之受始於后稷，而王業之成由於文王。以稷配天，所以尊稷也，倣乎古也；以文王配帝，所以親文王也，以義起也。尊尊親親，兩盡其道，此禮文之所以備也，此天心之所以格也，此有周所以為有道之長也。

春秋

州公如曹，桓公五年。公會宰周公、齊侯、宋子、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯于葵丘，僖公九年。

張天顯

同考試官教諭周批：題有明傳，作者率欠融會，冗碎厭觀。此作能悉傳意，而文理自然接續，属比之教得之深矣。

考試官教諭姜批：理明詞健。

考試官教諭徐批：謹嚴。

諸侯假朝禮，春秋原所稱而錄其本；宰臣與會
translation_en:
…surely because Hou Ji had long been able to win acceptance in Heaven’s heart. How could it merely be that the fragrant offerings were indeed presented at the proper time? Nevertheless, while Hou Ji was associated with Heaven in the sacrifice at the southern suburb, King Wen was also associated with the Lord on High in the offering at the Hall of Light. For the receipt of an enfeoffed domain began with Hou Ji, whereas the completion of the royal enterprise came through King Wen. Associating Hou Ji with Heaven honored Hou Ji and followed antiquity; associating King Wen with the Lord on High expressed familial affection for King Wen and was instituted on grounds of righteousness. By fully observing both the honoring of the honored and affection for one’s kin, the forms of ritual were made complete, Heaven’s heart was moved, and Zhou became foremost among those possessing the Way.

Spring and Autumn Annals

“The Duke of Zhou 州 went to Cao.” Fifth year of Duke Huan.
“The duke met with the Grand Steward, the Duke of Zhou 周, the Marquis of Qi, the Viscount of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao at Kuiqiu.” Ninth year of Duke Xi.

Zhang Tianxian

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “The topics have clear explanations in the commentary, yet writers generally fail to integrate them, producing tedious, fragmented accounts that weary the reader. This essay fully comprehends the commentary’s meaning, and its reasoning flows naturally and continuously. It has deeply grasped the teaching concerning the arrangement and comparison of events.”

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “Clear reasoning and vigorous language.”

Comment by Examiner Xu, Instructor: “Careful and rigorous.”
