title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
禮春秋隆所稱而正其分盖諸侯莫貴於稱公
而國宜常守宰臣莫貴於兼秩而分非常尊春
秋得不於州寔宰孔而兩致其意哉昔者河内
州寔度國多難棄彼郊畿之地躬脩如曹之禮
論其爵則諸侯也論其如則外事也春秋胡為
進秩稱公而又録其所往耶盖聞公也以賢入
相而以相出守是昔為師保之臣今居藩翰之
職無異乎衛武之入相于周畢高之保釐東土
矣何乃履滿弗戒而圖國無良執德不恒而依
人是賴今日假禮於曹明日資餼於魯是固曹
之過賓而我之寓公也淳于城陽之墟豈州公
所有乎經故書公以隆其稱又書如曹者將有
其末先録其本為爵尊而居正之戒若夫周有
宰孔為王輔臣奉賜胙之命與葵丘之會其在
朝則冢卿也其出會則貴賓也春秋胡為加秩
書公而不殊會耶盖聞公也累官大宰而兼任
三公是上焉兼乎師保而下焉行乎端揆無異
乎大禹之宅百揆周公之出正百工矣然□
punctuated: 禮，春秋隆所稱而正其分。盖諸侯莫貴於稱公，而國宜常守；宰臣莫貴於兼秩，而分非常尊。春秋得不於州寔、宰孔而兩致其意哉？昔者河内州寔，度國多難，棄彼郊畿之地，躬脩如曹之禮。論其爵，則諸侯也；論其如，則外事也。春秋胡為進秩稱公，而又録其所往耶？盖聞公也，以賢入相，而以相出守，是昔為師保之臣，今居藩翰之職，無異乎衛武之入相于周、畢高之保釐東土矣。何乃履滿弗戒，而圖國無良；執德不恒，而依人是賴？今日假禮於曹，明日資餼於魯，是固曹之過賓，而我之寓公也。淳于城陽之墟，豈州公所有乎？經故書公以隆其稱，又書如曹者，將有其末，先録其本，為爵尊而居正之戒。若夫周有宰孔，為王輔臣，奉賜胙之命，與葵丘之會。其在朝，則冢卿也；其出會，則貴賓也。春秋胡為加秩書公，而不殊會耶？盖聞公也，累官大宰，而兼任三公，是上焉兼乎師保，而下焉行乎端揆，無異乎大禹之宅百揆、周公之出正百工矣。然□
translation_en:
…ritual: the Spring and Autumn Annals elevates the designation accorded him while setting his proper standing aright. Among the feudal lords, no designation is more honorable than “duke,” yet each ought always to preserve his state. Among chief ministers, nothing is more honorable than holding concurrent ranks, yet their standing does not entitle them to exceptional precedence. How could the Spring and Autumn Annals fail to convey both intentions through Zhou Shi and Zai Kong?

Formerly, Zhou Shi of Henei, judging his state to be beset by troubles, abandoned its suburban and capital lands and personally performed the formalities of a visit to Cao. In rank, he was a feudal lord; his visit was an affair of external relations. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals advance his rank by calling him “duke,” while also recording where he went? We have heard that this duke entered service as chief minister because of his worthiness, and then left that position to govern a territory. Thus, formerly a minister serving as preceptor and guardian, he now held office as a bulwark of the realm. He was no different from Duke Wu of Wei entering service as chief minister to Zhou, or Bi Gao protecting and administering the eastern lands. Why, then, did he occupy so exalted a position without caution, devising no sound plans for his state? Why did he fail to remain constant in virtue and instead rely upon others? Today he sought the courtesies of hospitality in Cao; tomorrow he depended upon provisions from Lu. He was indeed a passing guest in Cao and a displaced lord residing in our state of Lu. Were the old sites of Chunyu and Chengyang really still possessions of the Duke of Zhou? The Classic therefore writes “duke” to honor his designation, yet also records that he “went to Cao”: before recording the eventual outcome, it first records its beginnings. This offers an admonition that those exalted in rank should remain in their proper place.

As for Zai Kong of Zhou, he was a minister assisting the king. Charged with conveying the royal gift of sacrificial meat, he attended the meeting at Kuiqiu. At court he was the chief minister; when attending the meeting abroad, he was an honored guest. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals enhance his rank by writing “duke,” yet not distinguish his participation in the meeting from that of the others? We have heard that this duke rose through successive offices to become Grand Steward, concurrently holding office among the Three Dukes. Thus, above, he combined the responsibilities of preceptor and guardian; below, he carried out the duties of chief minister. He was no different from Yu the Great presiding over the hundred officers, or the Duke of Zhou going forth to direct the hundred officials. Yet [illegible]…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
儋爵受禄則莫非王臣宅中居外皆侯于周服
分有均勞之義貴非常尊之比是宜諸侯莫先
而王人同序也儲君殊會之禮豈宰臣敢當乎
經故書宰兼公以隆其稱而不殊會者謹夫臣
禮正夫大分焉爵尊而居下之勸吁觀春秋尊
州寔而不沒其如曹則知尊爵可貴而君道難
觀春秋隆宰孔而不待以殊會則知尊爵可兼
而臣道卑書曰惟德是輔有國者明此必知所
難而保其尊易曰黃裳元吉相國者明此必知
===
所卑而永無咎如曹之事葵丘之會豈惟讀經
者所當知
公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯
于鹹〔僖公十三年〕諸侯城緣陵〔僖公十四年〕
陳塤
同考試官教諭周批緣陵功罪所以異
於城邢封衛處學者多欠區別此作據經組傳
說盡齊桓得失如權衡稱物錙銖不爽殆知春
秋家法者
punctuated:
儋爵受禄，則莫非王臣；宅中居外，皆侯于周服。分有均勞之義，貴非常尊之比。是宜諸侯莫先，而王人同序也。儲君殊會之禮，豈宰臣敢當乎？經故書宰兼公以隆其稱，而不殊會者，謹夫臣禮，正夫大分焉，爵尊而居下之勸。吁！觀《春秋》尊州寔而不沒其如曹，則知尊爵可貴而君道難；觀《春秋》隆宰孔而不待以殊會，則知尊爵可兼而臣道卑。《書》曰：「惟德是輔。」有國者明此，必知所難而保其尊。《易》曰：「黃裳元吉。」相國者明此，必知所卑而永無咎。如曹之事、葵丘之會，豈惟讀經者所當知？
公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯于鹹。〔僖公十三年〕諸侯城緣陵。〔僖公十四年〕
陳塤
同考試官教諭周批：緣陵功罪所以異於城邢封衛處，學者多欠區別。此作據經組傳，說盡齊桓得失，如權衡稱物，錙銖不爽，殆知《春秋》家法者。
translation_en:
…In bearing rank and receiving emoluments, none is other than the king’s subject; whether residing at the center or stationed beyond it, all serve Zhou. Their assigned duties entail sharing the burdens of service, and their eminence is not comparable to an enduring sovereign dignity. Thus it is fitting that no feudal lord should precede him, yet that he should be listed together with the king’s representatives. How could a minister dare claim the ceremonial distinction accorded to the heir apparent, whose participation in a meeting is recorded separately? The Classic therefore writes both “minister” and “duke” to exalt his designation, but does not record his participation separately: this safeguards the ritual obligations of a subject and rectifies the fundamental distinction of status. It encourages those of exalted rank to occupy a subordinate position.
Ah! Observing that the Spring and Autumn Annals honors Zhou Shi without suppressing his journey to Cao, we understand that exalted rank is worthy of esteem, but that the ruler’s way is difficult. Observing that the Spring and Autumn Annals exalts Minister Kong without according him a separate entry for his participation in the meeting, we understand that exalted rank may be held concurrently with other office, but that the subject’s way is one of humility. The Book of Documents says, “It is virtue alone that is aided.” Rulers of states who understand this will surely recognize the difficulties of their position and preserve their dignity. The Book of Changes says, “A yellow lower garment: supreme good fortune.” Ministers assisting a state who understand this will surely recognize the humility their position requires and remain forever free of blame. Are the journey to Cao and the meeting at Kuiqiu matters that only readers of the Classic ought to understand?
“The duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao at Xian.” 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Xi.〕 “The feudal lords fortified Yuanling.” 〔Fourteenth year of Duke Xi.〕
Chen Xun.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Students often fail to distinguish why the merits and faults of the undertaking at Yuanling differ from those of fortifying Xing and reestablishing Wei. This essay bases itself on the Classic and weaves together the commentaries [?], fully explaining Duke Huan of Qi’s successes and failures. Like a balance weighing objects, it is accurate to the smallest fraction. Its author surely understands the interpretive discipline of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭姜批文有抑揚可嘉
考試官教諭徐批得貴王賤伯之旨
霸主恤小而失於專春秋異詞以譏其專此緣
陵之諸侯所以前目後凡而不序春秋貴王賤
霸之意見矣嘅昔蠢爾淮夷敢萌窺伺之志蕞
爾杞國日受侵逼之危經斯世者所宜慮也于
時齊桓主霸憂于厥心控大扶小首定于鹹之
議量功命日遂建緣陵之城徙其朝市于以去
危而即安移其人民于以就利而避害侁夏肄
===
之五廟不底于丘墟杞國之四民得免於塗炭
內安外攘桓之功可少哉常情觀此宜若深合
於城邢之恤患而遠邁乎楚丘之專封矣君子
則曰救災恤隣固為霸者之功築邑遷國必須
天子之命使桓於是時稟命於周室監之以王
卿則事功或半於他役而道義無歉於吾心雖
南仲之城朔方仲山甫之城東方不是過也夫
何築之登登齊築之也命不請於王朝往哉生
生齊遷之也事不聞於天子為力固勤事則專
punctuated:
考試官教諭姜批：文有抑揚，可嘉。
考試官教諭徐批：得貴王賤伯之旨。
霸主恤小而失於專，春秋異詞以譏其專。此緣陵之諸侯所以前目後凡而不序，春秋貴王賤霸之意見矣。嘅昔蠢爾淮夷，敢萌窺伺之志；蕞爾杞國，日受侵逼之危。經斯世者所宜慮也。于時齊桓主霸，憂于厥心，控大扶小，首定于鹹之議，量功命日，遂建緣陵之城。徙其朝市，于以去危而即安；移其人民，于以就利而避害。侁夏肄之五廟不底于丘墟，杞國之四民得免於塗炭。內安外攘，桓之功可少哉？常情觀此，宜若深合於城邢之恤患，而遠邁乎楚丘之專封矣。君子則曰：救災恤隣，固為霸者之功；築邑遷國，必須天子之命。使桓於是時稟命於周室，監之以王卿，則事功或半於他役，而道義無歉於吾心。雖南仲之城朔方、仲山甫之城東方，不是過也。夫何築之登登，齊築之也，命不請於王朝；往哉生生，齊遷之也，事不聞於天子。為力固勤，事則專
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: The essay is commendable for its modulations of praise and blame.

Comment by Examiner Xu, Instructor: It grasps the principle of honoring the king and holding the hegemon in lesser esteem.

The hegemon showed solicitude for a small state but erred in acting on his own authority. The Spring and Autumn Annals varies its wording to censure that presumption. This is why the lords involved at Yuanling are individually named in the earlier entry but collectively designated, without an ordered listing, in the later one. Here the Annals’ intent to honor the king and hold the hegemon in lesser esteem becomes apparent.

Alas, in those days the unruly Huai Yi dared harbor designs of encroachment, while the tiny state of Qi daily faced the danger of invasion and coercion. Those responsible for ordering that age ought to have been concerned. At that time Duke Huan of Qi held the hegemony. Troubled at heart, he restrained the great states and supported the small. First he settled the deliberations at Xian; then, assessing the work and appointing a date, he built the walls of Yuanling. He moved the court and markets of the small state of Qi, taking them from danger to security; he relocated its people, enabling them to obtain benefits and avoid harm. The five ancestral temples associated with Xia [?] did not fall into ruins, and the four classes of the people of Qi escaped utter misery. Bringing peace within and repelling threats from without—could Duke Huan’s achievement be considered slight?

Viewed in ordinary terms, this would seem fully consonant with the relief of distress accomplished by walling Xing, and far superior to the unauthorized establishment of a state at Chuqiu. The gentleman, however, says: Relieving disaster and aiding neighbors are certainly achievements of a hegemon; but building a city and relocating a state require the Son of Heaven’s command. Had Duke Huan at that time received orders from the Zhou royal house and placed the undertaking under a royal minister’s supervision, his practical achievement might have been only half that of other undertakings, yet in moral principle there would have been nothing to trouble his conscience. Even Nan Zhong’s walling of Shuofang and Zhong Shanfu’s walling of the eastern city would not have surpassed it.

Why, then, the thudding sounds of construction? It was Qi that built the walls, without requesting orders from the royal court. ‘Go forth and live, and live on!’ It was Qi that relocated the people, without reporting the matter to the Son of Heaven. Its exertions were certainly diligent, but its conduct was presumptuous…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
矣方諸邢之自遷而從拳救急者豈可同日語
乎比於衞之既滅而擅拳專封者其罪薄乎云
耳春秋正義不謀利明道不計功故雖列序會
鄟之八國而終凡舉緣陵之諸侯既異於城邢
之再序三師亦異於楚丘之深沒其迹貴王賤
霸以正待人之體何如哉雖然桓之城緣陵以
遷杞固可罪矣觀其會首止以定王儲盟葵丘
而明王禁于洮之靖難甯母之通貢桓於周室
有大功焉是則以道義言固三王之罪人以功
===
烈言亦五霸之巨擘論者謂春秋明王法而不
廢五霸之功信夫
禮記
是故君子不自大其事不自尚其功以求
處情過行弗率以求處厚彰人之善而美
人之功以求下賢
鄭伯和
同考試官教諭方批辭約意盡作長題
難得如此殆經生中之穎出者宜取爲本房冠
punctuated:
矣。方諸邢之自遷而從拳救急者，豈可同日語乎？比於衞之既滅而擅拳專封者，其罪薄乎云耳。《春秋》正義不謀利，明道不計功，故雖列序會鄟之八國，而終凡舉緣陵之諸侯。既異於城邢之再序三師，亦異於楚丘之深沒其迹。貴王賤霸，以正待人之體何如哉！雖然，桓之城緣陵以遷杞，固可罪矣。觀其會首止以定王儲，盟葵丘而明王禁，于洮之靖難、甯母之通貢，桓於周室有大功焉。是則以道義言，固三王之罪人；以功烈言，亦五霸之巨擘。論者謂《春秋》明王法而不廢五霸之功，信夫！

《禮記》
是故君子不自大其事，不自尚其功，以求處情；過行弗率，以求處厚；彰人之善，而美人之功，以求下賢。

鄭伯和

同考試官教諭方批：辭約意盡，作長題難得如此，殆經生中之穎出者，宜取爲本房冠。
translation_en:
…indeed. How could this be spoken of in the same breath as Xing’s moving on its own initiative and his adopting expedient measures [?] to relieve its emergency? Compared with his exercising authority without authorization [?] and independently restoring Wei after its destruction, his offense was merely somewhat lighter. The Spring and Autumn Annals upholds righteousness without seeking profit and makes the Way clear without calculating achievements. Thus, although it lists in order the eight states that met at Zhuan [?], it ultimately refers collectively to the feudal lords at Yuanling. This differs both from its listing the three armies a second time in the account of fortifying Xing and from its thoroughly concealing the participants’ involvement at Chuqiu. How telling is its manner of honoring kingship and disparaging hegemony, judging men by what is right!

Nevertheless, Duke Huan may certainly be blamed for fortifying Yuanling to relocate Qi 杞. Yet consider his assembly at Shouzhi to secure the royal succession, his covenant at Kuiqiu to proclaim the royal prohibitions, his settling the troubles at Tao, and his facilitating tribute at Ningmu: Huan rendered great service to the royal house of Zhou. Judged by the Way and righteousness, he was indeed an offender against the Three Kings; judged by his accomplishments, he was also a towering figure among the Five Hegemons. Commentators say that the Spring and Autumn Annals makes royal law clear without denying the achievements of the Five Hegemons. How true!

Record of Rites

“Therefore the gentleman does not magnify his own deeds or exalt his own achievements, seeking thereby to remain true to his actual circumstances. He does not follow excessive conduct, seeking thereby to abide in generosity. He makes others’ goodness manifest and praises their achievements, seeking thereby to place himself below the worthy.”

Zheng Bohe

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor: “The wording is concise and the meaning fully expressed. Such quality is hard to achieve in an essay on a long topic. He is surely an outstanding student of the Classics and should be ranked first in this examining section.”

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭姜批寫出自卑尊人意
思宛然在目
考試官敎諭徐批詞不違理可錄
記者歷言君子謙己而尊人無非自卑之道也
蓋人莫難於自卑也使或矜於己而加於人則
豈爲君子之道哉記表記者因言謚以尊名節
以一惠而及於此謂夫君子恭儉以求役仁而
處己也謙信讓以求役禮而與人也敬是故事
雖爲人所大己未嘗自以爲大功雖爲人所尚
===
己未嘗自以爲高所以然者豈沽名哉蓋欲求
以處乎情實之地不肯虛爲矯飾也行或過高
而苟難則不敢率之於身事或驚世而駭俗則
不敢措之於己所以然者豈飾詐哉蓋欲求以
處乎篤厚之道不欲過爲已甚也至若人或有
善己則彰而明之人或有功己則頌而美之其
爲是者非虛譽也惟欲求以下乎有善之人而
不沒其善也求以下乎有功之人而不掩其功
也又豈敢娼嫉而蔽賢哉是則曰處情曰處厚
punctuated:
考試官敎諭姜批：寫出自卑尊人意思，宛然在目。
考試官敎諭徐批：詞不違理，可錄。
記者歷言君子謙己而尊人，無非自卑之道也。蓋人莫難於自卑也，使或矜於己而加於人，則豈爲君子之道哉？記《表記》者因言「謚以尊名，節以一惠」，而及於此，謂夫君子恭儉以求役仁，而處己也謙；信讓以求役禮，而與人也敬。是故事雖爲人所大，己未嘗自以爲大；功雖爲人所尚，己未嘗自以爲高。所以然者，豈沽名哉？蓋欲求以處乎情實之地，不肯虛爲矯飾也。行或過高而苟難，則不敢率之於身；事或驚世而駭俗，則不敢措之於己。所以然者，豈飾詐哉？蓋欲求以處乎篤厚之道，不欲過爲已甚也。至若人或有善，己則彰而明之；人或有功，己則頌而美之。其爲是者，非虛譽也，惟欲求以下乎有善之人，而不沒其善也；求以下乎有功之人，而不掩其功也。又豈敢娼嫉而蔽賢哉？是則曰「處情」，曰「處厚」
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: The meaning of humbling oneself and honoring others is expressed so vividly that it seems present before our eyes.
Comment by Examiner Xu, Instructor: The wording accords with principle; this may be selected.
The author of the Record explains in detail how the gentleman humbles himself and honors others: all of this concerns the way of placing oneself below others. Nothing, indeed, is harder for people than humbling themselves. If someone were to take pride in himself and set himself above others, how could this be the gentleman’s way? The author of “Record of Exemplary Conduct” (Biao ji), having said, “Posthumous titles honor names, distilling them into a single excellence,” proceeds to this point. He means that the gentleman, through reverence and frugality, seeks to serve benevolence [?], and is humble in his own conduct; through trustworthiness and deference, he seeks to serve ritual propriety [?], and is respectful in his dealings with others. Thus, although others regard his deeds as great, he has never regarded them as great himself; although others esteem his achievements, he has never considered himself exalted on their account. Is he acting thus to purchase a reputation? He seeks, rather, to abide in genuine feeling and reality, refusing empty pretense and affectation. If a course of conduct is excessively lofty and difficult merely for difficulty’s sake, he dares not adopt it himself; if a deed would startle the world and shock prevailing custom, he dares not undertake it. Is he acting thus to disguise deceit? He seeks, rather, to abide in the way of sincerity and generosity, unwilling to carry things to excess. When others possess goodness, he brings it to light and makes it manifest; when others have achievements, he praises and commends them. He does this without empty flattery: he wishes only to place himself below those who possess goodness, without allowing their goodness to go unrecognized, and below those who have achievements, without concealing their accomplishments. How, then, could he dare harbor jealousy [?] and obscure the worthy? Thus, the expressions “abiding in genuine feeling” and “abiding in generosity”…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
無非所以謙於已曰彰善曰美功無非所以尊
乎人君子自卑之道何其至哉大抵此章爲人
臣言也考之上章有曰舜禹文王周公有君民
之大德有事君之小心下文又曰后稷之爲烈
也欲行之浮於名也自謂便人合而觀之于以
見人臣之道以仁爲本雖有庇民之大德不敢
有君民之心必卑已而尊人小心而畏義然後
可以盡其道也故惟舜禹文王周公可以爲仁
之厚而后稷則庶乎近之舍是而欲他求也幾
===
希矣
故孝弟忠順之行立而後可以爲人
洪晅
同考試官教諭方批說理詳明是亦能
盡人道者
考試官教諭姜批敷腴
考試官教諭徐批文有矩度
惟能備夫成人之行斯不愧於爲人矣盖冠所
以責成人之行也誠能備其行而不虧則人道
punctuated:
無非所以謙於已；曰彰善，曰美功，無非所以尊乎人。君子自卑之道何其至哉！大抵此章爲人臣言也。考之上章，有曰：「舜禹文王周公，有君民之大德，有事君之小心。」下文又曰：「后稷之爲烈也，欲行之浮於名也，自謂便人。」合而觀之，于以見人臣之道以仁爲本。雖有庇民之大德，不敢有君民之心，必卑已而尊人，小心而畏義，然後可以盡其道也。故惟舜禹文王周公可以爲仁之厚，而后稷則庶乎近之。舍是而欲他求也，幾希矣！

「故孝弟忠順之行立，而後可以爲人。」
洪晅
同考試官教諭方批：「說理詳明，是亦能盡人道者。」
考試官教諭姜批：「敷腴。」
考試官教諭徐批：「文有矩度。」

惟能備夫成人之行，斯不愧於爲人矣。盖冠所以責成人之行也，誠能備其行而不虧，則人道
translation_en:
…all are means of being humble oneself. Manifesting goodness and praising achievements are both means of honoring others. How consummate is the gentleman’s way of humbling himself! In general, this chapter speaks to those who serve as ministers. Examining the preceding chapter, we find: “Shun, Yu, King Wen, and the Duke of Zhou possessed the great virtue needed to rule the people, yet maintained the cautious attentiveness needed to serve a ruler.” The following passage also says: “As for Hou Ji’s achievements, he wished his conduct to surpass his reputation and called himself a man of service to others [?].” Read together, these passages show that benevolence is the foundation of the minister’s way. Even with the great virtue needed to shelter the people, he dares not harbor the ambition to rule them. He must humble himself and honor others, remain cautious, and stand in awe of righteousness; only then can he fully realize this way. Thus only Shun, Yu, King Wen, and the Duke of Zhou may be considered profound in benevolence, while Hou Ji came close to them. To abandon this and seek elsewhere offers little hope indeed!

“Thus, only after conduct marked by filial piety, fraternal deference, loyalty, and obedience has been established can one be a proper human being.”
By Hong Xuan 洪晅.
Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor, comments: “The reasoning is detailed and clear. Here, too, is someone capable of fully realizing the human way.”
Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “Expansive and rich.”
Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “The composition observes proper rules and measure.”

Only by possessing the full conduct of an adult can one be unashamed of being human. The capping ceremony is, indeed, the means of requiring adult conduct. If one can truly fulfill that conduct without deficiency, then the human way…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
盡矣尚何愧於為人乎記冠義者謂夫備人道
者必本於禮責成人者必始於冠彼人之冠也
以内言之則有父焉有兄焉事父兄而不盡其
禮則衣裳而禽犢矣可乎以外言之則有君焉
有長焉事君長而不盡其禮則冠冕而夷裔矣
得乎是故入而處於家也必温清定省承顔順
志而於事親盡其孝敬恭友愛克念天顯而於
事兄盡其弟如是則孝弟之行立矣出而處於
外也必攄忠納悃恪共厥職而於事君盡其忠
===
徐行後長謙卑退遜而於事長盡其順如是則
忠順之行立矣夫成人之行既立則成人之禮
以備由是父焉安其孝而可以為之子兄焉安
其弟而可以為之弟為子為弟之道夫豈有不
盡者哉君焉安其忠而可以為之臣長焉安其
順而可以為之少為臣為少之道抑何有不盡
者哉夫然則人之成也以行為之先而行之立
也以禮為之要冠禮之責成人也可不重歟嗟
夫冠者禮之始也嘉事之重者也先王知其然
punctuated:
盡矣，尚何愧於為人乎？記冠義者謂夫備人道者必本於禮，責成人者必始於冠。彼人之冠也，以内言之，則有父焉，有兄焉；事父兄而不盡其禮，則衣裳而禽犢矣，可乎？以外言之，則有君焉，有長焉；事君長而不盡其禮，則冠冕而夷裔矣，得乎？是故入而處於家也，必温清定省，承顔順志，而於事親盡其孝；敬恭友愛，克念天顯，而於事兄盡其弟。如是則孝弟之行立矣。出而處於外也，必攄忠納悃，恪共厥職，而於事君盡其忠；徐行後長，謙卑退遜，而於事長盡其順。如是則忠順之行立矣。
夫成人之行既立，則成人之禮以備。由是父焉安其孝，而可以為之子；兄焉安其弟，而可以為之弟。為子為弟之道，夫豈有不盡者哉？君焉安其忠，而可以為之臣；長焉安其順，而可以為之少。為臣為少之道，抑何有不盡者哉？夫然則人之成也，以行為之先；而行之立也，以禮為之要。冠禮之責成人也，可不重歟？嗟夫！冠者，禮之始也，嘉事之重者也。先王知其然
translation_en:
…the duties of human life are fulfilled. What cause remains for shame at being human? The author of “The Meaning of the Capping Ceremony” says that fulfilling the duties of human life must be rooted in ritual propriety, and that holding someone to the responsibilities of adulthood must begin with capping. When a man is capped, within the household he has a father and elder brothers. If he serves them without fully observing ritual propriety, he is merely a bird or calf dressed in clothing [?]. Can this be acceptable? Outside the household, he has a ruler and elders. If he serves them without fully observing ritual propriety, he is merely a barbarian wearing a ceremonial cap. Can this be right? Thus, at home, he must keep his parents warm in winter and cool in summer [?], settle them at night and inquire after them in the morning, attend to their expressions, and comply with their wishes, thereby fulfilling his filial duty in serving them. He must be respectful and affectionate, keeping firmly in mind the manifest bonds ordained by Heaven, thereby fulfilling his fraternal duty in serving his elder brothers. In this way, filial and fraternal conduct is established. Outside the household, he must express his loyalty, offer his heartfelt sincerity, and reverently discharge his duties, thereby fulfilling his loyalty in serving his ruler. He must walk slowly behind his elders, be humble, and defer to others, thereby fulfilling his obedience in serving his elders. In this way, loyal and obedient conduct is established.
Once adult conduct is established, the ritual requirements of adulthood are fulfilled. His father can then rest content in his filial devotion, and he is fit to be his son; his elder brothers can rest content in his fraternal respect, and he is fit to be their younger brother. How could any part of his duty as a son or younger brother remain unfulfilled? His ruler can rest content in his loyalty, and he is fit to be his subject; his elders can rest content in his obedience, and he is fit to be their junior. How could any part of his duty as a subject or junior remain unfulfilled? Thus, in attaining adulthood, conduct comes first; and in establishing conduct, ritual propriety is essential. Can the capping ceremony, which imposes the responsibilities of adulthood, be treated as anything but weighty? Ah! Capping is the beginning of ritual observance and a momentous auspicious occasion. The former kings understood this…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
故行之於廟以示其尊筮日筮賓以致其敬何
也盖以孝弟忠順之行立而後孝弟忠順之化
行修己治人之道胥此焉出先王所以重禮以
爲國本焉是故也後世禮教不脩一切放廢而
於冠之一事尤爲率略是以人道不明出治無
本而於天下之禮卒不可行也噫
第貳場
論
孔子與天地參而四時同
===
張燮
同考試官訓導俞批官様題目作者不
泛則畧惟此篇有源委有操縱詞健而豐氣雄
而正寫出孔子同造化之旨無餘是宜録出
同考試官教諭魏批是論說孔子道德
教化詞約義該宛然一太極在目精微之學昌
大之氣率於此發之春闈大捷又當為子預占
考試官教諭姜批周子之學在太極
一圖而通書所以發其蘊也此作根本圖說□
punctuated:
故行之於廟，以示其尊；筮日筮賓，以致其敬。何也？盖以孝弟忠順之行立，而後孝弟忠順之化行，修己治人之道胥此焉出。先王所以重禮以爲國本焉，是故也。後世禮教不脩，一切放廢，而於冠之一事尤爲率略，是以人道不明，出治無本，而於天下之禮卒不可行也。噫！

第貳場
論
孔子與天地參而四時同
張燮

同考試官訓導俞批：官様題目，作者不泛則畧。惟此篇有源委，有操縱，詞健而豐，氣雄而正，寫出孔子同造化之旨無餘，是宜録出。

同考試官教諭魏批：是論說孔子道德教化，詞約義該，宛然一太極在目。精微之學，昌大之氣，率於此發之。春闈大捷，又當為子預占。

考試官教諭姜批：周子之學在太極一圖，而通書所以發其蘊也。此作根本圖說□
translation_en:
…Thus they performed it in the ancestral temple to demonstrate its dignity, and used milfoil divination to select the day and the guest who would officiate, thereby expressing their reverence. Why was this? Only after conduct characterized by filial piety, fraternal respect, loyalty, and obedience was established could transformation through these virtues spread. The ways of cultivating oneself and governing others both proceed from this. This is why the former kings esteemed ritual as the foundation of the state. In later ages, ritual instruction was neglected and everything abandoned; the capping ceremony in particular was treated carelessly. Consequently, the human way became obscure and government lacked a foundation, so that the rites of the realm ultimately could not be put into practice. Alas!

Second Session
Discourse
“Confucius Forms a Triad with Heaven and Earth and Accords with the Four Seasons”
Zhang Xie

Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Assistant Instructor: With a conventional examination topic of this kind, writers tend to be either vague or cursory. This essay alone traces its subject from source to outcome and displays mastery in its handling. Its language is vigorous and rich; its spirit, powerful and upright. It fully expresses the meaning of Confucius’s unity with the creative transformations of the cosmos, leaving nothing unexpressed. It deserves to be selected for inclusion.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wei, Instructor: This discourse expounds Confucius’s Way, virtue, teaching, and transforming influence. Its language is concise and its meaning comprehensive: it is as though the Supreme Ultimate itself were before one’s eyes. Subtle and profound learning, together with a vast and flourishing spirit, all find expression here. I would also venture to predict for you a great success at the spring Metropolitan Examination.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: Master Zhou’s learning is contained in the single Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate, while his Book of Penetration (Tongshu) brings out its deeper implications. This composition takes the Explanation of the Diagram as its foundation, [illegible]…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
加粧點而文理粲然蓋嘗究心理學者公閱之
秀無踰子矣
考試官教諭徐批文以理為主而能
輔之以氣斯為作家此論詞氣超逸所謂使人
擊節歎賞未如使人肅然生敬者也宜録之以
礪後進
論曰以太極之全體而擬聖人善言聖人者也
夫莫大於天地天地太極之體也莫久於四時
四時太極之用也聖人合陰陽之動靜妙五行
===
之生成道之高也配乎天德之厚也配乎地教
化之無窮也配乎四時故以一人之身位乎天
高地下之間而不見其小合乎四時變通之運
而不見其近非聖人全體太極其何以參天地
而同四時如此哉周子以是擬之可謂善言聖
人者矣請暢厥㫖世之言聖人者多矣仰宫墻
之高廣窺堂室之深奥有以日月而擬道之高
者矣有以淵泉而擬德之厚者矣有以時雨而
擬教化之妙者矣殊不知日月天之一象耳未
punctuated:
加粧點，而文理粲然，蓋嘗究心理學者。公閱之秀，無踰子矣。

考試官教諭徐批：文以理為主，而能輔之以氣，斯為作家。此論詞氣超逸，所謂使人擊節歎賞，未如使人肅然生敬者也。宜録之以礪後進。

論曰：以太極之全體而擬聖人，善言聖人者也。夫莫大於天地，天地，太極之體也；莫久於四時，四時，太極之用也。聖人合陰陽之動靜，妙五行之生成。道之高也配乎天，德之厚也配乎地，教化之無窮也配乎四時。故以一人之身，位乎天高地下之間，而不見其小；合乎四時變通之運，而不見其近。非聖人全體太極，其何以參天地而同四時如此哉？周子以是擬之，可謂善言聖人者矣。請暢厥㫖。世之言聖人者多矣，仰宫墻之高廣，窺堂室之深奥。有以日月而擬道之高者矣，有以淵泉而擬德之厚者矣，有以時雨而擬教化之妙者矣。殊不知日月，天之一象耳，未
translation_en:
…adding embellishment, yet the writing and its reasoning shine brilliantly: the author must have devoted himself to investigating the learning of principle. Among the outstanding works reviewed jointly [?], none surpasses yours.

Comment by Examiner Xu, Instructor: Writing takes principle as its foundation; when the author can support it with vital force, he is an accomplished writer. This discourse is extraordinary in its diction and spirit. As the saying goes, making readers beat time in admiration is less worthy than making them feel solemn reverence. It should be recorded to spur on younger scholars.

The discourse reads: To compare the sage to the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety is to speak well of the sage. Nothing is greater than Heaven and Earth: Heaven and Earth are the substance of the Supreme Ultimate. Nothing is more enduring than the four seasons: the four seasons are the functioning of the Supreme Ultimate. The sage accords with the movement and stillness of yin and yang and wondrously embodies the generation and completion of the Five Phases. The height of his Way matches Heaven; the depth of his virtue matches Earth; the inexhaustibility of his moral teaching and transforming influence matches the four seasons. Thus, with the body of a single person, he stands between Heaven above and Earth below without appearing small; he accords with the changing course of the four seasons without appearing limited. Unless the sage embodied the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety, how could he thus stand alongside Heaven and Earth as a third and accord with the four seasons? Master Zhou, in making this comparison, may indeed be said to have spoken well of the sage. Allow me to expound its meaning.

Many in this world have spoken of the sage, gazing up at the height and breadth of his palace walls and peering into the profound recesses of his halls and chambers. Some have compared the height of his Way to the sun and moon; some have compared the depth of his virtue to deep pools and springs; some have compared the wondrous efficacy of his teaching and transforming influence to timely rain. Yet they fail to realize that the sun and moon are merely one manifestation of Heaven, not yet …

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
足以言高之至也淵泉地之一物耳未足以言
厚之至也時雨但四時中之一氣耳又何以見
其無窮也謂之能言聖人則可謂之善言聖人
則未也若周子以天地而擬道德以四時而擬
教化是以太極之全體而論聖人也其善言聖
人者歟何則太極之未判也渾乎一理而已無
所謂天地亦無所謂四時迨夫一動一靜而兩
儀生一變一合而五行具陽上浮而為天日月
繫焉星辰麗焉穹然於萬物之上仰之而不見
===
其際也天何高乎陰下凝而為地華嶽載焉河
海振焉隤然於萬物之下測之而不知其極也
地何厚乎五行順布而為四時寒往而暑來暑
往而寒來推之而不見其始之合引之而不見
其終之離也四時何無窮乎孔子雖曰聖人而
亦人耳混然中處不能與天地同其大修短隨
化不能與四時同其久況事功不見於當時空
言何補於後世而謂其與天地參而四時同何
也噫不于其理而于其迹豈善言聖人者哉蓋
punctuated:
足以言高之至也。淵泉，地之一物耳，未足以言厚之至也。時雨，但四時中之一氣耳，又何以見其無窮也？謂之能言聖人則可，謂之善言聖人則未也。若周子以天地而擬道德，以四時而擬教化，是以太極之全體而論聖人也，其善言聖人者歟！

何則？太極之未判也，渾乎一理而已，無所謂天地，亦無所謂四時。迨夫一動一靜而兩儀生，一變一合而五行具，陽上浮而為天，日月繫焉，星辰麗焉，穹然於萬物之上，仰之而不見其際也，天何高乎！陰下凝而為地，華嶽載焉，河海振焉，隤然於萬物之下，測之而不知其極也，地何厚乎！五行順布而為四時，寒往而暑來，暑往而寒來，推之而不見其始之合，引之而不見其終之離也，四時何無窮乎！

孔子雖曰聖人，而亦人耳，混然中處，不能與天地同其大；修短隨化，不能與四時同其久。況事功不見於當時，空言何補於後世？而謂其與天地參而四時同，何也？噫！不于其理而于其迹，豈善言聖人者哉！蓋
translation_en:
…sufficient to express the utmost height. Deep springs are merely one thing within the earth, insufficient to express the utmost depth. Seasonable rain is merely one manifestation of vital force within the four seasons; how, then, could it reveal their inexhaustibility? Such speakers may be said to speak of the sage, but they cannot yet be said to speak well of him. Master Zhou, however, compares the sage’s Way and virtue to Heaven and Earth, and his transforming instruction to the four seasons. This is to discuss the sage in terms of the complete substance of the Supreme Ultimate. Surely he speaks well of the sage!

Why is this so? Before the Supreme Ultimate differentiated, there was simply one undivided principle: there was as yet neither Heaven and Earth nor the four seasons. When movement and stillness alternated, the Two Modes arose; through transformation and union, the Five Phases became complete. Yang floated upward to become Heaven, with the sun and moon suspended in it and the stars arrayed upon it. Vaulting above the myriad things, it has boundaries that cannot be seen when one looks up. How high Heaven is! Yin condensed below to become Earth, bearing Mount Hua and the other great peaks, sustaining [?] the rivers and seas. Lying low beneath the myriad things, it has depths whose limit cannot be known by sounding them. How deep Earth is! The Five Phases unfold in due order to become the four seasons: cold departs and heat arrives; heat departs and cold arrives. Tracing them back, one cannot see their initial union; extending them forward, one cannot see their final separation. How inexhaustible the four seasons are!

Although Confucius is called a sage, he was nevertheless a human being. Dwelling amid the whole, he could not equal Heaven and Earth in magnitude; the length of his life depended upon the transformations of nature, and he could not equal the four seasons in duration. Moreover, his practical achievements were not manifest in his own time; what benefit could empty words bring to later generations? Why, then, say that he stands alongside Heaven and Earth as a third and is one with the four seasons? Alas! To attend to his outward traces rather than his underlying principle—how could this be speaking well of the sage? For…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
天之所以高一太極之動也地之所以厚一太
極之靜也四時之所以無窮一太極之流行也
人具太極之理以有生則天地四時本吾一體
參兩而為三合四而為一固人之能事也但小
人悖之而不修始與天地不相似君子修之而
未盡則亦無以及乎天地矣惟孔子之生也稟
天地中和之氣全陰陽動靜之德其行之也中
其處之也正其發之也仁其裁之也義中與仁
為陽流行於感通之間不謂之道乎正與義為
===
陰存主於至寂之中不謂之德乎道德行於一
世則為法於一世道德行於萬世則為法於萬
世又不謂之教化乎故以其道言之若仁之於
父子義之於君臣禮之於賓主知之於賢否行
之而各極其至夷之清尹之任惠之和出之而
各以其時其道之高也譬如天之無不覆幬者
矣以其德言之若有容之仁有執之義有敬之
禮有別之知皆全體而無遺顏閔之德行游夏
之文學子張之威儀則具體而極大其德之厚
punctuated: 天之所以高，一太極之動也；地之所以厚，一太極之靜也；四時之所以無窮，一太極之流行也。人具太極之理以有生，則天地四時本吾一體。參兩而為三，合四而為一，固人之能事也。但小人悖之而不修，始與天地不相似；君子修之而未盡，則亦無以及乎天地矣。惟孔子之生也，稟天地中和之氣，全陰陽動靜之德。其行之也中，其處之也正，其發之也仁，其裁之也義。中與仁為陽，流行於感通之間，不謂之道乎？正與義為陰，存主於至寂之中，不謂之德乎？道德行於一世，則為法於一世；道德行於萬世，則為法於萬世。又不謂之教化乎？故以其道言之，若仁之於父子，義之於君臣，禮之於賓主，知之於賢否，行之而各極其至；夷之清，尹之任，惠之和，出之而各以其時。其道之高也，譬如天之無不覆幬者矣。以其德言之，若有容之仁，有執之義，有敬之禮，有別之知，皆全體而無遺；顏閔之德行，游夏之文學，子張之威儀，則具體而極大。其德之厚
translation_en: …Heaven is high through the movement of the one Supreme Ultimate; Earth is deep through the stillness of the one Supreme Ultimate; the four seasons are inexhaustible through the ceaseless operation of the one Supreme Ultimate. Human beings possess the principle of the Supreme Ultimate and thereby come into life; thus Heaven, Earth, and the four seasons are fundamentally one body with us. To stand alongside the two as a third, and to unite the four into one, are indeed within human capacity. Yet petty people contravene this principle and fail to cultivate it, and so cease to resemble Heaven and Earth. Gentlemen cultivate it, but if they do not realize it fully, they too cannot equal Heaven and Earth. Confucius alone, at his birth, received the balanced and harmonious vital energy of Heaven and Earth and possessed in full the virtues of yin and yang, movement and stillness. In action he attained the mean; in repose he was correct; in responding he was benevolent; in judging he was righteous. Attaining the mean and benevolence belong to yang, flowing through the interplay of stimulus and response: is this not called the Way? Correctness and righteousness belong to yin, abiding and governing within utmost stillness: is this not called virtue? When the Way and virtue are practiced in one age, they become the standard for that age; when practiced through ten thousand ages, they become the standard for ten thousand ages. Is this not also called teaching and moral transformation? Thus, speaking of his Way, benevolence between father and son, righteousness between ruler and minister, ritual propriety between guest and host, and wisdom in distinguishing the worthy from the unworthy were each practiced to their utmost perfection. The purity of Bo Yi, the responsibility assumed by Yi Yin, and the harmony of Liu Xiahui were each manifested as the occasion required. The height of his Way was like Heaven, which leaves nothing uncovered. Speaking of his virtue, the benevolence that embraces others, the righteousness that holds firm, the ritual propriety that embodies reverence, and the wisdom that makes distinctions were all present in their entirety, with nothing omitted. The virtuous conduct of Yan Hui and Min Ziqian, the literary learning of Ziyou and Zixia, and the dignified bearing of Zizhang were embodied in him and developed to their utmost greatness. The depth of his virtue…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
也譬如地之無不持載者矣是以天位乎上地
位乎下而孔子之道德相與並立而爲三焉以
其教化言之爲之親疎之殺而仁之教以立爲
之貴賤之等而義之教以行爲之制度文爲而
禮之教以得爲之開導禁止而知之教以明易
爲生民之府書爲長民之府易書之教化即春
夏之生長歴萬世而不已也詩爲收民之府春
秋爲藏民之府詩春秋之教化即秋冬之收藏
亘千古而如斯也故四時錯行循環不已而孔
===
===
子之教化相與同運而無窮焉是則道髙如天
陽也德厚如地陰也教化無窮則四時五行也
太極全體之道具於孔子之一身吾不知孔子
其太極乎太極其孔子乎周子有見於此而發
以示人可謂善觀聖人而善言德行者矣豈日
月淵泉時雨之喻所能彷彿哉雖然天地四時
固可以擬聖人矣而聖人之道恐非天地四時
所能盡也天能覆而不能載地能載而不能覆
四時各適其用而不能相通也孔子則兼陰陽
punctuated: 也，譬如地之無不持載者矣。是以天位乎上，地位乎下，而孔子之道德相與並立而爲三焉。以其教化言之，爲之親疎之殺，而仁之教以立；爲之貴賤之等，而義之教以行；爲之制度文爲，而禮之教以得；爲之開導禁止，而知之教以明。易爲生民之府，書爲長民之府，易、書之教化，即春夏之生長，歴萬世而不已也。詩爲收民之府，春秋爲藏民之府，詩、春秋之教化，即秋冬之收藏，亘千古而如斯也。故四時錯行，循環不已，而孔子之教化相與同運而無窮焉。是則道髙如天，陽也；德厚如地，陰也；教化無窮，則四時五行也。太極全體之道，具於孔子之一身。吾不知孔子其太極乎？太極其孔子乎？周子有見於此，而發以示人，可謂善觀聖人而善言德行者矣。豈日月淵泉時雨之喻所能彷彿哉！雖然，天地四時固可以擬聖人矣，而聖人之道恐非天地四時所能盡也。天能覆而不能載，地能載而不能覆，四時各適其用而不能相通也。孔子則兼陰陽
translation_en:
…is like the earth, which bears and sustains everything. Thus Heaven occupies its place above and Earth its place below, while Confucius’s Way and virtue stand alongside them, forming a triad. As for his transforming instruction, he established gradations of closeness and distance in kinship, thereby founding instruction in benevolence; he established ranks of noble and lowly, thereby putting instruction in righteousness into practice; he established institutions and ceremonial observances, thereby giving effect to instruction in ritual propriety; and he provided guidance and prohibitions, thereby making instruction in wisdom clear. The Book of Changes is the repository for bringing the people to life; the Book of Documents is the repository for nurturing their growth. The transforming instruction of the Changes and Documents is thus the generation and growth of spring and summer, continuing through ten thousand generations without ceasing. The Book of Odes is the repository for gathering the people in; the Spring and Autumn Annals is the repository for sheltering them. The transforming instruction of the Odes and the Spring and Autumn Annals is thus the gathering and storing of autumn and winter, remaining so throughout the ages. Hence, as the four seasons alternate in an unceasing cycle, Confucius’s transforming instruction moves together with them without end.

Thus his Way, lofty as Heaven, is yang; his virtue, substantial as Earth, is yin; and his inexhaustible transforming instruction is the four seasons and the Five Phases. The Way of the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety is embodied in Confucius alone. I do not know: is Confucius the Supreme Ultimate? Is the Supreme Ultimate Confucius? Master Zhou perceived this and expounded it to instruct others. He may indeed be called one who understood well how to contemplate the sage and speak of virtuous conduct. How could comparisons to the sun and moon, deep pools and wellsprings, or timely rain even approximate this!

Nevertheless, although Heaven, Earth, and the four seasons can certainly serve as comparisons for the sage, I fear that they cannot encompass the entirety of the sage’s Way. Heaven can cover but cannot bear; Earth can bear but cannot cover. Each of the four seasons fulfills its own function but cannot exercise those of the others. Confucius, however, unites yin and yang…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
五行而全體之高明所以覆物也博厚所以載
物也悠久所以成物也天地賴以立四時賴以
順是則孔子之道德教化不惟參天地同四時
而又有功於天地四時也愚敢爲是說以補周
子之未備謹論
表
擬宋賜禮部進士吕蒙正等及第謝表〔太平〕
興國二年
林輅
===
同考試官訓導俞批一榜及第處此篇
獨能道出當是作者
同考試官教諭魏批組織宋事縟麗可
觀必閩中竒士也
考試官教諭姜批温純典則且能道
當時事
考試官教諭徐批真抽黄對白手
伏以
禮樂致太平仰
punctuated:
五行而全體之。高明所以覆物也，博厚所以載物也，悠久所以成物也。天地賴以立，四時賴以順。是則孔子之道德教化，不惟參天地、同四時，而又有功於天地四時也。愚敢爲是說，以補周子之未備。謹論。

表

擬宋賜禮部進士吕蒙正等及第謝表〔太平〕興國二年

林輅

同考試官訓導俞批：「一榜及第處，此篇獨能道出，當是作者。」
同考試官教諭魏批：「組織宋事，縟麗可觀，必閩中竒士也。」
考試官教諭姜批：「温純典則，且能道當時事。」
考試官教諭徐批：「真抽黄對白手。」

伏以：禮樂致太平，仰
translation_en:
…and the Five Phases, embodying them in their entirety. His loftiness and brilliance enable him to shelter all things; his breadth and depth enable him to sustain all things; his enduring constancy enables him to bring all things to completion. Heaven and Earth depend upon him to stand established, and the four seasons depend upon him to follow their proper course. Thus Confucius’s Way, virtue, and transforming instruction not only rank alongside Heaven and Earth and accord with the four seasons, but also contribute to their workings. I venture to offer this explanation to supplement what Master Zhou left incomplete. Respectfully submitted as a discourse.

Memorial

A simulated memorial of thanks by Lü Mengzheng and others, metropolitan graduates of the Ministry of Rites, upon being awarded passing status under the Song. Second year of the 〔Taiping〕 Xingguo reign [977].

By Lin Lu.

Associate Examiner Yu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “On the matter of passing together on a single list, this essay alone succeeds in expressing the point. Its author must be an accomplished writer.”
Associate Examiner Wei, Instructor, comments: “It weaves together events of the Song with rich and splendid embellishment, well worth admiring. The author must be an exceptional talent from Fujian.”
Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “Gentle and pure in tone, classical and disciplined in form; it also succeeds in recounting the events of that time.”
Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “Truly a master at drawing out the yellow and matching it with the white—that is, at crafting elegant parallel phrases.”
