title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
一人之興國文章關氣運占五緯之聚奎掄材
偶入於彀中
賜第驚踰於望外叨榮旅進揣分私慙茲蓋
伏遇
〇〇〇〇
大智用人
沉幾先物
好學邁商宗之志嫚儒陋漢祖之風自巳至
申手不遑於釋卷技十得五心恒切於求
===
賢謂多取勢家在
先帝盡革其弊而思振淹滯宜今日廣開其途
溥一榜之
殊恩超諸科之常格並稱及第不限倫魁蓋自
開寶
召對以來雖每親於覆試然而顯德殿罰之
式曾未副於旁求惟茲
明詔之頒用表作人之盛纔抱白苧遽爛銀袍
給左藏之青錢何啻二十萬數拜省中之
punctuated: 一人之興國；文章關氣運，占五緯之聚奎。掄材偶入於彀中，賜第驚踰於望外。叨榮旅進，揣分私慙。茲蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，大智用人，沉幾先物。好學邁商宗之志，嫚儒陋漢祖之風。自巳至申，手不遑於釋卷；技十得五，心恒切於求賢。謂多取勢家，在先帝盡革其弊；而思振淹滯，宜今日廣開其途。溥一榜之殊恩，超諸科之常格。並稱及第，不限倫魁。蓋自開寶召對以來，雖每親於覆試，然而顯德殿罰之式，曾未副於旁求。惟茲明詔之頒，用表作人之盛。纔抱白苧，遽爛銀袍。給左藏之青錢，何啻二十萬數；拜省中之
translation_en:
…the One Man’s raising the realm to prosperity. Literary accomplishment is bound to the fortunes of the age: its auspicious sign is the gathering of the five planets in Kui. In the selection of talent, we happened to fall within your bowshot; the conferral of degrees surpassed our expectations to our astonishment. Undeservedly receiving this honor and advancing together, we privately feel ashamed when we measure our own worth.

This is because we have reverently encountered 〇〇〇〇, who employs men with supreme wisdom and, through profound discernment of incipient change, anticipates events. Your love of learning surpasses the aspirations of the Shang king; you disdain the Han founder’s habit of treating scholars contemptuously. From the si hour to the shen hour, your hands find no leisure to put down a book; accepting five out of ten accomplishments [?], your heart remains intent on seeking worthy men. As for the excessive selection of men from powerful families, the late emperor entirely abolished that abuse; to raise up those long held back, it is fitting today to open their avenues of advancement widely. You extend exceptional favor to an entire examination list, exceeding the usual rules of the various examinations. All alike are designated as having passed with a degree, without restricting this distinction to the foremost candidates.

Ever since candidates were summoned for an imperial audience and questioning in the Kaibao era, the emperor has regularly conducted their reexamination in person. Yet the practice of demotion and punishment from the Xiande era [?] never fulfilled the aim of seeking talent far and wide. Now the promulgation of this enlightened edict manifests the flourishing cultivation of men of talent. Only just clad in white ramie, we suddenly shine in silver robes. The bronze cash granted from the Left Treasury amounts to far more than two hundred thousand; we reverently receive from the Department of State Affairs the …

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
黃甲共誇三百九人吾道增輝士林拭目
伏念臣蒙正等草塵微質樞蠹朽材蚊睫
焦冥極卑棲之可陋蹄涔鼁鼃亦亂聒之
相叢每思畫地自陳繆執昔年之策豈謂
挑燈不寐悉觀
上國之光馬奏天閑牝而黃牡而驪同歸一
視木掄匠石大為杗細為桷不棄寸長遂
厪累日之披翻盡出
重瞳之鑒別
===
明良際會匪止誇一時榮一鄉
上下交脩敢忘正其誼明其道伸素懷之耿
耿世務可陳達片語之拳拳
君鼇是祝伏願先人民而後疆土脩内治以来
遠夷封違命於隴西赤心既感置太原於
度外黑子何逃丕昭偃武之休益闡崇文
之化華山歸馬洛水呈龜魚躍鳶飛誰識
形容於有象
龍行虎步但知頌禱於無疆臣等無任瞻
punctuated:
黃甲，共誇三百九人，吾道增輝，士林拭目。
伏念臣蒙正等，草塵微質，樞蠹朽材；蚊睫焦冥，極卑棲之可陋；蹄涔鼁鼃，亦亂聒之相叢。每思畫地自陳，繆執昔年之策；豈謂挑燈不寐，悉觀上國之光。馬奏天閑，牝而黃、牡而驪，同歸一視；木掄匠石，大為杗、細為桷，不棄寸長。遂厪累日之披翻，盡出重瞳之鑒別。
明良際會，匪止誇一時、榮一鄉；上下交脩，敢忘正其誼、明其道。伸素懷之耿耿，世務可陳；達片語之拳拳，君鼇是祝。伏願先人民而後疆土，脩内治以来遠夷。封違命於隴西，赤心既感；置太原於度外，黑子何逃。丕昭偃武之休，益闡崇文之化。華山歸馬，洛水呈龜，魚躍鳶飛，誰識形容於有象；龍行虎步，但知頌禱於無疆。臣等無任瞻
translation_en:
…the yellow register of successful candidates: together we acclaim its three hundred and nine men. Our Way gains new lustre, and the community of scholars watches with renewed attention.
We, your servants Mengzheng and the others, humbly reflect that our substance is as insignificant as grass and dust, our timber rotten and worm-eaten [?]. Like the tiny jiaoming insect upon a mosquito’s eyelash, we occupy the most contemptibly lowly perch; like frogs gathered in a hoofprint’s puddle, we merely add to the confused croaking. We had always thought only of marking out the ground to present our case, mistakenly clinging to the policy essays of former years. How could we have expected to trim our lamps and remain awake, beholding in full the splendour of the imperial capital? When horses are presented to the imperial stables, whether yellow mares or black stallions, all receive the same consideration. When timber is selected by Carpenter Shi, the large pieces become beams and the slender ones rafters: not an inch of useful length is discarded. Thus we have occasioned Your Majesty’s laborious reading over successive days, and all have undergone the discerning scrutiny of your double-pupilled eyes.
This meeting of an enlightened sovereign and worthy servants is more than a boast for one moment or an honour for one locality. As those above and below cultivate themselves together, how could we forget to uphold righteousness and illuminate the Way? In expressing the steadfast loyalty we have long cherished, we may speak of the affairs of the realm; in conveying our devotion through these few words, we pray for Your Majesty’s [longevity?]. We humbly wish that you put the people before territory, and cultivate internal government so as to attract distant foreign peoples. By enfeoffing in Longxi the one who defied your command, you have already moved his heart to sincerity; even if you set Taiyuan aside from your calculations, how could that tiny black speck escape? Magnificently display the blessings of laying down arms, and further extend the transforming influence of honouring civil culture. Let horses return to Mount Hua and the Luo River present its tortoise. Fish leap and kites fly: who could capture this in tangible forms? With a dragon’s gait and a tiger’s stride, Your Majesty advances; we know only to offer praise and prayers for your boundless reign. We, your servants, cannot restrain ourselves as we gaze…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
天仰
聖激切屛營之至謹奉
表稱謝以
聞
第叁塲
策
第一問
張燮
同考試官訓導俞批此作敷揚
===
聖製若數甲乙異日效用於時必知急先務矣宜冠多士
同考試官教諭魏批五策筆力雄健而
聖製一對尤見俊偉叅之前二塲俱優擢冠多士當讓子矣
考試官教諭姜批善鳴
國家之盛
考試官教諭徐批宣揚
聖訓文勢超邁如川流迅激有洄洑逶迤觀者不厭
讀伊訓之書知古人所以重太子之教讀
周官之書知古人所以嚴大臣之選甚矣
punctuated:
天仰聖，激切屛營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叁塲
策
第一問
張燮

同考試官訓導俞批：此作敷揚聖製，若數甲乙，異日效用於時，必知急先務矣。宜冠多士。

同考試官教諭魏批：五策筆力雄健，而聖製一對尤見俊偉。叅之前二塲俱優，擢冠多士，當讓子矣。

考試官教諭姜批：善鳴國家之盛。

考試官教諭徐批：宣揚聖訓，文勢超邁，如川流迅激，有洄洑逶迤，觀者不厭。

讀《伊訓》之書，知古人所以重太子之教；讀《周官》之書，知古人所以嚴大臣之選。甚矣，
translation_en:
… looking up to Heaven and reverently toward Your Majesty, with the utmost fervor and trepidation, we respectfully submit this memorial expressing our thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Zhang Xie

Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Assistant Instructor: This composition expounds the imperial text as clearly as enumerating A and B. When he renders service in the future, he will surely know to give precedence to the most urgent tasks. He should rank first among the candidates.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wei, Instructor: All five policy essays display vigorous and forceful writing, while the response to the imperial text is especially outstanding. Considered together with his work in the preceding two sessions, all are excellent. In selecting the foremost among the candidates, we must yield that place to you.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: He ably proclaims the flourishing condition of the state.

Comment by Examiner Xu, Instructor: He expounds the imperial instructions with exceptional literary momentum, like a river rushing swiftly, with swirling eddies and winding turns. Readers never tire of it.

Reading the Instructions of Yi (Yi xun), one understands why the ancients attached importance to the education of the crown prince; reading the Offices of Zhou (Zhou guan), one understands why the ancients were exacting in selecting high ministers. How very great indeed …

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
太子之教與大臣之選在商周盛時尤知
所以重之嚴之如此况後世於太子可不
素教而預養之於大臣可不旁求而慎選
之哉夫太子國之主器所以嗣天下者也
大臣君之股肱所以輔天下者也根本之
地所係甚重觀賈生之諫漢文帝朱子之
告宋孝宗則於天下之根本知所以培植
之矣我
宣宗章皇帝以廣運之德承富有之業知太子
===
之當輔翼大臣之當選任也故所製五倫
書言無不備理無不包而於建儲命官二
事特加詳焉以漢唐以下之為太子言之
若漢武帝以其子壯大多知而位儲宫明
帝以其子聖表有異而承世序宋太宗欲
其子之動皆由禮則告李沆等以勗其謙
冲孝宗欲其子之練歷庶務則責虞允文
以戒其縱逸此皆
聖製所叙以垂範者也若所謂連抱之木必授
punctuated:
太子之教與大臣之選，在商周盛時，尤知所以重之嚴之如此。况後世於太子，可不素教而預養之；於大臣，可不旁求而慎選之哉？夫太子，國之主器，所以嗣天下者也；大臣，君之股肱，所以輔天下者也。根本之地，所係甚重。觀賈生之諫漢文帝、朱子之告宋孝宗，則於天下之根本，知所以培植之矣。
我宣宗章皇帝以廣運之德，承富有之業，知太子之當輔翼、大臣之當選任也。故所製《五倫書》，言無不備，理無不包，而於建儲、命官二事特加詳焉。以漢唐以下之為太子言之，若漢武帝以其子壯大多知而位儲宫，明帝以其子聖表有異而承世序，宋太宗欲其子之動皆由禮，則告李沆等以勗其謙冲；孝宗欲其子之練歷庶務，則責虞允文以戒其縱逸。此皆聖製所叙以垂範者也。若所謂連抱之木必授
translation_en:
…the education of the heir apparent and the selection of high ministers: in the flourishing age of Shang and Zhou, they understood so well why the former must be taken seriously and the latter conducted rigorously. How much more, in later ages, must the heir apparent be taught regularly and nurtured in advance, and high ministers sought widely and selected with care! The heir apparent is the guardian of the state's sacred vessels, the one who will inherit rule over all under Heaven. High ministers are the ruler's arms and legs, those who assist him in governing all under Heaven. These foundational positions carry responsibilities of the greatest weight. By considering Jia Yi's remonstrance to Emperor Wen of Han and Master Zhu's counsel to Emperor Xiaozong of Song, one can understand how to nurture the foundations of the realm.
Our Emperor Xuanzong Zhang, with his far-reaching virtue, inherited a richly endowed imperial enterprise. He understood that the heir apparent required guidance and support, and that high ministers must be selected and appointed. Thus the Book of the Five Relationships (Wulun shu), which he composed, is comprehensive in its statements and all-embracing in its principles, while treating the two matters of establishing an heir and appointing officials in particular detail. To speak of those who became heirs apparent from the Han and Tang onward: Emperor Wu of Han installed his son in the heir apparent's palace because he had grown to maturity and possessed extensive knowledge; Emperor Ming had his son continue the dynastic succession because his sagely bearing was extraordinary. Emperor Taizong of Song wished his son's every action to accord with ritual propriety, and therefore instructed Li Hang and others to encourage his modesty and humility. Xiaozong wished his son to gain practical experience in the various affairs of government, and therefore charged Yu Yunwen with warning him against indulgence and idleness. These are all matters recounted in the imperial composition to furnish models for posterity. As for the saying that a tree whose trunk takes several people to encircle must be entrusted to…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
良匠萬金之璧不付拙工所謂周公教成
王以克詰戎兵召公教康王以張皇六師
則我
太祖高皇帝之所以戒劉基李善長者然而不
嫌屢書盖貽輔翼太子之準繩也以漢唐
以下之為大臣言之如房玄齡為百司之
首則有佐理陰陽之責竇德玄列司元之
班則有必資良佐之託憲宗之重裴垍也
必曰以先帝之明猶藉輔佐以成其理孝
===
宗之禮張浚也必曰當萬機之煩宜以元
老而輔朕政此皆
聖製所取以示教者也若所稱鑑明則物之妍
媸無所遁衡平則物之輕重得其當所稱
壅蔽於言者禍亂之萌專恣於事者拳奸
之漸則我
太祖高皇帝之所以告劉仁李守道者然而不
辭備錄盖立選任大臣之標的也有典有
則貽厥子孫不愆不忘率由舊章
punctuated:
良匠，萬金之璧不付拙工，所謂「周公教成王以克詰戎兵，召公教康王以張皇六師」，則我太祖高皇帝之所以戒劉基、李善長者，然而不嫌屢書，盖貽輔翼太子之準繩也。
以漢唐以下之為大臣言之，如房玄齡為百司之首，則有佐理陰陽之責；竇德玄列司元之班，則有必資良佐之託；憲宗之重裴垍也，必曰「以先帝之明，猶藉輔佐以成其理」；孝宗之禮張浚也，必曰「當萬機之煩，宜以元老而輔朕政」。此皆聖製所取以示教者也。若所稱「鑑明則物之妍媸無所遁，衡平則物之輕重得其當」，所稱「壅蔽於言者，禍亂之萌；專恣於事者，拳奸之漸」，則我太祖高皇帝之所以告劉仁、李守道者，然而不辭備錄，盖立選任大臣之標的也。
有典有則，貽厥子孫；不愆不忘，率由舊章。
translation_en:
…a skilled craftsman; a jade disk worth ten thousand in gold must not be entrusted to an inept artisan.” And the statements that “the Duke of Zhou instructed King Cheng to put military affairs in order, and the Duke of Shao instructed King Kang to give full scope to the six armies” were what our Emperor Taizu Gao used to admonish Liu Ji and Li Shanchang. Yet the imperial work does not shrink from recording these repeatedly, thereby bequeathing standards for those who assist and guide the heir apparent.
As for those who served as great ministers from the Han and Tang onward: when Fang Xuanling stood at the head of the hundred offices, he bore responsibility for assisting in harmonizing yin and yang. When Dou Dexuan held a post in the Ministry of Revenue, he was entrusted with the charge expressed in the words, “One must rely upon worthy assistants.” In expressing his esteem for Pei Ji, Emperor Xianzong declared, “Even with the late emperor’s wisdom, he still relied upon assistants to accomplish his governance.” In treating Zhang Jun with honor, Emperor Xiaozong declared, “Amid the burdens of the myriad affairs of state, it is fitting that a senior statesman should assist me in governing.” These are all examples selected in the imperial work to provide instruction. As for the statements, “When a mirror is clear, neither beauty nor ugliness can escape it; when a balance is level, things are properly assessed as light or heavy,” and “Obstructing and concealing speech is the germ of calamity and disorder; acting arbitrarily in affairs is the gradual rise of ‘clenched treachery’ [?],” these were what our Emperor Taizu Gao used to admonish Liu Ren and Li Shoudao. Yet the work spares no effort to record them fully, thereby establishing a standard for selecting and appointing great ministers.
There are established institutions and rules, bequeathed to their descendants; neither transgressing nor forgetting them, they follow the ancient statutes.

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
皇上嗣大歷服有年于兹矣養正
東宮非其禮不舉投艱相位非其器不使其
所以培固天下之根本誠不外是矣天眷
皇明慶鍾
元子聰明得於天性仁孝見於躬行所學者
正道所親者正人所見者正事所聞者正
言習與智長化與心成
祖宗所訓以輔翼之道至是不有成效乎在廷
大臣皆才兼文武世篤忠貞有坐而論道
===
者有起而作事者有疏附先後者有折衝
禦侮者身任天下心在王室則
祖宗所訓以選任之道至是不有明驗乎愚也
生逢熙皞荷
帝力於不知教沐菁莪誦
聖謨於不替雖天地之大未易形容而涓埃之
微豈勝報答敢拜手稽首而獻頌曰
一人元良萬邦以貞又曰股肱惟人良臣惟聖
所以衍億萬年之
punctuated:
皇上嗣大歷服，有年于兹矣。養正東宮，非其禮不舉；投艱相位，非其器不使。其所以培固天下之根本，誠不外是矣。天眷皇明，慶鍾元子，聰明得於天性，仁孝見於躬行。所學者正道，所親者正人，所見者正事，所聞者正言。習與智長，化與心成。祖宗所訓以輔翼之道，至是不有成效乎？在廷大臣，皆才兼文武，世篤忠貞。有坐而論道者，有起而作事者，有疏附先後者，有折衝禦侮者。身任天下，心在王室，則祖宗所訓以選任之道，至是不有明驗乎？
愚也生逢熙皞，荷帝力於不知，教沐菁莪，誦聖謨於不替。雖天地之大，未易形容，而涓埃之微，豈勝報答？敢拜手稽首而獻頌曰：「一人元良，萬邦以貞。」又曰：「股肱惟人，良臣惟聖。」所以衍億萬年之
translation_en:
His Majesty has inherited the great succession and has now occupied the throne for some years. In nurturing rectitude in the Eastern Palace, he undertakes nothing that does not accord with proper ritual; in entrusting arduous responsibilities to the chief minister’s position, he employs no one who lacks the requisite capacity. These, indeed, are the means by which he strengthens the foundations of the realm. Heaven favors the august Ming, and its blessings are concentrated upon the eldest son. His intelligence is innate; his benevolence and filial devotion appear in his personal conduct. What he studies is the correct Way; those with whom he associates are upright people; what he sees are proper affairs; what he hears are correct words. His habits grow with his understanding, and his moral transformation develops with his mind. Have not the ancestral emperors’ instructions on assisting and guiding the heir now borne fruit? The great ministers at court all combine civil and military talents and have maintained steadfast loyalty and integrity for generations. Some sit and discuss the Way; some rise to carry out affairs; some draw others into allegiance and provide assistance on every side; some repel attacks and resist aggression. They shoulder responsibility for the realm, their hearts devoted to the imperial house. Is this not clear proof of the efficacy of the ancestral emperors’ instructions on selecting and appointing ministers?
I, in my humble ignorance, was born into an age of radiant harmony. Unconsciously enjoying the benefits of imperial power, I have received the nurturing instruction celebrated in “Luxuriant Southernwood” and have never ceased reciting the sage imperial counsels. Though the greatness of Heaven and Earth cannot readily be put into words, how could my contribution, as slight as a drop of water or a speck of dust, suffice to repay these blessings? I venture to bow with hands joined and knock my head upon the ground, offering these words of praise: “When the one man is supremely good, the myriad states are thereby set upright.” It is also said: “Arms and legs make the man; worthy ministers make the sage ruler.” These are the means of extending for hundreds of millions of years the …

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
皇圖輔億□之盛治不在茲乎謹對
第二□
戴大賓
同考試官教諭李批敷荅詳明貫穿經
史□宜高薦
同考試官學正王批文以載道本諸六
經此策涉獵諸子之文終篇知所歸重殆蘊藉
之深者况舒竒吐秀不露鋒鋩他日黼黻
皇猷必當出色矣健羨健羨
===
考試官教諭姜批文章小□根於道術
尊此作知所折衷而五策該博通暢當是竒才
得士如此能不為之慶幸
考試官教諭徐批大家文章機軸自異
文以載道而諸子之所造有淺深文以時
異而諸子之所遇有隆替此諸子之文所
以雖僅成一家之言而皆不能造六經之
閫奧也論文者其可不觀其道而考其時
哉知此則明問可得而復矣夫經天緯地
punctuated:
皇圖，輔億□之盛治，不在茲乎？謹對。

第二□，戴大賓。

同考試官教諭李批：敷荅詳明，貫穿經史，□宜高薦。

同考試官學正王批：文以載道，本諸六經。此策涉獵諸子之文，終篇知所歸重，殆蘊藉之深者。况舒竒吐秀，不露鋒鋩，他日黼黻皇猷，必當出色矣。健羨，健羨！

考試官教諭姜批：文章小□，根於道術。尊此作，知所折衷，而五策該博通暢，當是竒才。得士如此，能不為之慶幸？

考試官教諭徐批：大家文章，機軸自異。

文以載道，而諸子之所造有淺深；文以時異，而諸子之所遇有隆替。此諸子之文所以雖僅成一家之言，而皆不能造六經之閫奧也。論文者，其可不觀其道而考其時哉？知此，則明問可得而復矣。夫經天緯地
translation_en:
…the imperial enterprise, and sustain flourishing government for countless [?]—does this not lie herein? I respectfully submit my reply.

Second [?]: Dai Dabin.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “The response is detailed and clear, drawing together the Classics and histories. [?] He merits a high recommendation.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Director of Studies: “Writing conveys the Way and takes the Six Classics as its foundation. This policy essay ranges through the writings of the various masters, yet by its conclusion shows where the greatest weight belongs. Its author surely possesses profound learning and refinement. Moreover, he unfolds unusual ideas and displays elegance without exposing a sharp edge. In days to come, he will surely distinguish himself in embellishing imperial plans. How admirable, how admirable!”

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “Writing is a minor [?], rooted in learning concerning the Way. Esteeming this composition [?], one sees that its author knows how to weigh competing views; moreover, his five policy essays are comprehensive in learning, lucid, and fluent. He must be an exceptional talent. Having obtained such a scholar, how could we fail to rejoice in our good fortune?”

Comment by Examiner Xu, Instructor: “The writing of a great master has a distinctive conception and structure.”

Writing conveys the Way, yet the attainments of the various masters differ in depth. Writing varies with its age, and the circumstances encountered by the various masters include both flourishing and decline. This is why their writings, though each constitutes a school of thought, all fail to penetrate the inner mysteries of the Six Classics. Can those who discuss writing neglect to examine its Way and investigate its age? Once this is understood, your illuminating question can be answered. Now, ordering Heaven and Earth…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
文也垂世立教亦文也文可以易言哉彼
文者貫道之器李漢嘗有是言然以文貫
道是以本為末宜朱子以此議之也我所
謂文必與道俱蘇軾曾為此語然文與道
俱是與道為二宜朱子以此病之也楊雄
擬論語而作法言朱子謂其不過長楊較
獵之流而麤變其音節當矣韓愈法雅頌
而頌聖德蘇轍譏其為李斯頌秦之陋誤
矣學問之中紀綱法制井然而有條則大
===
學之明明德非為文之大者歟日用之間
人倫物理秩然而有序則聖門之所謂道
與義非為文之一般歟六經純乎道德左
傳國語浮華繁委戰國策則馳騁縱橫計
較利害此治世衰世亂世之文所由分也
相如子雲正氣不足司馬遷馳騁有餘仲
舒劉向則發明經術究述天人此譎諫裁
成通儒之文所由異也自文之祖言之道
德篇為玄言之祖離騷為詞賦之祖史記
punctuated: 文也，垂世立教亦文也。文可以易言哉？彼「文者貫道之器」，李漢嘗有是言。然以文貫道，是以本為末，宜朱子以此議之也。「我所謂文必與道俱」，蘇軾曾為此語。然文與道俱，是與道為二，宜朱子以此病之也。楊雄擬《論語》而作《法言》，朱子謂其不過《長楊》《較獵》之流，而麤變其音節，當矣。韓愈法《雅》《頌》而頌聖德，蘇轍譏其為李斯頌秦之陋，誤矣。學問之中，紀綱法制井然而有條，則《大學》之明明德，非為文之大者歟？日用之間，人倫物理秩然而有序，則聖門之所謂道與義，非為文之一般歟？《六經》純乎道德，《左傳》《國語》浮華繁委，《戰國策》則馳騁縱橫，計較利害，此治世、衰世、亂世之文所由分也。相如、子雲正氣不足，司馬遷馳騁有餘，仲舒、劉向則發明經術，究述天人，此譎諫、裁成、通儒之文所由異也。自文之祖言之，《道德篇》為玄言之祖，《離騷》為詞賦之祖，《史記》
translation_en:
…is also literary pattern (wen); leaving teachings to posterity and establishing instruction are likewise wen. Can wen be spoken of lightly? Li Han once said, “Writing is a vessel for threading together the Way.” Yet to thread together the Way through writing is to treat the root as the branch: Master Zhu was right to criticize this. Su Shi once said, “What I call writing must accompany the Way.” Yet to have writing accompany the Way makes them two separate things: Master Zhu was right to find fault with this. Yang Xiong modeled his Model Sayings (Fayan) on the Analects. Master Zhu said that it was merely of the same kind as the Tall Poplars and Imperial Hunt rhapsodies, with a rough alteration of their cadence. This judgment was correct. Han Yu modeled his praise of sagely virtue on the Odes and Hymns, but Su Zhe derided it as sharing the baseness of Li Si’s praise of Qin. This judgment was mistaken.

Within learning, guiding principles, laws, and institutions are arranged with clear coherence. Is not the Great Learning’s “making bright virtue manifest,” then, a great instance of wen? Within everyday life, human relationships and the principles of things have their proper order. Are not what the school of the sages calls the Way and righteousness, then, one aspect of wen? The Six Classics are pure in their expression of the Way and virtue; the Zuo Commentary and Discourses of the States are florid, elaborate, and intricate; the Strategies of the Warring States ranges freely through diplomatic maneuvering and calculations of advantage and harm. These are the grounds for distinguishing the writings of ages of good government, decline, and disorder. Sima Xiangru and Ziyun lack upright vigor; Sima Qian displays an excess of unrestrained sweep; Dong Zhongshu and Liu Xiang elucidate classical learning and thoroughly expound Heaven and humanity. These are the grounds for distinguishing writings of oblique remonstrance, shaping and refinement, and comprehensive Confucian scholarship.

Speaking of the progenitors of literary forms, the Chapters on the Way and Virtue is the progenitor of discourse on the mysteries; Encountering Sorrow (Lisao) is the progenitor of lyrical verse and rhapsody; the Records of the Historian…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
其傳記之祖歟自文之變言之莊子者易
之變離騷者詩之變史記其春秋之變歟
讀伯夷傳貨殖傳而皆悟作文之法者陳
后山徐節孝其人也熟戰國策熟孟子書
而皆造作文之妙者蘇明允朱文公其人
也曰文辭奇險曰叙意苟通曰文必當對
曰文不當對曰宜深曰宜易此爲文之六
說也成周之文典雅七國之文壯偉西漢
之文華贍此古文之三等也蘇洵則投之
===
所向無不如意非能一乎古作者邪曰奏
議宜雅曰書論宜理曰銘誄尚實曰詩賦
欲麗此爲文之四科也事不詭誕則易見
字不艱深則易識書不晦滯則易讀此爲
文之三易也歐陽脩則參取諸家曲盡其
妙非能備乎衆美者耶韓柳以文鳴唐如
韓之淮西碑則有得於書柳之淮西雅則
有得於詩也歐蘇以文鳴宋若歐陽脩之
論道專袒退之蘇子瞻之叙事則法子厚
punctuated: 其傳記之祖歟？自文之變言之，《莊子》者《易》之變，《離騷》者《詩》之變，《史記》其《春秋》之變歟？讀《伯夷傳》《貨殖傳》而皆悟作文之法者，陳后山、徐節孝其人也；熟《戰國策》、熟《孟子》書而皆造作文之妙者，蘇明允、朱文公其人也。曰文辭奇險，曰叙意苟通，曰文必當對，曰文不當對，曰宜深，曰宜易，此爲文之六說也。成周之文典雅，七國之文壯偉，西漢之文華贍，此古文之三等也。蘇洵則投之所向，無不如意，非能一乎古作者邪？曰奏議宜雅，曰書論宜理，曰銘誄尚實，曰詩賦欲麗，此爲文之四科也。事不詭誕則易見，字不艱深則易識，書不晦滯則易讀，此爲文之三易也。歐陽脩則參取諸家，曲盡其妙，非能備乎衆美者耶？韓柳以文鳴唐，如韓之《淮西碑》，則有得於《書》；柳之《淮西雅》，則有得於《詩》也。歐蘇以文鳴宋，若歐陽脩之論道，專袒退之；蘇子瞻之叙事，則法子厚
translation_en: …might it be the progenitor of biographical writing? Speaking of transformations in writing, the Zhuangzi is a transformation of the Book of Changes, and Encountering Sorrow (Li sao) is a transformation of the Book of Odes; might the Records of the Grand Historian be a transformation of the Spring and Autumn Annals? Chen Houshan and Xu Jiexiao were those who read the “Biography of Bo Yi” and the “Biographies of the Money-makers” and thereby grasped the methods of composition. Su Mingyun and Master Zhu, posthumously honored as Wen, were those who thoroughly mastered the Strategies of the Warring States and the Mencius, respectively, and thereby attained excellence in composition. Some say that diction should be unusual and daring; others, that conveying the meaning intelligibly suffices; some, that writing must employ parallelism; others, that it should not; some, that it should be profound; others, that it should be accessible. These are six views on composition. The writing of the Zhou at its height was stately and refined; that of the Seven States, vigorous and grand; that of the Western Han, ornate and abundant. These are three grades of ancient prose. Whatever direction Su Xun turned his writing toward, he invariably achieved his purpose: was he not able to become one with the writers of antiquity? It is said that memorials and deliberations should be refined; letters and discourses should be reasoned; inscriptions and elegies should prize factual substance; and poems and rhapsodies should seek beauty. These are the four categories of composition. If the subject matter is not bizarre or fantastic, it is easy to comprehend; if the words are not obscure, they are easy to recognize; if the writing is not opaque or cumbersome, it is easy to read. These are the three kinds of ease in composition. Ouyang Xiu drew upon the various masters and fully realized their subtleties: was he not able to encompass all their excellences? Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan won renown for prose under the Tang. Han’s “Stele Inscription for the Pacification of Huaixi” drew upon the Book of Documents, while Liu’s “Huaixi Hymn” drew upon the Book of Odes. Ouyang Xiu and Su Shi won renown for prose under the Song. In his discussions of the Way, Ouyang Xiu championed Tuizhi [Han Yu] exclusively; in his narration of events, Su Zizhan [Su Shi] took Zihou [Liu Zongyuan] as his model…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
也然此皆藝焉耳經以明道斯爲真儒學
以窮經斯爲實學若周子太極圖明陰陽
五行之理張子西銘推理一分殊之義程
明道定性一書廓大公之心妙應物之用
伊川春秋易傳二序則明體用之一源著
聖人之大用皆擴前聖所未發有功於聖
門者也明道之儒莫如此四子窮經之士
亦莫如此四子可以表裏乎六經者此也
可爲六經之階梯者亦此也夫豈漢唐以
===
下諸子詞章之文所可同日語哉嗟夫六
經之外皆虚文三代以下無善治錦心繡
口詞則文矣其於道何與駢四驪六法則
文矣其於治何補學文者必先造道以充
其體而又際時以養其氣則文其庶幾矣
此固執事之所望而亦豈非愚生之所願
哉謹對
第三問
張天顯
punctuated:
也。然此皆藝焉耳。經以明道，斯爲真儒；學以窮經，斯爲實學。若周子《太極圖》明陰陽五行之理，張子《西銘》推理一分殊之義，程明道《定性》一書廓大公之心，妙應物之用，伊川《春秋》《易傳》二序則明體用之一源，著聖人之大用，皆擴前聖所未發，有功於聖門者也。明道之儒，莫如此四子；窮經之士，亦莫如此四子。可以表裏乎六經者，此也；可爲六經之階梯者，亦此也。夫豈漢唐以下諸子詞章之文所可同日語哉！嗟夫！六經之外皆虚文，三代以下無善治。錦心繡口，詞則文矣，其於道何與？駢四驪六，法則文矣，其於治何補？學文者必先造道以充其體，而又際時以養其氣，則文其庶幾矣。此固執事之所望，而亦豈非愚生之所願哉！謹對。
第三問
張天顯
translation_en:
… Yet all this is merely literary skill. To elucidate the Way through the Classics is to be a true Confucian; to study so as to fathom the Classics is true learning. Master Zhou’s Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji tu) explains the principles of yin and yang and the Five Phases. Master Zhang’s Western Inscription (Xi ming) develops the meaning of the unity of principle and the differentiation of its particular manifestations. Cheng Mingdao’s letter On Stabilizing the Nature (Dingxing) enlarges the mind’s complete impartiality and brings its capacity to respond to things to wondrous perfection. Yichuan’s two prefaces, to the Spring and Autumn Annals and to the Commentary on the Changes, clarify the common source of substance and function and reveal the great workings of the sages. All these writings extend what earlier sages had left unexpressed and render service to the sages’ teaching. Among Confucians who elucidate the Way, none equal these four masters; among scholars who fathom the Classics, likewise none equal them. These are the writings that can complement the Six Classics, inwardly and outwardly; these, too, can serve as steps toward the Six Classics. How could the literary compositions of the various writers from the Han and Tang onward be mentioned in the same breath?
Alas! Outside the Six Classics, all is empty writing; since the Three Dynasties, there has been no good government. With a mind of brocade and a mouth of embroidery, one’s diction may indeed be ornate, but what has it to do with the Way? With paired phrases of four and six characters, one’s technique may indeed be polished, but what does it contribute to government? Those who study writing must first attain the Way to give fullness to its substance, and then engage with their times to nourish its vital force. Only then may their writing approach the ideal. This is surely what you, honored examiners, hope for; is it not also what I, your unworthy student, desire? Respectfully submitted in reply.
Third Question
Zhang Tianxian

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭周批是策正欲求士子
今日所學以驗諸他日所施此作評品昔人無
毫髮爽其所師法又深得第一流相業於此占
廟堂之志亦必無負於公輔之望者
考試官教諭姜批策問政以觀士子
器識子之器識具見此策施于有政必有可觀
考試官教諭徐批策無襲積故實雕
繪語句之病可錄
在韋布而待以公輔之器處江湖而責
===
以廟堂之職此執事以古之豪傑待天下
而不以今之章句視諸生也古人有言曰
有才智然後可以辦天下之事有德望然
後可以服天下之心此宰相之職也顧愚
淺陋何敢過為厚望以犯不韙之責哉然
見賢思齊亦學者之素志也請得而陳之
昔者六佐六相立功於羲軒之世百揆四
岳佐治於唐虞之時伊尹以聖輔聖而格
天傅說以賢輔賢而納誨有商之名相也
punctuated:
同考試官教諭周批：「是策正欲求士子今日所學，以驗諸他日所施。此作評品昔人，無毫髮爽；其所師法，又深得第一流相業。於此占廟堂之志，亦必無負於公輔之望者。」

考試官教諭姜批：「策問政，以觀士子器識。子之器識，具見此策；施于有政，必有可觀。」

考試官教諭徐批：「策無襲積故實、雕繪語句之病，可錄。」

在韋布而待以公輔之器，處江湖而責以廟堂之職，此執事以古之豪傑待天下，而不以今之章句視諸生也。古人有言曰：「有才智，然後可以辦天下之事；有德望，然後可以服天下之心。」此宰相之職也。顧愚淺陋，何敢過為厚望，以犯不韙之責哉？然見賢思齊，亦學者之素志也，請得而陳之。昔者六佐六相立功於羲軒之世，百揆四岳佐治於唐虞之時。伊尹以聖輔聖而格天，傅說以賢輔賢而納誨，有商之名相也。
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “This policy question seeks precisely to discover what candidates have learned today, as a test of what they will put into practice in the future. This essay assesses men of the past without the slightest error. In its choice of exemplars, it also shows a profound grasp of the achievements of the very foremost chief ministers. Judging from this the writer’s aspirations toward service at court, he will surely fulfill the hopes placed in him for high ministerial office.”

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “The policy question asks about government in order to discern candidates’ capacity and judgment. Your capacity and judgment are fully evident in this essay. Applied to the conduct of government, they will surely produce noteworthy results.”

Comment by Examiner Xu, Instructor: “This policy essay is free from the faults of piling up borrowed historical precedents and elaborately embellishing its phrases. It merits selection.”

Though we wear the leather belts and plain cloth of commoners, you treat us as men capable of high ministerial office; though we dwell far from court, you hold us responsible for duties at its center. In this, you, honored examiners, treat the men of the realm as the outstanding figures of antiquity, rather than regarding us students as today’s mere scholars of textual phrases. An ancient said: ‘Only with talent and wisdom can one manage the affairs of the realm; only with virtue and prestige can one win the allegiance of its people’s hearts.’ Such is the duty of a chief minister. Yet, shallow and ill-informed as I am, how could I dare entertain excessive expectations for myself and incur blame for impropriety? Nevertheless, to see worthy men and aspire to equal them is also a scholar’s abiding ambition. Allow me to set forth my views.

In antiquity, the Six Assistants and Six Ministers achieved distinction in the ages of Fuxi and Xuanyuan, the Yellow Emperor; the Director of All Officials and the Chiefs of the Four Mountains assisted government in the times of Tang Yao and Yu Shun. Yi Yin, a sage assisting a sage, moved Heaven; Fu Yue, a worthy assisting a worthy, presented admonitions. These were renowned chief ministers of the Shang dynasty.

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
周公輔嗣君而制禮作樂召公夾王室而
秉德迪教成周之大臣也元首股肱都俞
於一堂之上鹽梅舟楫際遇於千載之期
論相於三代以前無容贅矣若夫三代而
下擇相者或賢而或否居相者有得而有
失不能無可議也稱於漢者若蕭何之營
輯關中而根本以固曹參之恪守成規而
百姓寧一丙吉則深厚不伐魏相則剛毅
自持之四臣者漢之為相莫過焉稱於唐
===
者若房玄齡之善謀而首扶義旗杜如晦
之善斷而才比王佐宋璟則長於持正姚
崇則善於應變之四子者唐之為相莫加
焉若夫功施社稷有若韓琦身任天下有
若范仲淹負平治之寄而國體有賴其富
弼乎有敢諫之勇而親讎不避其歐陽脩
乎宋之賢相舍數子其何取哉然此特論
其槩耳若諸葛孔明之相漢陸宣公之相
唐司馬光之相宋功雖未竟而當時已服
punctuated:
周公輔嗣君而制禮作樂，召公夾王室而秉德迪教，成周之大臣也。元首股肱，都俞於一堂之上；鹽梅舟楫，際遇於千載之期。論相於三代以前，無容贅矣。若夫三代而下，擇相者或賢而或否，居相者有得而有失，不能無可議也。
稱於漢者，若蕭何之營輯關中而根本以固，曹參之恪守成規而百姓寧一，丙吉則深厚不伐，魏相則剛毅自持，之四臣者，漢之為相莫過焉。稱於唐者，若房玄齡之善謀而首扶義旗，杜如晦之善斷而才比王佐，宋璟則長於持正，姚崇則善於應變，之四子者，唐之為相莫加焉。若夫功施社稷，有若韓琦；身任天下，有若范仲淹。負平治之寄而國體有賴，其富弼乎？有敢諫之勇而親讎不避，其歐陽脩乎？宋之賢相，舍數子，其何取哉？
然此特論其槩耳。若諸葛孔明之相漢，陸宣公之相唐，司馬光之相宋，功雖未竟，而當時已服
translation_en:
…The Duke of Zhou assisted the succeeding ruler, instituted rites, and composed music; the Duke of Shao supported the royal house, upheld virtue, and guided its teaching. These were great ministers of the Zhou dynasty. Sovereign and ministers, like head and limbs, exchanged assent and counsel within a single hall. Ministers who served as salt and plum in seasoning, or as boats and oars in crossing a river, encountered their sovereigns at moments that come but once in a thousand years. In discussing chief ministers of the Three Dynasties and earlier, nothing further need be added. After the Three Dynasties, however, those who selected chief ministers were sometimes worthy and sometimes not; those who held that office had successes and failures. There is inevitably room for criticism.
Among those celebrated in the Han were Xiao He, whose management and consolidation of Guanzhong secured the dynasty’s foundations, and Cao Can, whose scrupulous adherence to established rules brought peace and unity to the people. Bing Ji was generous and profound, without boasting; Wei Xiang was firm and resolute in his conduct. No chief ministers of the Han surpassed these four. Among those celebrated in the Tang were Fang Xuanling, skilled in planning and among the first to support the righteous banner, and Du Ruhui, skilled in decision-making and possessed of talents befitting an adviser to a true king. Song Jing excelled at upholding what was right; Yao Chong excelled at responding to changing circumstances. No chief ministers of the Tang exceeded these four. As for achievements benefiting the altars of soil and grain, there was Han Qi; as for taking responsibility for all under Heaven upon oneself, there was Fan Zhongyan. Was it not Fu Bi who bore the charge of securing peace and good government, and upon whom the state depended? Was it not Ouyang Xiu who had the courage to remonstrate boldly, sparing neither relatives nor enemies? Among the worthy chief ministers of the Song, whom should we choose apart from these men?
Yet this is only a discussion of their broad outlines. As for Zhuge Kongming’s service as chief minister to the Han, Lu Xuangong’s to the Tang, and Sima Guang’s to the Song, although their achievements remained incomplete, their contemporaries already admired…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
其忠義志雖未酬而後世猶仰其聲華豈
出諸臣之下乎然而得失互異長短亦殊
又不可以一槩論也自漢言之則蕭過於
曹丙優於魏而養民致賢志在調燮尤蕭
丙一事之優也自唐論之房大於杜宋正
於姚而樂易有容剛強不屈尤房宋一事
之長也在宋諸臣無大優劣而韓范之識
量政事富歐之忠義文學亦各有所長也
若通而論之則諸葛孔明三代以下一人
===
而已論世考人循名責實豈能逃後世之
公論哉雖然高山仰止景行行止古人皆
我師也一夫不獲時予之辜天下皆我責
也不其位不可以虛居遭其時不可以虛
度以伊周爲法以格君爲先以濟時行道
爲要此愚夙昔之志如此夫豈直爲比方
人物論哉執事許以爲何如謹對
第四問
陳艮山
punctuated:
其忠義，志雖未酬，而後世猶仰其聲華，豈出諸臣之下乎？然而得失互異，長短亦殊，又不可以一槩論也。自漢言之，則蕭過於曹，丙優於魏，而養民致賢，志在調燮，尤蕭、丙一事之優也。自唐論之，房大於杜，宋正於姚，而樂易有容，剛強不屈，尤房、宋一事之長也。在宋諸臣，無大優劣，而韓、范之識量政事，富、歐之忠義文學，亦各有所長也。若通而論之，則諸葛孔明，三代以下一人而已。論世考人，循名責實，豈能逃後世之公論哉？雖然，高山仰止，景行行止，古人皆我師也；一夫不獲，時予之辜，天下皆我責也。不其位不可以虛居，遭其時不可以虛度。以伊、周爲法，以格君爲先，以濟時行道爲要，此愚夙昔之志如此，夫豈直爲比方人物論哉？執事許以爲何如？謹對。
第四問
陳艮山
translation_en:
…their loyalty and righteousness. Although their aspirations remained unfulfilled, later generations still look up to their illustrious reputations. Could they rank below the other ministers? Yet their successes and failures differed, as did their strengths and weaknesses; they cannot all be judged by one standard. Speaking of the Han, Xiao He surpassed Cao Can, and Bing Ji excelled Wei Xiang. In nurturing the people and attracting worthy men, with their minds set on harmonizing the government, Xiao and Bing were especially distinguished in their respective endeavors. Speaking of the Tang, Fang Xuanling was greater than Du Ruhui, and Song Jing more upright than Yao Chong. An affable and accommodating disposition, and an unbending firmness, were the particular strengths of Fang and Song respectively. Among the Song ministers, there were no great differences in merit, but Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan each had strengths in discernment, breadth of mind, and administration, as did Fu Bi and Ouyang Xiu in loyalty, righteousness, and literary learning. Taking them all together, however, Zhuge Kongming stands alone in the ages since the Three Dynasties.

When we examine men in the context of their times and measure their actual achievements against their reputations, how could they escape the impartial judgment of posterity? Nevertheless, “We look up to the lofty mountain; we follow the broad road”: the ancients are all my teachers. “If even one man fails to find his proper place, this is my fault”: all under Heaven is my responsibility. One must not occupy one’s position to no purpose [?]; when one encounters one’s time, one must not let it pass in vain. To take Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou as models, to give first priority to rectifying the ruler, and to regard meeting the needs of the age and putting the Way into practice as essential—such has long been my humble aspiration. How could this merely be a discussion comparing historical figures? What judgment would you, honored examiners, be willing to grant it? I respectfully submit my reply.

Fourth Question
Chen Genshan

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭杜批條陳古人用將之
法無遺區處今日用將之術有見胸中殆自有
甲兵者
同考試官教諭羅批邊計務得名將此
作於求任處規畫分曉錄之以表有用之學
考試官教諭姜批天下信未嘗無才
顧求而任之者何如耳此策或可備
廟堂一畫宜是錄也
考試官教諭徐批所答縝密若經櫽
===
括拳衡者
誦簡練傑俊之言則知將之不可以易求
讀錫命長子之訓則知將之不可以輕任
誠以使貪用過之道薄而拊髀側席之念
與分閫責成之禮廢而死綏任咎之志衰
然則人君求將豈可以不廣而任將豈可
以不專也哉請因明問而陳之粤自周置
六軍而將有統制之權齊作内政而帥有
分職之寄在漢有大將之拜在唐有帥府
punctuated:
同考試官教諭杜批：條陳古人用將之法無遺，區處今日用將之術有見，胸中殆自有甲兵者。
同考試官教諭羅批：邊計務得名將，此作於求任處規畫分曉，錄之以表有用之學。
考試官教諭姜批：天下信未嘗無才，顧求而任之者何如耳。此策或可備廟堂一畫，宜是錄也。
考試官教諭徐批：所答縝密，若經櫽括拳衡者。
誦簡練傑俊之言，則知將之不可以易求；讀錫命長子之訓，則知將之不可以輕任。誠以使貪用過之道薄，而拊髀側席之念與；分閫責成之禮廢，而死綏任咎之志衰。然則人君求將豈可以不廣，而任將豈可以不專也哉？請因明問而陳之。粤自周置六軍，而將有統制之權；齊作内政，而帥有分職之寄；在漢有大將之拜，在唐有帥府
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Du, Instructor, comments: “The ancient methods of employing generals are set out point by point without omission, and the arrangements proposed for employing generals today show insight. The writer surely has troops and weapons within his breast.”
Associate Examiner Luo, Instructor, comments: “Planning for the frontiers requires securing distinguished generals. This essay clearly sets out plans for seeking and appointing them. It is selected to give recognition to learning of practical use.”
Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “The world has indeed never lacked talent; the question is simply how people seek it out and employ it. This policy essay might furnish the court with a useful plan, and deserves selection.”
Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “The answer is meticulous, as though it had been shaped with a straightening frame and weighed in a balance [?].”
Reciting the words about selecting and training outstanding men, one understands that generals cannot be sought casually; reading the admonition about conferring command upon the eldest son, one understands that generals cannot be appointed lightly. Indeed, the practice of employing the greedy and those who have committed faults has declined, while the desire expressed by slapping one’s thigh and sitting to one side of the seat has arisen [?]; the ceremonial propriety of entrusting a general with command beyond the palace gate and holding him responsible for success has been abandoned, while the resolve to die rather than retreat and to accept blame has weakened. Should a ruler, then, not search widely for generals and entrust them with undivided authority? Allow me to set this out in response to your illuminating question. From the time when the Zhou established the Six Armies, generals possessed authority to exercise overall command; when Qi organized its internal administration, commanders were entrusted with distinct duties. Under the Han there were appointments of generals-in-chief; under the Tang there were military headquarters…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
之設置將之法其來尚矣非廣博以求之
則未免有遺材之歎非推誠以任之則未
免有掣肘之虞然若之何而求之耶彼范
仲淹之告仁宗欲於諸班中搜羅智勇而
試以武藝歐陽脩之告仁宗欲就軍伍間
較其技勇而擇爲大將請復武舉而爲之
新制以革其舊弊則蘇洵之所陳也請詔
近臣及藩鎭大臣而各舉武略則富弼之
所陳也夫如是則求將之方可謂廣矣然
===
猶未也要必不以疏遠而遺不以有罪而
廢不以親暱而避不以仇怨而黜庶幾求
之不拘於程度而干城分閫之責有其人
矣夫何遺材之足歎哉抑若之何而任之
耶彼選任將帥端拱於委任陸贄之告德
宗欲專付受以息苟且也將帥之任宜久
於其職張方平之告仁宗欲責久任以觀
成效也王巖叟之建議則曰大帥之任母
輕用人言輒行進退而重謹之當加胡寅
punctuated:
之設，置將之法，其來尚矣。非廣博以求之，則未免有遺材之歎；非推誠以任之，則未免有掣肘之虞。然若之何而求之耶？彼范仲淹之告仁宗，欲於諸班中搜羅智勇，而試以武藝；歐陽脩之告仁宗，欲就軍伍間較其技勇，而擇爲大將。請復武舉，而爲之新制，以革其舊弊，則蘇洵之所陳也；請詔近臣及藩鎭大臣，而各舉武略，則富弼之所陳也。夫如是，則求將之方可謂廣矣。然猶未也，要必不以疏遠而遺，不以有罪而廢，不以親暱而避，不以仇怨而黜，庶幾求之不拘於程度，而干城分閫之責有其人矣。夫何遺材之足歎哉！
抑若之何而任之耶？彼「選任將帥，端拱於委任」，陸贄之告德宗，欲專付受以息苟且也；「將帥之任，宜久於其職」，張方平之告仁宗，欲責久任以觀成效也。王巖叟之建議則曰：「大帥之任，母輕用人言，輒行進退。」而重謹之當加。胡寅
translation_en:
…and the establishment of military headquarters. The practice of appointing generals thus has a long history. Unless the search for them is broad, there will inevitably be cause to lament overlooked talent; unless they are entrusted with office in complete sincerity, there will inevitably be concern that their actions will be hampered. How, then, should they be sought? In his advice to Emperor Renzong, Fan Zhongyan wished to seek out men of intelligence and courage among the various guard units and test them in martial skills. Ouyang Xiu, advising Emperor Renzong, wished to compare the skills and courage of men in the ranks and select great generals from among them. Su Xun proposed restoring the military examinations and establishing new regulations to eliminate their longstanding abuses. Fu Bi proposed ordering the emperor’s close ministers and the high officials commanding regional garrisons each to recommend men versed in military strategy. With such measures, the methods of seeking generals could indeed be called broad. Yet this is still not enough. Above all, men must not be overlooked because they are remote from the court, discarded because they have committed offenses, passed over because they are close associates, or dismissed because of enmity. Only then might the search be unconfined by fixed standards, and suitable men be found to shoulder the responsibilities of defending the state and exercising independent regional military command. What cause would there then be to lament overlooked talent?
How, moreover, should generals be entrusted with office? “Select and appoint generals, then sit with hands folded, leaving affairs to those entrusted with them”: in advising Emperor Dezong, Lu Zhi wished to make the delegation and acceptance of authority exclusive [?], so as to put an end to perfunctory conduct. “Generals should remain long in their posts”: in advising Emperor Renzong, Zhang Fangping wished to hold them accountable over long tenures so that their achievements could be assessed. Wang Yansou proposed: “In appointing a commander-in-chief, do not lightly heed what others say and forthwith promote or dismiss him.” Greater gravity and caution should therefore be exercised. Hu Yin…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
之建議則曰任將之實在有功必賞有罪
必刑而虚文之必去夫如是則任將之道
可謂專矣然猶未也要必隆之以恩禮結
之以誠信富之以貨財假之以威拳庶幾
任之不間於疑貳而折衝禦侮之寄有所
託矣又何掣肘之足慮哉嗟夫天生五材
兵不可廢也天下雖治戰不可忘也兵不
可廢戰不可忘則所謂求將之方與任將
之道固不可一日而不講矣然其要又在
乎吾
君吾相一心之公焉爾誠能公以求之而請託
不交於貴幸之門公以任之而毀譽不行
於愛憎之口則求之必得其人任之必得
其力邊報之警可得而息醜虜之命可得
而制而
國家長治久安之基端有在於此矣管見如
斯不識執事以為然否
第五問
punctuated:
之建議則曰：「任將之實，在有功必賞，有罪必刑，而虚文之必去。」夫如是，則任將之道可謂專矣。然猶未也，要必隆之以恩禮，結之以誠信，富之以貨財，假之以威拳，庶幾任之不間於疑貳，而折衝禦侮之寄有所託矣。又何掣肘之足慮哉！嗟夫！天生五材，兵不可廢也；天下雖治，戰不可忘也。兵不可廢，戰不可忘，則所謂求將之方與任將之道，固不可一日而不講矣。然其要又在乎吾君吾相一心之公焉爾。誠能公以求之，而請託不交於貴幸之門；公以任之，而毀譽不行於愛憎之口，則求之必得其人，任之必得其力。邊報之警可得而息，醜虜之命可得而制，而國家長治久安之基，端有在於此矣。管見如斯，不識執事以為然否？

第五問
translation_en:
…his proposal stated: “The substance of employing generals lies in invariably rewarding merit and invariably punishing offenses, while eliminating empty formalities.” If this is done, the method of entrusting generals with command may be called wholehearted. Yet this is still insufficient. One must honor them with favor and courtesy, bind them through sincerity and trust, enrich them with goods and wealth, and invest them with authority [?]. Then their employment may be free from the intrusion of suspicion and divided trust, and the responsibility for repelling attacks and resisting aggression will have someone to whom it can be entrusted. What further cause would there be to fear interference with their command?

Alas! Heaven brought forth the five materials, and arms cannot be discarded. Though all under Heaven is well governed, warfare must not be forgotten. Since arms cannot be discarded and warfare must not be forgotten, the methods of seeking generals and the principles of employing them must never go unexamined for even a single day. Yet the essential point lies in our sovereign and our chief ministers being united in impartiality. If generals are truly sought impartially, so that requests for favors do not pass through the gates of powerful favorites, and employed impartially, so that praise and slander issuing from personal affection or hatred have no effect, then the search will surely find the right men, and their employment will surely secure their utmost efforts. Alarming reports from the frontier can then cease, and the fate of the vile invaders can be brought under our control. Here indeed lies the foundation of lasting order and enduring peace for the state. Such is my limited view; I do not know whether you, Sir, consider it correct.

Fifth Question

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
鄭伯和
同考試官教諭方批以書生談當世務
鑿鑿可行如此必俊傑也
考試官教諭姜批范文正做秀才時
便理會天下事此作談天下事如指諸掌豈亦
甞理會過耶
考試官教諭徐批有大抱負必有大
設施者於此策覘之
誦詩而授政必達不愧其所學之多得志
===
而與民共由斯驗其所養之大盖達之所
施即窮之所養今之所行即昔之所學曽
謂學者可置時務大體於不講哉古者樵
夫且談王道嫠婦尚憂王室今日執事之
所問與愚生之所對固皆有不容已者也
粤自四門之闢詢及四岳九徳之謀施及
百寮求賢之法其来尚矣後世或求其名
而不責其實或聴其言而不觀其行至有
四科六科之設取舎殊途而卒無定論也
punctuated:
鄭伯和

同考試官教諭方批：「以書生談當世務，鑿鑿可行如此，必俊傑也。」

考試官教諭姜批：「范文正做秀才時，便理會天下事。此作談天下事，如指諸掌，豈亦甞理會過耶？」

考試官教諭徐批：「有大抱負，必有大設施者，於此策覘之。」

誦詩而授政必達，不愧其所學之多；得志而與民共由，斯驗其所養之大。盖達之所施，即窮之所養；今之所行，即昔之所學。曽謂學者可置時務大體於不講哉？古者樵夫且談王道，嫠婦尚憂王室。今日執事之所問，與愚生之所對，固皆有不容已者也。

粤自四門之闢，詢及四岳；九徳之謀，施及百寮。求賢之法，其来尚矣。後世或求其名而不責其實，或聴其言而不觀其行，至有四科六科之設，取舎殊途，而卒無定論也。
translation_en:
Zheng Bohe

Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor, comments: “For a scholar to discuss the affairs of the present day with such precision and practicability, he must be a man of outstanding talent.”

Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “When Fan Wenzheng was still a student, he already concerned himself with the affairs of the realm. This essay discusses those affairs as clearly as if pointing to something in the palm of one’s hand. Has its author likewise given them thought before?”

Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “Here is someone whose great aspirations will surely lead to great accomplishments: this policy essay affords a glimpse of them.”

One who has recited the Odes must prove capable when entrusted with government, thus doing credit to his extensive learning; when he attains his ambition and follows the Way together with the people, the greatness of his self-cultivation is thereby demonstrated. For what a man puts into practice when successful is precisely what he has cultivated while obscure; what he does today is precisely what he learned in the past. Could anyone suppose that scholars may leave current affairs and the broad principles of government undiscussed? In antiquity, even woodcutters spoke of the Kingly Way, and even widows worried about the royal house. Thus both the questions you gentlemen have posed today and the replies of this humble student arise from concerns that cannot be suppressed.

Ever since the four gates were opened and counsel was sought from the Four Peaks, and plans concerning the Nine Virtues were put into effect among the hundred officials, methods of seeking worthy men have had an ancient pedigree. In later ages, some sought men’s reputations without demanding actual merit; others listened to their words without examining their conduct. There were even systems of four categories and six categories, with divergent procedures for accepting and rejecting candidates, yet in the end no settled judgment was reached.

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
虞廷三載黜陟幽明漢法三歲會計群吏
考課之法其來久矣後世或廢大臣而任
有司或棄衡鑑而信簿書至有七事九事
之目好惡異趨而卒無至當也方
今之制進士之科酌唐宋之法而用之不為
不善第在乎得其人以任之則自然去取
公而人材得矣考課之制倣周漢之故而
行之不為不美第在乎得其人以主之則
自然功罪當而治效著矣教化繫於士習
===
固也然不汲汲於富貴則戚戚於貧賤久
矣廉恥之斲喪也治道本之民心宜也然
不曰撫我則后則曰虐我則讎甚矣去留
之不常也為今之計要必勵行檢以敦風
化絕請託以抑浮靡而又示之以好惡齊
之以禁令庶幾士習厚而奔競之風可息
薄賦稅以厚其生均徭役以節其力而又
導之以禮樂感之以恩信庶幾民心悅而
愛戴之誠以至若夫詰爾戎兵姬旦有訓
punctuated:
虞廷三載黜陟幽明，漢法三歲會計群吏，考課之法其來久矣。後世或廢大臣而任有司，或棄衡鑑而信簿書，至有七事九事之目，好惡異趨而卒無至當也。方今之制，進士之科酌唐宋之法而用之，不為不善，第在乎得其人以任之，則自然去取公而人材得矣。考課之制倣周漢之故而行之，不為不美，第在乎得其人以主之，則自然功罪當而治效著矣。
教化繫於士習，固也。然不汲汲於富貴，則戚戚於貧賤，久矣廉恥之斲喪也。治道本之民心，宜也。然不曰「撫我則后」，則曰「虐我則讎」，甚矣去留之不常也。為今之計，要必勵行檢以敦風化，絕請託以抑浮靡，而又示之以好惡，齊之以禁令，庶幾士習厚而奔競之風可息。薄賦稅以厚其生，均徭役以節其力，而又導之以禮樂，感之以恩信，庶幾民心悅而愛戴之誠以至。若夫「詰爾戎兵」，姬旦有訓，
translation_en:
At the court of Yu, every three years the benighted were demoted and the enlightened promoted; under Han regulations, the accounts of all officials were reviewed every three years. The practice of evaluating officials thus has a long history. In later ages, some bypassed the great ministers and entrusted the work to the responsible offices; others abandoned discerning judgment and trusted registers and documents. Eventually there were lists of seven or nine criteria, yet preferences and aversions diverged, and no perfectly fitting standard was ever attained. Under the present arrangements, the examination for metropolitan graduates (jinshi) draws upon and employs the methods of the Tang and Song; it can certainly be called sound. The essential point is simply to find suitable men to administer it: selection and rejection will then naturally be impartial, and talented men will be obtained. The system of evaluating officials follows the precedents of the Zhou and Han; it can certainly be called excellent. The essential point is simply to find suitable men to preside over it: assessments of merit and fault will then naturally be appropriate, and the results of good government will become manifest.
That moral instruction depends upon the conduct of scholars is certainly true. Yet if they are not anxiously pursuing wealth and rank, they are grieving over poverty and low station. Long indeed have integrity and a sense of shame been eroded! That the way of government should be rooted in the people's hearts is fitting. Yet if they do not say, “He who cherishes us is our sovereign,” they say, “He who mistreats us is our enemy.” How greatly they waver between withdrawing and maintaining their allegiance! In planning for the present, it is essential to encourage disciplined conduct so as to strengthen moral customs, and to cut off private solicitation so as to curb frivolity and extravagance. Further, show scholars what is approved and disapproved, and bring them into conformity through prohibitions and ordinances. Then their conduct may become upright, and the practice of competing for advancement may cease. Reduce taxes to improve the people's livelihood, distribute labor service equitably to conserve their strength, and further guide them through rites and music and move them through kindness and good faith. Then the people's hearts may be pleased, and sincere affection and allegiance may follow [?]. As for “Put your arms and troops in order,” Ji Dan left this admonition…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
張皇六師召奭示教戎伍誠不可不充也
今或虛耗則奸宄竊發何以禦之洪範八
政以食爲先軻書論道以穀爲重倉廩誠
不可不實也今或空匱則水旱荐至何以
待之其道又在乎簡卒伍時教閱嚴漏籍
之禁革朘削之弊則貔貅百萬之衆可坐
而致矣廣儲蓄時出納謹鉤校之法汰冗
食之徒則紅腐因陳之積可立而待矣夷
狄中國之疥癘也今或跳梁我邊陲腥羶
===
===
我兵刃若何而制之異端吾道之蟊賊也
今或簧鼓我民心蠹斁我財用若何而處
之其道又在乎廣恩威據形勝來則弗貸
去則勿追而又脩自治之道則犬羊之徒
豈有不馴者哉明教化厚倫理門墻則麾
之夷狄則進之而又嚴衛道之功則佛老
之徒何有不化者哉凡是數者皆時政之
急務爲治之大體也愚生學不足以博古
固不能究其立法之原才不足以通今亦
punctuated:
張皇六師，召奭示教，戎伍誠不可不充也。今或虛耗，則奸宄竊發，何以禦之？洪範八政，以食爲先；軻書論道，以穀爲重。倉廩誠不可不實也。今或空匱，則水旱荐至，何以待之？其道又在乎簡卒伍，時教閱，嚴漏籍之禁，革朘削之弊，則貔貅百萬之衆可坐而致矣；廣儲蓄，時出納，謹鉤校之法，汰冗食之徒，則紅腐因陳之積可立而待矣。
夷狄，中國之疥癘也。今或跳梁我邊陲，腥羶我兵刃，若何而制之？異端，吾道之蟊賊也。今或簧鼓我民心，蠹斁我財用，若何而處之？其道又在乎廣恩威，據形勝，來則弗貸，去則勿追，而又脩自治之道，則犬羊之徒豈有不馴者哉？明教化，厚倫理，門墻則麾之，夷狄則進之，而又嚴衛道之功，則佛老之徒何有不化者哉？凡是數者，皆時政之急務，爲治之大體也。愚生學不足以博古，固不能究其立法之原；才不足以通今，亦
translation_en:
…“Magnify the six armies”: Shao Shi offered this teaching. The military ranks must indeed be filled. If they are now depleted, how can we resist evildoers when they suddenly rise? Among the eight concerns of government in the Great Plan, food comes first; in discussing the Way, the Book of Meng Ke gives grain particular weight. The granaries must indeed be filled. If they are now empty, how can we cope when floods and droughts strike repeatedly? The means lie in selecting the troops, conducting instruction and reviews at proper intervals, strictly enforcing the prohibition against omission from the military registers, and eliminating exploitative exactions. Then a million warriors, fierce as wild beasts, can be assembled with ease. Expand reserves, regulate receipts and disbursements according to the seasons, carefully apply procedures for checking accounts, and eliminate superfluous mouths maintained at public expense. Then stores so abundant that grain reddens and decays, with old stocks piled upon old, may soon be expected.
The foreign peoples are an affliction upon China, like scabies. If they now rampage along our frontiers and befoul our weapons with their rank smell, how are we to subdue them? Heterodox teachings are vermin that prey upon our Way. If they now beguile our people's hearts and consume our financial resources, how are we to deal with them? The means lie in extending benevolence and authority and occupying strategically advantageous terrain: when they come, spare them not; when they depart, do not pursue them. If we also cultivate sound government within our own realm, how could these dog- and sheep-like hordes fail to submit? Make moral instruction clear and strengthen ethical relationships; drive them away when they are within our gates and walls, but bring them forward when they are among the foreign peoples [?]. If we also rigorously defend the Way, how could the followers of Buddhism and Daoism fail to be transformed? All these matters are urgent tasks of present government and fundamental principles of governing. My humble learning is insufficient for a broad understanding of antiquity, so I certainly cannot fathom the origins of its institutions; my abilities are insufficient for comprehending the present, and likewise…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
不能悉其救弊之術又惡敢率易僭妄以
輒自附於古豪傑志士之末哉但區區忠
藎直欲為吾
君吾相陳之久矣而況明問之所及乎惟進而
教之
punctuated: 不能悉其救弊之術，又惡敢率易僭妄，以輒自附於古豪傑志士之末哉？但區區忠藎，直欲為吾君吾相陳之久矣，而況明問之所及乎？惟進而教之。
translation_en: …nor can I fully comprehend the methods for remedying their abuses. How, then, would I dare rashly and presumptuously to count myself even among the least of the heroes and men of high purpose of antiquity? Yet, in my humble loyalty and devotion, I have long wished to lay these matters before our sovereign and our chief ministers. How much more so when they fall within the scope of your enlightened question! I ask only that you guide and instruct me.

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄕試錄後序
聖天子臨御十有四年
詔天下賓興賢能巡按福建監
察御史陸偁合藩臬重臣祗
若
德意恊心共事考試聘公而明者
執事選才而良者革訛剔蠹
===
百度惟貞乃合八郡一州五
十三縣之士三試之如故事
而加密芳等目視心惟稱量
品第雖於知人之哲不敢妄
議而秉公持平或庶幾焉得
士九十人勒其氏名文字為
錄以
punctuated:
福建鄕試錄後序

聖天子臨御十有四年，詔天下賓興賢能。巡按福建監察御史陸偁合藩臬重臣，祗若德意，恊心共事。考試聘公而明者，執事選才而良者，革訛剔蠹，百度惟貞。乃合八郡一州五十三縣之士，三試之如故事，而加密。芳等目視心惟，稱量品第，雖於知人之哲不敢妄議，而秉公持平，或庶幾焉。得士九十人，勒其氏名文字為錄，以
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

In the fourteenth year of the sage Son of Heaven’s reign, he decreed that worthy and capable men throughout the realm should be honored as guests and advanced for selection. Lu Cheng, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Fujian, brought together the senior officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions. Reverently following the imperial benevolent intent, they worked together with one purpose. For Examiners, they engaged men who were impartial and discerning; for other examination duties, they selected men who were capable and upright. They corrected errors and rooted out abuses, ensuring that all procedures were proper. They then assembled the candidates from the eight prefectures, one subprefecture, and fifty-three counties, examining them in three sessions according to established practice, but with greater rigor.

We, Fang and the others, read carefully and reflected, weighing and ranking the candidates. Though we dare not make unwarranted claims to the wisdom of knowing men, we may perhaps have come close to upholding impartiality and fairness. We selected ninety men and had their names and compositions engraved for printing as a record, in order to…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
獻竊惟試之有錄即古者鄉大
夫所獻賢能書也嘗見人閱
前輩小錄輒指而議之曰某
也賢某也能是科某人司考
試得人如是一有貶議亦及
于有司茲錄之傳能無私議
之者乎而芳輩臧否將有不
===
得掩者固不容嘿嘿無以相
感發也君子立身行己之方
安上治民之道見於經傳炳
如也髻而誦之弁而味之壯
而以是策名于賢科及見諸
行事顧有背而馳者亦獨何
哉人之議不議不足校獨不
punctuated:
獻。竊惟試之有錄，即古者鄉大夫所獻賢能書也。嘗見人閱前輩小錄，輒指而議之曰：「某也賢，某也能，是科某人司考試，得人如是。」一有貶議，亦及于有司。茲錄之傳，能無私議之者乎？而芳輩臧否，將有不得掩者，固不容嘿嘿無以相感發也。
君子立身行己之方，安上治民之道，見於經傳，炳如也。髻而誦之，弁而味之，壯而以是策名于賢科，及見諸行事，顧有背而馳者，亦獨何哉？人之議不議，不足校，獨不
translation_en:
…to present it. I humbly reflect that an examination record is equivalent to the register of the worthy and able presented in antiquity by the district grand masters. I have seen people reading the brief records of earlier generations, pointing to them and commenting: “This man was worthy; that man was able. So-and-so served as Examiner in this examination, and these were the men he selected.” Whenever there is an adverse judgment, it also extends to the responsible officials. Once this record circulates, can there be no one who discusses it privately? The merits and failings of Fang and his colleagues will then in some measure be impossible to conceal. We certainly cannot remain silent and offer nothing to inspire and encourage one another.
The methods by which a gentleman establishes himself and conducts his life, and the way to secure the ruler and govern the people, are brilliantly manifest in the classics and their commentaries. As children with their hair in knots, men recite them; upon donning the adult cap, they savor their meaning; in maturity, through these teachings they gain a place on the rolls of an examination for the worthy. Yet when it comes to putting them into practice, some instead turn their backs and hasten in the opposite direction. Why indeed is this so? Whether others criticize them is not worth reckoning; the sole concern is whether they are not…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
愧於心歟使能尊所聞行所
知卓卓自立於斯世庶無愧
于賢能矣然是鄉一變于常
衮興學之日再變于楊時道
南之餘及朱子而文獻大聚
蔚為東南道義之鄉我
朝文命四敷詩書禮樂之澤洽
===
于百年遂彬彬為賢才淵藪
夫
化育漸涵若此其久也故老風
流若此其未遠也士生其間
稍有識見者當知所致身矣
尚俟愚言哉他日有追頌福
建鄉試某科某科得賢能士
punctuated: 愧於心歟？使能尊所聞，行所知，卓卓自立於斯世，庶無愧于賢能矣。然是鄉一變于常衮興學之日，再變于楊時道南之餘，及朱子而文獻大聚，蔚為東南道義之鄉。我朝文命四敷，詩書禮樂之澤洽于百年，遂彬彬為賢才淵藪。夫化育漸涵若此其久也，故老風流若此其未遠也，士生其間，稍有識見者，當知所致身矣，尚俟愚言哉？他日有追頌福建鄉試某科某科得賢能士
translation_en: …feel ashamed in one's own heart? If they can honor what they have heard and practice what they know, standing firmly and independently in this world, they may prove worthy of being called worthy and capable. This region was first transformed when Chang Gun promoted learning, and transformed again in the wake of Yang Shi's transmission of the Way southward. By the time of Master Zhu, writings and learned worthies had gathered in abundance, making it a flourishing home of the Way and righteousness in the southeast. Our dynasty's civilizing influence has spread in all directions; the beneficent influence of the Odes, the Documents, rites, and music has permeated the region for a hundred years, so that it has become a richly cultivated gathering place for worthy talent. Such nurturing and gradual cultivation have continued for so long, and the exemplary influence of the venerable elders remains so near. Scholars born here who possess even some discernment should know to what they ought to devote themselves. Need they still await my humble words? If, in days to come, people look back with praise upon particular sittings of the Fujian Provincial Examination for having obtained worthy and capable scholars…

title: 弘治十四年福建鄉試錄
text:
最多而是科亦預焉豈惟芳
輩旁被光熌而實
明詔賓興之意幸相與勉之
江西吉安府廬陵縣儒學教
諭姜芳謹序
punctuated:
最多，而是科亦預焉，豈惟芳輩旁被光熌，而實明詔賓興之意。幸相與勉之。
江西吉安府廬陵縣儒學教諭姜芳謹序。
translation_en:
…the greatest number, and this examination too is counted among them, would that not merely bring reflected glory upon us, but also fulfill the intent of the enlightened imperial edict to honor and advance worthy men? May we encourage one another in this endeavor.
Preface respectfully written by Jiang Fang, Instructor in the Confucian School of Luling County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi.
